show.title: Let's Murder Marsha
show.author: Monk Ferris
show.description: A happy housewife named Marsha, hopelessly addicted to reading murder mysteries, overhears her loving husband discussing her upcoming birthday surprise with an interior decorator. To her ears, though, it sounds like they are planning to murder her! With the assistance of her next-door neighbor, she tries to turn the tables on them with a poisoned potion. When her own mother shows up for her birthday a day early, Marsha thinks she is in on the diabolical scheme. When her maid’s date, a policeman, shows up to take the maid out, Marsha think he is on to her poisoning attempt. Well, finally, just when you would think all this would be cleared up, Marsha’s intended victims discover what she has supposed, and decide to teach her a lesson by actually pretending to be murderers. This is a terrific show for family audiences who like their comedy broad, fast, and nonstop.

show.title: Finding Nemo, Jr
show.author: Lindsay Anderson
show.description: Disney’s Finding Nemo JR. is a 60-minute musical adaptation of the beloved 2003 Pixar movie Finding Nemo, with new music by award-winning songwriting team Kristen Anderson-Lopez and Robert Lopez. Marlin, an anxious and over-protective clownfish, lives in the Great Barrier Reef with his kid Nemo, who longs to explore the world beyond their anemone home. But when Nemo is captured and taken to Sydney, Marlin faces his fears and sets off on an epic adventure across the ocean. With the help of lovable characters such as optimistic Dory, laid-back sea turtle Crush, and the supportive Tank Gang, Marlin and Nemo both overcome challenges on their journey to find each other and themselves.

show.title: Women in White
show.author: James Reach
show.description: Kate Fawcett, stern but fair Superintendent of Nurses, thinks of the girls in her charge almost as daughters. Hester is interested only in books, hard boiled Gloria is waiting for her guy to return from Korea, sentimental Betsy wants a man, Ann has a past she tries desperately to keep hidden, and Elaine and Molly share a strange and incriminating secret. Laurie and Celia are new probationers; one is full of ideals and the other is just looking for a job. One of the girls is murdered and Julia Robertson, a policewoman working her first homicide, is called in. Julia is determined to solve the baffling mystery and does, but not before another girl's life has been jeopardized, and not before one of the most terrifying climaxes ever written.
show.contentWarnings: Mild Adult Themes

show.title: Irving Berlin’s White Christmas
show.author: David Ives and Paul Blake
show.description:
When Christmas is truly warm and cozy!

Veterans Bob Wallace and Phil Davis have a successful song-and-dance act after World War II. With romance in mind, the two follow a duo of beautiful singing sisters en route to their Christmas show at a Vermont lodge, which just happens to be owned by Bob and Phil's former army commander. With a dazzling score featuring well-known standards including “Blue Skies,” “I Love A Piano,” “How Deep Is the Ocean” and the perennial title song, White Christmas is an uplifting, wholesome musical that will delight audiences of all ages.

Recommended for all ages

show.title: Irving Berlin’s White Christmas
show.author: David Ives and Paul Blake
show.description:
When Christmas is truly warm and cozy!

Veterans Bob Wallace and Phil Davis have a successful song-and-dance act after World War II. With romance in mind, the two follow a duo of beautiful singing sisters en route to their Christmas show at a Vermont lodge, which just happens to be owned by Bob and Phil's former army commander. With a dazzling score featuring well-known standards including “Blue Skies,” “I Love A Piano,” “How Deep Is the Ocean” and the perennial title song, White Christmas is an uplifting, wholesome musical that will delight audiences of all ages.

Recommended for all ages

show.title: The House on Haunted Hill
show.author: Tommy Jamerson
show.description:
The Doors Lock at Midnight. Good Luck.

You’re cordially invited to a party to die for.

Based on the Vincent Price cult classic, House on Haunted Hill is a deliciously suspenseful thriller filled with mystery, dark humor, and unexpected twists. Eccentric millionaire Frederick Loren invites five strangers to spend the night in a notorious haunted mansion, promising each guest a fortune if they can survive until sunrise.

But as the night unfolds, long-buried secrets, double-crosses, ghostly encounters, and deadly surprises turn the mansion into a terrifying game of survival. With every creaking door and shadowy hallway, the question becomes not who will claim the prize—but who will make it out alive.

Packed with chills, laughs, and edge-of-your-seat suspense, House on Haunted Hill is a haunting theatrical experience you’ll never forget.

show.title: It's a Wonderful Life: A Live Radio Play
show.author: Adapted by Joe Landry
show.description:
Tune Into Hope This Holiday Season.

Celebrate the magic of the season with It’s a Wonderful Life: A Live Radio Play, a heartwarming theatrical adaptation of the beloved American holiday classic.

Presented as a live 1940s radio broadcast, this inventive production transports audiences to the golden age of radio, where a talented ensemble brings dozens of unforgettable characters to life using vintage microphones, live sound effects, and holiday charm. Follow the inspiring journey of George Bailey, whose Christmas Eve despair is transformed by the unexpected visit of an angel who reveals the profound difference one life can make.

Filled with nostalgia, warmth, laughter, and hope, It’s a Wonderful Life: A Live Radio Play is a timeless celebration of family, community, and the enduring spirit of the holiday season.

show.title: Frozen
show.author: Jennifer Lee
show.description:
The global phenomenon comes alive on stage! Frozen delivers breathtaking theatrical magic, epic adventure, and the unforgettable songs you love—plus new ones written just for Broadway. Packed with laugh-out-loud moments and stunning visuals, this heartwarming story celebrates love, courage, and family. Experience the magic together—this is the show that brings the whole family closer and creates memories you’ll treasure.
Season Package holders get your tickets now to get the best seats.
Single Tickets go on sale September 25, 2026.

show.title: A Christmas Carol
show.author: Adapted by Charlie Lovett from the novel by Charles Dickens
show.description:
Few stories endure like A Christmas Carol. This richly theatrical adaptation captures the wonder, warmth, and transformation at the heart of Dickens’ timeless tale. With evocative scenery and unforgettable ghostly visits, it’s a holiday experience that has become a cherished tradition—and one audiences won’t want to miss while it’s on our stage.

Season Package Holders get early access to this sold out production and 25% off tickets.

Single Tickets on sale November 20, 2026.

show.title: Fiddler on the Roof
show.author: Joseph Stein
show.description: Set in the small village of Anatevka, Fiddler on the Roof follows Tevye, a dairyman trying to hold onto tradition as his daughters—and the world around him—change. Featuring timeless songs like "Tradition," "If I Were a Rich Man," and "Sunrise, Sunset," this beloved musical is a funny, moving celebration of family, community, and resilience.

show.title: Frozen
show.author: Jennifer Lee
show.description: Based on the hit Disney film, Frozen is a dazzling Broadway-style musical about two sisters—Elsa and Anna—learning that love is stronger than fear. With beloved songs like "Let It Go" alongside new music written for the stage, this spectacular production features breathtaking visuals, big laughs, and an uplifting story about family, acceptance, and finding your own strength.

show.title: Rosencrantz and Guildenstern Are Dead
show.author: Tom Stoppard
show.description: Two minor characters from Hamlet suddenly find themselves at the center of one of theatre’s funniest and imaginative comedies and Stoppard’s most well known work. As the two lead characters search for answers, they encounter actors, royalty, pirates, impossible coincidences, and a world that never quite explains itself or lets them in on the full story. Filled with fast-paced wordplay, unforgettable performances, and surprising heart, Tom Stoppard’s modern classic is less about Shakespeare and more about all of us trying to figure out where we fit. It’s an exhilarating evening of actor-driven performances that celebrates the joy, wit, and wonder of live theatre.
show.runtime: Approximately 2 hours 30 minutes, with one intermission
show.contentWarnings: Mild adult themes and language. Recommended for ages 13 and up.

tickets.notes: Prices exclude taxes and fees. Senior/Student/Military $30; seniors are 62 and up, students through college. General admission seating.

show.title: Cinderella
show.author: Based on the fairy tale by Charles Perrault   Adaptation and lyrics by Jim Eiler
show.description: RLT’s holiday tradition returns to celebrate its 42nd year! Kids of all ages will love this retelling of the beloved fairy tale, filled with music, laughs, and a sparkle of magic. This musical comedy features elegant costumes and scenery and a cast of memorable characters including some conniving step-relatives, royals, everyone’s favorite resourceful Fairy Godmother, and Ella, of course!

tickets.notes: Prices exclude taxes and fees. Child price is for ages 12 and under. Reserved seating. ASL interpretation is available by advance request.

show.title: Four Old Broads on the High Seas
show.author: Leslie Kimbell
show.description:
Get ready to set sail with your favorite Old Broads. Yes ... they're back again and all ready for a Sassy Seniors cruise to the Bahamas. Beatrice is determined to have her pick of ALL the eligible men on the ship ... but Maude, fresh from her win at The Miss Magnolia Senior Citizen Pageant, plans on being her biggest competition. Wedding bells are ringing for Imogene and Sam ... maybe. And Eaddy? ... well ... she just wants to know what all the fuss is about up on the topless sun deck. Throw in a murder mystery, a fabulous drag queen, and a crazy costume party, and you're in for a laugh-a-minute night of fun.
​

show.title: Gypsy: A Musical Fable
show.author: Book by Arthur Laurents Suggested by the memoirs of Gypsy Rose Lee
show.composer: Music by Jule Styne Lyrics by Stephen Sondheim
show.description: Gypsy, the musical fable suggested by the memoirs of Gypsy Rose Lee, centers on Momma Rose, a driven and often overbearing stage mother who pushes her two daughters toward the stardom she always wanted for herself as vaudeville slowly dies around them. Rose drags June and Louise, along with a troupe of young performers, through the seedy backstages and run-down hotels of 1920s show business, with the devoted Herbie trying to be both a father figure to the girls and a suitor to Rose. When June, who first loves the spotlight and later resents it, runs off with fellow performer Tulsa, the quieter Louise is pushed forward and, after an encounter with three seasoned burlesque performers, transforms into the burlesque star Gypsy Rose Lee. Town Theatre's production stars Shannon Willis Scruggs as Rose, with Ashton Boland as the grown-up Louise, Hayle Barry as June, Joel Yarborough as Herbie and Kieran Eustace as Tulsa. It is directed by Jerry Crouch, with music direction by Michael Simmons and choreography by Joy Alexander, and features a live five-piece orchestra.

show.title: A Christmas Carol: The Musical *12th Annual*
show.author: Lynn Ahrens & Mike Ockrent
show.description:
A favorite Triad holiday tradition returns with High Point Community Theatre’s musical version of Charles Dickens’ classic holiday tale. Ebenezer Scrooge is a prosperous curmudgeon who believes personal wealth is far more valuable than the happiness and comfort of others.

Ebenezer Scrooge is a prosperous curmudgeon who believes personal wealth is far more valuable than the happiness and comfort of others. With an infuriated "Bah! Humbug!" Scrooge summates his feelings about Christmas tidings and charitable giving, but he's forced to face his selfish ways when three ghosts on Christmas Eve lead him through his Past, Present, & Future. Thanks to their guidance, Scrooge recognizes his faults and greets Christmas morning with a cheerful "Happy Christmas" before spending the day reconnecting and sharing love with those who mean the most to him.

This is a spectacular adaptation of Charles Dickens' most well-known story that had a decade-long run at the Theatre at Madison Square Garden. The show has featured well-known actors such as Terrence Mann, Roddy McDowall, Frank Langella, Tim Curry, Roger Daltrey, Emily Skinner, Christopher Sieber, Didi Conn, Ben Vereen, and more. It was made into a movie starring Kelsey Grammer, Jesse L. Martin, Jane Krakowski, Jennifer Love Hewitt, and Jason Alexander. You will love it!

Runtime is approximately 90 minutes. No intermission.

Contains some mild adult language.

show.title: Dracula: A Comedy of Terrors
show.author: Gordon Greenberg and Steve Rosen
show.description: Ever wondered what would happen if you took Bram Stoker’s legendary vampire tale and put it into a blender with Mel Brooks, Monty Python, and The 39 Steps? That’s just what happens in this lightning-fast, laugh-out-loud, 90-minute, gender-bending romp. When her sister Mina falls ill with a mysterious disease of the blood, Lucy Westfeldt and her fiancé, Jonathan Harker, enlist the help of famed female vampire hunter Doctor Jean Van Helsing. Their hunt for the dangerous and sexy Count Dracula abounds with clever wordplay and quick-change antics. Five actors play over a dozen roles in this bloodcurdlingly hilarious send-up of the literary classic.

tickets.notes: Pay-What-You-Can ($5+) Performance: Thursday, October 22, 7:30 PM (PWYC Pricing Goes Live October 8)

show.title: Reader’s Theatre – War of the Worlds, The 1938 Radio Script
show.author: Howard Koch
show.description: Broadcast from New York’s Mercury Theatre in 1938, this infamous radio play, based on the novel by H. G. Wells, had many terrified listeners convinced that an actual alien invasion of Earth was taking place. Adapted by Howard E. Koch, co-writer of Casablanca, and directed and narrated by Orson Welles, this original script detailing the frightening tale of an extraterrestrial takeover is now available to bring to life onstage to thrill and chill audiences.

tickets.notes: Pay-What-You-Can ($5+) Performance: Thursday, October 22, 7:30 PM (PWYC Pricing Goes Live October 8)

show.title: Little Women
show.author: Kate Hamill
show.description:
o March isn’t your typical Victorian lady. She’s indecorous and headstrong, and one day she’s going to be a great American novelist. As she and her sisters grow up in the middle of the Civil War, they strive to be brave, intelligent and imaginative young women. But as adulthood approaches, each sister must negotiate her private ambitions with society’s expectations. In a wartorn world defined by gender, class and personal tragedy, Jo March gives us her greatest story: that of the March sisters, four dreamers destined to be imperfect little women.

In classic Kate Hamill fashion, a literary masterpiece is updated and refreshed for the modern age, with focus given to the strong, seldom well-behaved women who make history. Bursting with humor and emotional intelligence, this Little Women speaks across centuries and generations.

tickets.notes: Pay-What-You-Can ($5+) Performance: Thursday, December 17, 7:30 PM (PWYC Pricing Goes Live December 3)

show.title: The Haunting of Hill House
show.author: F. Andrew Leslie
show.description: This gothic horror follows four characters who spend a summer in the eerie Hill House, hoping to encounter supernatural phenomena.

show.title: Frosty
show.description: A discarded silk top hat becomes the focus of a struggle between a washed-up stage magician and a group of schoolchildren after it magically brings a snowman to life.

show.title: Travesties
show.author: Tom Stoppard
show.description: A dazzling, fast-talking comedy where history, memory, and total absurdity collide — featuring appearances by figures like James Joyce and Vladimir Lenin. It’s sharp, chaotic, and wildly funny in a way that keeps you leaning forward the entire time.

show.title: The Seafarer
show.author: Conor McPherson
show.description: On a stormy Christmas Eve, a group of men gather for drinks and a card game with unusually high stakes. What starts as grounded and familiar slowly twists into something eerie, gripping, and unexpectedly moving.

show.title: The Crucible
show.author: Arthur Miller
show.description: One of the most acclaimed plays in the American theatrical canon, this exciting drama about the Puritan purge of witchcraft in old Salem is a gripping and timely parable of contemporary society, as well as a studied historical tale. The story focuses upon a young farmer, his wife and a young servant-girl who maliciously causes the wife’s arrest for witchcraft. The farmer brings the girl to court to admit the lie – and the monstrous course of bigotry and deceit is terrifyingly depicted. The farmer, instead of saving his wife, finds himself also accused of witchcraft and ultimately condemned along with a host of others.

show.title: The Outsiders
show.author: Christopher Sergel From the book by S.E. Hinton
show.description: Based on S.E. Hinton’s novel about rival teenage gangs in 1960s Tulsa, Oklahoma, the Greasers come from troubled working-class backgrounds, contrasted with the Socials, whose members are from upper-middle-class families.

show.title: Frankenstein
show.author: Nick Dear From the novel by Mary Shelley
show.description: Mary Shelley’s revolutionary horror classic is shocked to life in Nick Dear’s thrilling adaptation. Told through the eyes of the abandoned Creature, this bold gothic retelling follows a life born innocent and curious, only to be rejected by the very man who made him. Alone in a world that fears and despises him, his yearning for connection spirals into rage and revenge. Determined to confront his creator, he hunts him down to demand a terrifying bargain. Visceral and haunting, this powerful production explores the explosive bond between maker and creation, confronting us with urgent questions of responsibility, belonging, and what it truly means to be human. In the end, Frankenstein dares us to decide: who is the real monster?
show.runtime: Approximately 2 hours and 15 minutes with intermission.
show.contentWarnings: Frankenstein contains violence, mature themes, and emotionally intense scenes. We encourage patrons to use their judgment based on their own research of the show, and their sensibilities.

show.title: A Christmas Carol
show.author: Adapted by Julius Arthur Leonard From the novel by Charles Dickens
show.description: For 20 years, A Christmas Carol has been Theatre Charlotte’s treasured holiday tradition. This anniversary production celebrates the warmth and wonder of Charles Dickens’ beloved novel through the eyes of the characters who have captured hearts for generations. As Ebenezer Scrooge is guided by the Ghosts of Christmas Past, Present, and Future, he encounters the Cratchit family and young Tiny Tim, whose hope, courage, and joy embody the true spirit of the season. Filled with magic, mystery, and timeless storytelling, this classic holiday favorite reminds audiences of all ages that compassion and generosity can change lives.
show.runtime: Approximately 90 minutes including a 15 minute intermission.
show.contentWarnings: A Christmas Carol includes fog and lighting effects. We encourage patrons to use their judgment based on their own research of the show, and their sensibilities.

show.title: Lost in Yonkers
show.author: Neil Simon
show.runtime: Approximately 2 hours and 15 minutes with intermission.
show.contentWarnings: Lost in Yonkers contains mature themes. We encourage patrons to use their judgment based on their own research of the show, and their sensibilities.

show.title: Annie
show.author: Thomas Meehan (book)
show.description: Leapin' Lizards! The irrepressible comic strip heroine takes center stage in one of the world's best-loved musicals. With equal measures of pluck and positivity, little orphan Annie charms everyone's hearts despite a next-to-nothing start in 1930s New York City. Directed by Ella Riley.

show.title: House on Haunted Hill
show.author: Tommy Jamerson
show.description:
Adapted from the Vincent Price classic, The House on Haunted Hill tells the twisted tale of millionaire Frederick Lauren, his fourth wife Annabelle, and five, money-hungry guests who will each received fifty thousand dollars if they stay in a supposedly haunted house until sunrise.

Filled with double crosses, jilted lovers, a wicked sense of humor, and a restless spirit or two, Haunted Hill proves to be a night you’ll never forget.

show.title: Reefer Madness: The Musical
show.author: Kevin Murphy and Dan Studney
show.description:
Inspired by the original 1936 film of the same name, this raucous musical comedy takes a tongue-in-cheek look at the hysteria caused when clean-cut kids fall prey to marijuana, leading them on a hysterical downward spiral filled with evil jazz music, sex and violence.

You won’t be able to resist the spoofy fun of Reefer Madness. The addictive, clever musical numbers range from big Broadway-style showstoppers to swing tunes like “Down at the Ol’ Five and Dime” and the Vegas-style “Listen to Jesus, Jimmy,” featuring J.C. Himself leading a chorus of showgirl angels. Refeer Madness is a highly stylized and satirical political commentary that will leave you wanting more.

show.title: Greater Tuna
show.author: Jaston Williams, Ed Howard, and Joe Sears
show.description:
Summer fun is just around the corner!  Why not cool down in our AC with a beverage in hand and sit back and laugh at our production of Greater Tuna!

This sharp-witted and wildly funny live stage comedy that takes you to the quirky, fictional small town of Tuna, Texas—the “third-smallest” in the state. Performed by a cast of just two actors playing dozens of eccentric characters, the show satirizes small-town life with heart and hilarity. From gleefully nosy neighbors to bizarre radio DJs and local officials, Greater Tuna delivers rapid-fire humor, clever observations, and unforgettable personalities in a rollicking theatrical celebration of rural American culture.

Once said to be "one of the most produced plays in America," you won't want to miss it!

Rated PG-13 due to adult content and language.

show.title: My Fair Lady
show.author: Alan Jay Lerner
show.description: Based on George Bernard Shaw's Pygmalion, this classic musical follows Eliza Doolittle, a Cockney flower seller transformed into an elegant lady by Professor Henry Higgins, sparking an unlikely friendship. Features 'Wouldn't It Be Loverly,' 'The Rain in Spain,' and 'I Could Have Danced All Night.'
show.contentWarnings: Recommended ages 8+

show.title: FLT's Christmas Extravaganza
show.description: An evening of holiday cheer featuring a visit from Santa Claus, festive vendors, local talent performing Christmas classics and contemporary music, and heartwarming holiday stories. A family-friendly FLT tradition.

tickets.notes: Season Ticket Holders receive 20% off

show.title: One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest
show.author: Dale Wasserman (based on the novel by Ken Kesey)
show.description: After being convicted of a petty crime, rebellious rogue McMurphy contrives to serve his sentence in a mental institution rather than prison. He clashes with the authoritarian Nurse Ratched, leading a revolt among the other patients, but his brash insubordination has consequences.
show.contentWarnings: Recommended ages 17+. Strong language, sexual content, and mature themes.

show.title: Stephen King's Misery
show.author: William Goldman (based on the novel by Stephen King)
show.description: Successful romance novelist Paul Sheldon is rescued from a car crash and wakes up captive in a secluded home owned by his self-proclaimed 'number one fan,' Annie Wilkes. When Annie discovers he's killed off her favorite character, she forces Paul to write a new novel — and has no intention of letting him go.
show.contentWarnings: Recommended ages 17+. Intense violence, psychological terror, and strong language.

show.title: Ebenezer Scrooge's BIG Sumter Christmas Show
show.description: A holiday production inspired by Charles Dickens' A Christmas Carol, bringing Ebenezer Scrooge's journey of redemption to the Sumter stage with music and community holiday spirit. A festive tradition for the whole family.

show.title: Intimate Apparel
show.author: Lynn Nottage
show.description: Set in 1905 New York City, this play follows Esther Mills, a skilled African-American seamstress who navigates a changing, dangerous world with her needle and thread. Through the intimate garments she sews, she forms unlikely bonds with women across race and class lines, all while corresponding with a suitor from Panama.

show.title: Wiley and the Hairy Man
show.author: Suzan Zeder
show.description: Drawn from African-American folk wisdom, this family-friendly folk tale follows young Wiley as he ventures through a mysterious swamp, learning to rely on his own courage and resourcefulness to outwit two villains: the fearsome Hairy Man and his own fear. Tradition says if you outwit the Hairy Man three times, he'll never scare you again.

show.title: Bright Star
show.author: Steve Martin & Edie Brickell
show.description: Inspired by a true story and featuring a Tony-nominated score of bluegrass and gospel-tinged music, Bright Star tells a sweeping tale of love and redemption set against the backdrop of the American South in the 1920s and '40s.

show.title: It's a Wonderful Life
show.description: The beloved holiday classic follows George Bailey, a man who has spent his life sacrificing his own dreams for the good of his community, only to find himself on the brink of despair one Christmas Eve. When his guardian angel, Clarence, shows him what the world would have been like had he never been born, George discovers the profound impact of his life on those around him. NOTE: I could not confirm the specific stage adaptation/authorship used for this production (e.g. Joe Landry's radio play version vs. a traditional dramatization) — recommend checking directly with Swamp Fox Players for the exact script credit.

show.title: Under a Broadway Spell
show.description: A Halloween revue show presented in partnership with City of Halloween. This thrilling revue conjures up Broadway's most magical and mysterious moments, featuring favorite Halloween hits and chilling showstoppers, with dazzling dancers, stunning costumes, and unforgettable characters — a haunting celebration the whole family will love.

show.title: Holiday on Main Christmas Revue Show
show.description: From familiar carols to fresh new arrangements, this holiday revue is filled with songs both new and old that will have audiences of all ages smiling, singing, and feeling the spirit of the season. Perfect for the entire family.

show.title: Murder on the Orient Express
show.author: Ken Ludwig (adapted from the novel by Agatha Christie)
show.description: All aboard the Orient Express in Ken Ludwig's suspenseful adaptation of Agatha Christie's classic murder mystery. Audiences follow the brilliant detective Hercule Poirot as he investigates a gallery of intriguing suspects, where every passenger is a potential killer, in this suspenseful whodunit perfect for the Halloween season.
show.contentWarnings: Depicts murder; mature themes.

show.title: John Lloyd Young: Broadway's Jersey Boy (in Concert)
show.description: A one-night-only exclusive concert featuring Tony® and Grammy® Award winner John Lloyd Young, best known as the original star of Broadway's Jersey Boys and the Warner Bros. film adaptation directed by Clint Eastwood.

show.title: To Kill a Mockingbird
show.author: Aaron Sorkin (adapted from the novel by Harper Lee)
show.description: This powerful stage adaptation of Harper Lee's classic novel comes to the stage once more. Set in 1930s Alabama, lawyer and father Atticus Finch takes on the complications of defending an innocent Black man in a deeply divided America. Through the lens of his young children, questions are asked, tension is felt, and moral courage rises to the top.
show.contentWarnings: Depicts racial injustice and violence.

show.title: Hairspray
show.author: Mark O'Donnell & Thomas Meehan (book)
show.composer: Marc Shaiman (music); Scott Wittman & Marc Shaiman (lyrics)
show.description: "Welcome to the 60's!" The Tony Award-winning musical comedy bursts back onto the Greenville Theatre stage, filled with high-energy, high emotions, and high hair. Tracy Turnblad takes Baltimore by storm and dances her way into the hearts of an ever-changing America, celebrating the joy of standing up, standing out, and letting your voice be heard.
show.contentWarnings: Explores racial segregation and civil rights themes.

show.title: Big Fish
show.author: John August (book)
show.description: Based on the moving Tim Burton film, fantasy and reality are explored when a son seeks the truth of his father's fantastical life. This imaginative, larger-than-life musical explores the importance of family and love, with a soaring score and unforgettable characters, taking audiences on a journey of wonder, myth, and enormous heart to discover the enduring power of storytelling.

show.title: The Wizard of Oz
show.author: L. Frank Baum
show.composer: Harold Arlen (music); E.Y. Harburg (lyrics); Herbert Stothart (background music)
show.description: Journey "Over the Rainbow" with Dorothy and her loyal dog Toto in this timeless musical based on the beloved 1939 MGM film. Follow the Yellow Brick Road as Dorothy meets the Scarecrow, Tinman, and Cowardly Lion to discover wisdom, heart, and courage in this holiday favorite reminding us there's no place like home.

show.title: Jesus Christ Superstar in Concert
show.author: Tim Rice (lyrics)
show.description: A concert co-production between Greenville Theatre and Mauldin Theatre Company. This legendary rock opera, told entirely through song, explores the personal relationships and struggles during the final days of Jesus of Nazareth, viewed through the complex, critical eyes of Judas Iscariot.
show.contentWarnings: Rated PG-13 for mature themes. NOTE: This is a concert-style co-production with Mauldin Theatre Company.

show.title: Mean Girls
show.author: Tina Fey (book, based on the Paramount Pictures film)
show.description:
Based on the hit film by Tina Fey, Mean Girls is the hilarious, high-energy musical that proves high school is the wildest place of all. When Cady Heron arrives at North Shore High after years of homeschooling, she’s quickly swept up into the ruthless social hierarchy ruled by the Plastics—led by the unforgettable Regina George.

Packed with sharp wit, explosive choreography, and a pop-infused score, Mean Girls takes a no-holds-barred look at friendship, popularity, and the pressure to fit in. As alliances shift and reputations are put to the test, Cady must decide who she really is—and how to survive without becoming the very thing she fears.

Smart, bold, and laugh-out-loud funny, Mean Girls is a fiercely entertaining musical about finding your voice, owning your power, and being true to yourself—no matter what anyone else thinks.

show.title: Once Upon a Mattress
show.author: Jay Thompson, Dean Fuller, & Marshall Barer (book)
show.description:
A hilarious twist on The Princess and the Pea, Once Upon a Mattress turns a classic fairy tale upside down. When an outspoken, unconventional princess arrives at a kingdom where no one can marry until Prince Dauntless finds a bride, she must pass an impossible test—one that stands between true love and a very tall stack of mattresses.

Bursting with charm, physical comedy, and toe-tapping songs, this beloved musical celebrates individuality, honesty, and the joy of being unapologetically yourself. With its colorful characters, fairy-tale fun, and heart at its center, Once Upon a Mattress is a crowd-pleasing comedy for all ages.

Lighthearted, clever, and irresistibly fun, this musical proves that sometimes the real happily ever after comes from daring to be different.

show.title: Ain't Too Proud
show.author: Dominique Morisseau (based on the book "The Temptations" by Otis Williams with Patricia Romanowski)
show.description:
Ain’t Too Proud is the electrifying musical that tells the true story of The Temptations, charting their journey from the streets of Detroit to international superstardom. Bursting with signature harmonies, precision choreography, and a parade of iconic hits—including “My Girl,” “Just My Imagination,” “Get Ready,” and “Papa Was a Rolling Stone”—this exhilarating show brings Motown magic to life onstage.

As brotherhood, ambition, and the pressures of fame collide, Ain’t Too Proud explores the triumphs and trials behind the music, set against the social and political upheaval of the 1960s and ’70s. Written by Dominique Morisseau, this Tony Award®–winning musical is a soulful, high-octane celebration of artistry, resilience, and the sound that changed music forever.

show.title: The 39 Steps
show.author: Patrick Barlow (adapted from the novel by John Buchan and the movie by Alfred Hitchcock)
show.description:
The 39 Steps is a fast-paced, tongue-in-cheek thriller that turns Hitchcock’s classic spy story into a whirlwind of theatrical invention. With a small cast playing dozens of characters, this madcap adventure races from London to the Scottish Highlands, blending suspense, romance, and razor-sharp comedy at breakneck speed.

Equal parts spy thriller and farce, The 39 Steps is packed with quick changes, inventive staging, and laugh-out-loud physical comedy. Clever, stylish, and endlessly entertaining, it’s a brilliantly playful love letter to classic cinema—and a high-energy joyride from start to finish.

show.title: Million Dollar Quartet Christmas
show.author: Colin Escott (book)
show.composer: Elvis Presley, Jerry Lee Lewis, Carl Perkins, & Johnny Cash
show.description: Million Dollar Quartet Christmas brings together legendary icons Elvis Presley, Johnny Cash, Jerry Lee Lewis, and Carl Perkins for a joyful holiday celebration inspired by the famous 1956 jam session. Blending rock-and-roll classics, gospel favorites, and beloved Christmas songs, this festive musical captures the spirit of friendship, faith, and music during the most wonderful time of the year. Filled with electrifying performances, heartfelt storytelling, and a soundtrack that ranges from toe-tapping rock hits to soul-stirring holiday tunes, Million Dollar Quartet Christmas is a high-energy, feel-good celebration for audiences of all ages. Warm, nostalgic, and irresistibly fun, this holiday hit is the perfect way to make spirits bright—and rock around the Christmas tree. If you loved our production of Million Dollar Quartet, you will love this Christmas rendition by the same incredible actors who brought the story to life on our stage before.

show.title: Marjorie Prime
show.author: Jordan Harrison
show.description:
Set in the near future, Marjorie Prime is a quietly powerful and deeply moving exploration of memory, love, and the stories we tell ourselves to survive. Marjorie, an aging woman losing her grasp on the present, spends her days with a “Prime”—a lifelike artificial intelligence programmed to remember her life alongside her. But as memories are revisited and reshaped, the line between truth and comfort begins to blur.

Tender, thoughtful, and unexpectedly funny, Marjorie Prime asks big questions about humanity, technology, and the legacy we leave behind. A richly intimate play, it invites audiences to reflect on how memory defines us—and who gets to decide which moments endure.

show.title: The Break
show.author: Christopher Dimond (book & lyrics)
show.description:
A SCNPF Alumni Show

The Break is a witty, rock-infused musical comedy about Sam and Charlie—a couple who have been together since college and now face the looming question: should they get married? Deciding they need answers (and perhaps a bit of perspective), they agree to take a month-long break from one another, free to explore life, new connections, and the modern dating landscape before recommitting… or rethinking everything.

Funny, honest, and full of heart, The Break explores commitment, curiosity, and what we learn about ourselves when we step outside our comfort zones. This two-person musical takes you on a journey through the hilarious and heartfelt ups and downs of choosing love, leaving it, and discovering what it really means to grow together—or apart.

show.title: 24th Annual New Play Festival
show.author: Various (finalist playwrights)
show.description: Centre Stage's 24th Annual New Play Festival presents professional staged readings of the year's Top Three Finalists, selected from this year's Top 10 Semifinalists: The Sugar Mountain Methodist Women's Fashion Show by Laura King, John Deserves to Die by Rachel Beth Greene, and This Is the Subtext by Brian James Polak. Following the festival, one winning play will be selected for a full production at Centre Stage during the 2027-2028 season. The festival is free and open to the public.

show.title: Chrysalis
show.author: Gwyneth Strope
show.description:
What does it take to break the cycle—and begin again?

In Chrysalis, Mirage, a woman facing an unexpected pregnancy, is pulled into a surreal inner landscape where memory, trauma, and self-preservation collide. As she confronts fragmented versions of her past, Mirage is forced to reckon with what she has buried—and what healing might demand.

Poetic, intimate, and unflinchingly honest, Chrysalis is a memory play about survival, transformation, and the courage it takes to reclaim one’s story. Moving between the past and present, reality and imagination, the play illuminates the long, nonlinear journey of healing—and the possibility of emerging stronger on the other side.

Selected from hundreds of submissions nationwide, Chrysalis was chosen by Centre Stage audiences as the standout work of the New Play Festival and now receives its full production premiere.

Content Advisory: Chrysalis explores themes of sexual assault, grooming and exploitation of a minor, emotional abuse, and suicide. These topics are central to the story and may be difficult for some viewers. Audience discretion is strongly advised. Resources and support information will be available.

show.title: POTUS: Or, Behind Every Great Dumbass Are Seven Women Trying to Keep Him Alive
show.author: Selina Fillinger
show.description: One four-letter word is about to rock 1600 Pennsylvania Avenue. When the President unwittingly spins a PR nightmare into a global crisis, the seven brilliant and beleaguered women he relies upon most risk life, liberty, and the pursuit of sanity to keep the commander-in-chief out of trouble. Fast, chaotic, and gloriously profane. Directed by Maegan McNerney Azar.
show.contentWarnings: Contains adult language and mature political satire.

show.title: Little Women
show.author: Kate Hamill (adapted from the novel by Louisa May Alcott)
show.description:
Jo March is stubborn, ambitious, wildly creative, and absolutely not interested in being the kind of proper Victorian lady society expects her to be. As the March sisters navigate love, loss, family, and growing up, Little Women delivers all the warmth and heart of the classic novel with fresh humor, energy, and emotional honesty, and the persistent suspicion that Laurie deserved better. Timeless for a reason.

WHY SEE THIS SHOW: Every generation gets a version of LITTLE WOMEN because the story endures. A quintessential American novel, this theatrical adaptation hews closely to the book while allowing for the contemporary relevance to shine through. It is a beautiful story about ambition, finding your place, purpose and identity, and how to have hope when things are dark. It’s a chance for Greenville to get its own version of the March sisters, and we can’t wait to bring this story to life.

WHO SHOULD SEE THIS SHOW?  If you like these things, you’ll like this: Uh, pretty much any adaptation of LITTLE WOMEN or the original novel itself.  Also our PRIDE AND PREJUDICE, THE CHERRY ORCHARD, and any stories about families banding together.

show.title: The Pillowman
show.author: Martin McDonagh
show.description: In a totalitarian state, a writer of dark, violent fairy tales is interrogated by two detectives after a string of gruesome child murders eerily mirror the plots of his stories. As the interrogation unfolds, the play weaves together storytelling, family trauma, and moral ambiguity in a work that is by turns hilarious and horrifying. Directed by Stephen Thorne.
show.contentWarnings: Contains graphic descriptions of violence against children, dark themes, and disturbing content.

show.title: Bat City (World Premiere)
show.author: Josh Tobiessen
show.description: For a one-hit songwriter and a poet with grad school debts, the only logical next career move is to rob the hip Austin (aka Bat City) restaurant where they work. A romantic comedy about when to quit, when to hold on, and whether stealing from your day job counts as following your heart. Not everyone gets to be a star, but that shouldn't stop you from following your dreams — or robbing your place of work to make your dreams come true. Directed by Caroline Jane Davis. Produced in association with PURE Theatre.

show.title: Good Vibrations: The Sounds of the 60's
show.description:
The Sounds of the 60’s!

A high-energy music revue celebrating the unforgettable American sound of the 1960s, Good Vibrations: The Sounds of the 60’s captures a transformative decade when music turned louder, freer, and full of possibility. From sun-drenched surf rock and breezy beach harmonies to soulful folk-pop, raw rock-and-roll energy, and stirring protest anthems, this original live concert experience explores the diverse sounds that defined an era of both carefree summer spirit and powerful social change.
show.contentWarnings: Appropriate for all ages.    This production may include flashing or strobe lighting effects and theatrical haze.

show.title: The Diary of Anne Frank
show.author: Frances Goodrich & Albert Hackett, adapted by Wendy Kesselman (based on the diary of Anne Frank)
show.description:
A young girl’s inspiring story of hope in hiding

A powerful and intimate drama, The Diary of Anne Frank follows eight people forced into hiding during the Nazi occupation as they live in secrecy within a concealed attic, struggling with fear, confinement, and uncertainty. In this tightly bound space, tensions rise, bonds are tested, and moments of hope and humanity persist against the odds. At the heart of the story is a young girl whose diary captures both the everyday realities of life in hiding and the extraordinary resilience required to endure it.
show.contentWarnings: Contains mature themes related to war, persecution, and the Holocaust. Some scenes may be emotionally intense. Parental/audience discretion is advised.    This production may also include flashing or strobe lighting effects and theatrical haze.

show.title: The Hunchback of Notre Dame
show.author: Peter Parnell (book), based on the novel by Victor Hugo and the 1996 Disney film
show.description: A sweeping tale of love, longing, and courage, The Hunchback of Notre Dame brings Victor Hugo’s beloved story to life with powerful music and haunting beauty. Beneath the towering bells of Notre Dame, the kind-hearted Quasimodo dreams of a world that will accept him, while the fearless Esmeralda challenges the darkness surrounding them. As passion and obsession collide, destinies are forever changed. Rich with soaring melodies and emotional depth, this unforgettable musical explores what it truly means to be seen, to belong, and to be human.
show.contentWarnings: Contains mature themes and intense moments involving lust, betrayal, religious persecution, and violence. Parental/audience discretion is advised.    This production may also include flashing or strobe lighting effects and theatrical haze.

show.title: Clue
show.author: Sandy Rustin (book), with additional material by Hunter Foster & Eric Price (based on the Paramount Pictures film and the Hasbro board game)
show.description:
One mansion. Six suspects. Multiple endings.

A storm rages outside Boddy Manor, but inside, the real chaos is just beginning. In CLUE: Live on Stage, six mysterious guests gather for a dinner party that quickly turns deadly when their host is found murdered—and everyone is a suspect. As secrets unravel, motives multiply, and bodies start dropping, the race is on to uncover who did it, with what weapon, and in which room. Fast-paced, hilarious, and packed with twists, this theatrical whodunit keeps audiences guessing until the very last reveal.
show.contentWarnings: Contains comic violence, murder mystery themes, loud sound effects, mild adult language, and occasional suggestive humor. Parental discretion is advised.    This production may also include flashing or strobe lighting effects and theatrical haze.

show.title: The Wedding Singer
show.author: Chad Beguelin & Tim Herlihy (book); based on the 1998 New Line Cinema film
show.description:
Love, laughs, and last-chance romance!

Step back into the neon-soaked world of the 1980s with The Wedding Singer, a high-energy musical full of romance, comedy, and pop nostalgia. Based on the hit 1998 film, it follows Robbie Hart, a charming wedding singer whose wedding ends in heartbreak at the altar, leaving him adrift. When he meets Julia, a kind-hearted waitress engaged to the wrong man, an unexpected connection sparks complications—and possibilities. With big laughs, ‘80s style, and an upbeat score, it’s a feel-good celebration of second chances and finding your spotlight.

show.title: The Play That Goes Wrong
show.author: Henry Lewis, Jonathan Sayer & Henry Shields
show.description: The Play That Goes Wrong is an award-winning comedy following the Cornley Drama Society as they attempt to stage a classic 1920s murder mystery. What begins as a straightforward production quickly spirals into complete chaos as everything that can possibly go wrong does — from set malfunctions to missed cues to outright disasters. The show delivers nonstop laughter through physical comedy, perfectly timed mishaps, and a cast whose determination shines through even as the production collapses around them.

show.title: The 2nd Annual 24 Hour Theatre Project, 2026
show.description:
NEW BERN CIVIC THEATRE proudly presents our 2nd Annual
24 HOUR THEATRE PROJECT
Saturday, October 17, 2026

HERE’S HOW IT WORKS:
At 7:30 PM on Friday, October 16, five writers will gather and, by random draw, each will receive a genre and a quote for inspiration. They’ll then have just 12 hours to write an original 10-minute play.

At 7:30 AM on Saturday, October 17, the writers and directors reconvene at New Bern Civic Theatre. Scripts are randomly assigned to directors, auditions begin at 8:00 AM, and the shows are cast on the spot.

From there, it’s a race against the clock! Casts and directors rehearse all day, and by 7:30 PM, the finished productions are performed live for an audience.

Fast. Fearless. Unforgettable.
You won’t want to miss this thrilling, one-of-a-kind theatrical event!

show.title: In the Heights
show.description: From the creative soul of Lin Manuel Miranda, the genius behind Hamilton – in the heart of Washington Heights, dreams are big, the streets sizzle with music, and change is in the air. In The Heights is a high-energy celebration of family, love, and finding home — with a beat that won’t quit and a heart that runs deep.

show.title: VHS Christmas Carol
show.description: A Christmas Carol… like you’ve NEVER seen it before! Step into a retro holiday fever dream with VHS Christmas Carol — a wild, neon-drenched twist on Dickens’ classic. Think fuzzy tapes, synth beats, big hair, and bigger shoulder pads, as Ebenezer Scrooge’s ghostly journey gets rewound and remixed for the ultimate ‘80s-style holiday party. It’s nostalgic, hilarious, and brimming with holiday spirit — the kind of Christmas story you’ll want to play, pause, and replay all season long! Rated [PG]

show.title: Disney's Frozen
show.author: Jennifer Lee (book, based on the Disney film she wrote and co-directed with Chris Buck)
show.description:
For the first time in forever, experience the musical phenomenon that has taken the world by storm! Based on the Academy Award-winning animated feature film, Disney’s Frozen includes all the film’s beloved songs by Kristen Anderson-Lopez and Robert Lopez, along with new music written exclusively for the stage.

In the beautiful mountainous kingdom of Arendelle, Princesses Anna and Elsa grow up sheltered inside their castle, isolated from the world and increasingly distant from each other. When Elsa is crowned queen, the magical powers she’s desperately tried to conceal from her sister take control, and she flees into the mountains. As a ferocious winter descends on Arendelle, Anna sets off on an epic journey to find Elsa and bring her home – with the help of hardworking ice harvester Kristoff, his loyal reindeer Sven, and a happy-go-lucky snowman named Olaf.

Full of magic, humor, and a stunning musical score, Frozen is a powerful tale of sisterhood, acceptance, and finding the real meaning of true love.

show.title: Sweeney Todd: The Demon Barber of Fleet Street
show.author: Hugh Wheeler (book), from an adaptation by Christopher Bond
show.description:
Sweeney Todd has become a bloody, worldwide success since being awarded eight Tony’s, (including Best Musical), for its Broadway premiere. Stephen Sondheim’s and Hugh Wheeler’s tasty, thrilling, theatrical treat has simultaneously shocked, awed and delighted audiences across the world.

An infamous tale, Sweeney Todd, an unjustly exiled barber, returns to nineteenth century London, seeking vengeance against the lecherous judge who framed him and ravaged his young wife. The road to revenge leads Todd to Mrs. Lovett, a resourceful proprietress of a failing pie shop, above which, he opens a new barber practice. Mrs. Lovett’s luck sharply shifts when Todd’s thirst for blood inspires the integration of an ingredient into her meat pies that has the people of London lining up… and the carnage has only just begun!
show.contentWarnings: Contains graphic violence, murder, and dark themes involving cannibalism.

show.title: Miracle on 34th Street
show.author: Meredith Willson (book), based on the 20th Century Fox picture with story by Valentine Davies and screenplay by George Seaton
show.description:
Based on the 20th Century Fox Picture of the same name, with story by Valentine Davies and screenplay by George Seaton

A holiday classic from the writer of the musical theatre classic, The Music Man!, and based on the movie of the same name, Miracle on 34th Street features a book and score by none other than Meredith Willson.

Single mother, Doris Walker, doesn’t want her six-year-old Susan’s head filled with romantic notions. Their neighbor, Fred Gailey, tries to woo Doris by charming Susan and taking her to see Santa Claus at Macy’s, where Doris works. Doris is not impressed, but when it turns out that Macy’s Santa may, in fact, be the real Kris Kringle, a wave of love spreads across New York City that melts even the most cynical hearts.

show.title: Joseph and the Amazing Technicolor Dreamcoat
show.author: Tim Rice (lyrics)
show.description:
“Sha la la, Joseph, you’re doing fine! You and your dreamcoat, ahead of your time!” One of the most enduring shows of all time, Joseph and the Amazing Technicolor Dreamcoat is a reimagining of the Biblical story of Joseph, his father Jacob, eleven brothers and the coat of many colors.

Told entirely through song with the help of a main character Narrator, the musical follows preferred son Joseph. After being sold into slavery by his brothers, he ingratiates himself with Egyptian noble Potiphar but ends up in jail after refusing the amorous advances of Potiphar’s wife. While imprisoned, Joseph discovers his ability to interpret dreams, and he soon finds himself in front of the mighty but troubled, Elvis-inspired, Pharaoh. Joseph’s solution to Egypt’s famine elevates him to Pharaoh’s right-hand man and reunites him with his family.

show.title: Come From Away
show.author: Irene Sankoff & David Hein
show.description: Come From Away is based on the true story of the time when the isolated community of Gander, Newfoundland, played host to the world. What started as an average day in a small town turned into an international sleepover, when 38 planes, carrying thousands of people from around the globe, were diverted to Gander’s airstrip on September 11, 2001. Undaunted by culture clashes and language barriers, the people of Gander cheered the stranded travelers with music, an open bar and the recognition that we’re all part of a global family.
show.contentWarnings: Contains discussion related to the September 11 terrorist attacks.

show.author: Steven Levenson
show.description: Seventeen-year-old Evan Hansen has felt invisible his entire life. But when a tragedy shocks his community and thrusts him into the center of a rapidly evolving controversy, Evan is given the opportunity of a lifetime: the chance to be somebody else. As his web of well-intentioned lies begins to unravel, though, Evan is forced to confront the fact that the price of belonging may be far steeper than he bargained for.
show.contentWarnings: Contains mature themes including suicide, grief, and mental health struggles.

show.title: Once On This Island
show.author: Lynn Ahrens (book & lyrics)
show.description: Ti Moune, a peasant girl, rescues a wealthy boy from the other side of the island, Daniel, with whom she falls in love. Unbeknownst to Ti Moune, the pompous gods who preside over the island make a bet with one another over which is stronger, love or death, the stakes being Ti Moune’s life. When she pursues Daniel, who has returned to his people, Ti Moune is shunned because of her lowly status. Her determination and capacity to love, though, is not enough to win Daniel’s heart, and Ti Moune pays the ultimate price; but the gods turn Ti Moune into a tree that grows so strong and so tall, it breaks the wall that separates the societies and ultimately unites them.

show.title: The Wild Party
show.author: Andrew Lippa (book & lyrics)
show.description: Step inside Queenie’s apartment and become part of the party. HART’s fully immersive production of Andrew Lippa’s The Wild Party transforms the Fangmeyer Theater into a sultry, jazz-drenched speakeasy, with the bar open all night and audience members free to move, mingle, and experience the action up close. Lovers Queenie and Burrs, both vaudeville performers, throw the party-to-end-all-parties, attracting a dazzling crowd living on the edge. When Queenie’s wandering eye meets the mysterious Black, passions ignite, and jealousy erupts, sending the night spiraling toward danger and betrayal. With a thrilling score, seductive choreography, and razor-sharp storytelling, this bold, intoxicating, and unforgettable production makes you more than a spectator—you’re living the wild party.
show.contentWarnings: Contains simulated sexual violence, strong language, sounds of gunshots, portrayal of physical violence, domestic abuse, and substance and alcohol abuse.

tickets.notes: The Wild Party is an immersive theatrical experience set in the Fangmeyer Theatre, where the entire space becomes the stage. To make sure every guest has the best possible experience, we offer two ways to enjoy the show — both priced at $39.  Fly-on-the-Wall Best for guests who prefer a traditional theatre experience  As a Fly-on-the-Wall, you’ll have a reserved seat in the audience for the full performance. Sit back, relax, and take in the show from beginning to end. Please note that because the action unfolds throughout the entire Fangmeyer Theatre, sightlines will vary — some moments may be easier to see from certain seats than others.  Party-Goer Best for guests who want to be part of the action  As a Party-Goer, you’re not just watching The Wild Party — you’re attending it. You’re encouraged to move freely throughout the space and follow the action as it unfolds around you. At select moments, you’ll even be invited to join the cast on the dance floor. While seating areas will be available on and around the set, you’ll get the most out of this experience by staying on your feet and moving with the show.  Please note: Party-Goers should be comfortable with standing and moving around for extended periods of the evening. We also encourage you to come dressed in your best 1920s fashion — the more flair, the better!

show.title: Disney's Frozen Jr. (Academy Performance)
show.author: Jennifer Lee (book, based on the Disney film she co-wrote and co-directed with Chris Buck)
show.description: The beloved story of Elsa and Anna comes to life on stage in a production that will delight the whole family. Disney’s Frozen Jr. follows two royal sisters whose bond is tested by secrets, powers, and a journey into the unknown, with a little help from a snowman named Olaf, a charming reindeer handler, and an unforgettable score full of songs you already know and love. Bursting with heart, humor, and the kind of joy only young performers can bring, this is a magical celebration of sisterhood, courage, and the power of love.

show.title: Sister Act
show.author: Cheri & Bill Steinkellner (book), based on the Touchstone Pictures motion picture
show.description:
When disco diva Deloris Van Cartier witnesses a crime, she hides out in the last place anyone would look — a convent. Suddenly, the sequins are swapped for habits, and the nightclub turns into a nave. But when Deloris brings her unholy amount of soul to the choir loft, heaven gets a whole new groove.

Sister Act is a holy-rolling, soul-lifting celebration of sisterhood, second chances, and songs that raise the roof. As Deloris helps the sisters find their voices, they just might change her heart in return.

Part divine comedy, part disco revival, it’s proof that a little funk — and a lot of faith — can turn any sanctuary into a showstopper.

show.title: Rumpelstiltskin
show.author: Ben Mackel
show.description:
A world premiere musical spun from the Grimm Brothers’ classic — a tale of gold, grit, and a touch of magic, set to a captivating score that fuses folk, rap, and percussion.

The kingdom is in crisis, the villagers are hungry, and their future rests in the hands of a poor miller’s daughter. Her only hope is a daring bargain with a mysterious stranger — one that tests the worth of a name, the power of trust, and the courage to spark change.

This new musical explores the cost of greed and the grace of kindness, reminding us that what truly matters can’t be measured in gold.

Be the first to experience a brand-new American musical by Ben Mackel, developed through the Playhouse Jr. Licensing New Works Initiative. Created entirely under our roof, this world premiere offers new theatre for all — big and small — continuing a bright new chapter of storytelling from the Playhouse’s stage to the world’s.

show.title: A Flat Rock Playhouse Christmas Show (10th Anniversary Special)
show.description:
For a decade, A Flat Rock Playhouse Christmas has been the cherished gathering that brings our community together,  where Broadway sparkle meets small-town heart and the spirit of the season takes center stage.

This year’s festivities are stuffed fuller than Santa’s sleigh with the songs you can’t wait to hear — the holiday hits and beloved carols you ask for every year, delivered with fa-la-la flair and show-stopping shine.
