show.title: Spider's Web
show.author: Agatha Christie
show.description: Synopsis: Clarissa, wife of a diplomat, is adept at spinning tales of adventure, but when a murder takes place in her drawing room, she finds live drama much harder to cope with. Desperate to dispose of the body before her husband arrives with an important politician, she enlists the help of her guests. Hilarity ensues when they are interrupted by the arrival of wry detective Inspector Lord. With this conscious parody of the detective thriller, Christie delivers a unique blend of suspense and humor. There are tension and laughter in equal parts in an intricate plot of murder, police, drug addicts, invisible ink, hidden doorways and secret drawers.
show.contentWarnings: Rated PG-13 for depictions of death, alcohol, and drugs.

show.title: Mama Won't Fly
show.author: Jones Hope Wooten
show.description: Synopsis: An outrageously hilarious race against the clock begins when Savannah Sprunt Fairchild Honeycutt agrees to get her feisty mother all the way from Alabama to California in time for her brother's wedding. Savannah's problem: Mama won't fly. With only four days to make it to the ceremony, this determined daughter has no choice but to drive cross-country with her equally willful mother, Norleen Sprunt, in Mama's vintage sedan. As Savannah steels herself for this hastily conceived road trip, another outrageous complication arises: the bubbly, over-eager bride-to-be arrives unannounced. Hayley Quinn, delighted to finally meet her future in-laws, is convinced that travelling together to her wedding is the perfect way to bond. The folly of her decision quickly becomes apparent when the journey begins and comedic chaos ensues. Every conceivable—and inconceivable—mishap that can occur does.
show.contentWarnings: Rated PG-13 for mild adult themes.

show.title: Annie
show.author: Thomas Meehan (book)
show.description:
Leapin' Lizards! The irrepressible comic strip heroine takes center stage in one of the world's best-loved musicals.

With equal measures of pluck and positivity, little orphan Annie charms everyone's hearts despite a next-to-nothing start in 1930s New York City. She is determined to find the parents who abandoned her years ago on the doorstep of a New York City Orphanage that is run by the cruel, embittered Miss Hannigan. With the help of the other girls in the Orphanage, Annie escapes to the wondrous world of NYC. In adventure after fun-filled adventure, Annie foils Miss Hannigan's evil machinations... and even befriends President Franklin Delano Roosevelt! She finds a new home and family in billionaire, Oliver Warbucks, his personal secretary, Grace Farrell, and a lovable mutt named Sandy.

show.title: Swept Away
show.author: John Logan (book)
show.description: Synopsis: In 1888, four men aboard a whaling ship—Mate, a haunted soul; a guilt-ridden Captain; Little Brother, an adventurous romantic; and his devout sibling, Big Brother—are shipwrecked off the coast of New Bedford, Massachusetts. Stranded on a lifeboat, they are forced to confront their pasts, moral choices, and the limits of human endurance as they fight for survival. Their story unfolds through the poetic book by John Logan and the hauntingly beautiful and raw music of The Avett Brothers, with a gripping narrative that explores themes of sacrifice, forgiveness, brotherhood, and redemption.
show.contentWarnings: Rated PG-13 for adult themes.

show.title: La Maison des Horreurs: An Evening at the Grand Guignol
show.description: Experience the shocks, suspense, and horrors of the legendary Parisian theatre. Enter if you dare...
show.contentWarnings: Graphic horror content in the Grand Guignol tradition; likely includes depictions of violence and gore.

show.title: Grey House
show.author: Levi Holloway
show.description: A winter storm, a remote cabin, and terrifying secrets within. Broadway's chilling thriller where nothing is what it seems.
show.contentWarnings: Disturbing psychological horror content.

show.title: Whisper House
show.author: Kyle Jarrow (book)
show.description: A lonely boy sent to a remote lighthouse is haunted by restless spirits in this musical ghost story from Tony-winning composer Duncan Sheik.
show.contentWarnings: Themes of death, grief, wartime paranoia, and ghosts.

show.title: The Little Dog Laughed
show.author: Douglas Carter Beane
show.description: A closeted rising movie star, his fiercely ambitious and manipulative agent, a charming male escort, and the escort's on-again-off-again girlfriend collide in this sharp, satirical comedy about Hollywood, image, ambition, and the lengths people will go to protect a career.
show.contentWarnings: Adult themes and language.

show.title: Looped
show.author: Matthew Lombardo
show.description: Inspired by a true event: legendary, larger-than-life actress Tallulah Bankhead is called into a Hollywood studio in 1965 to re-record a single line of dialogue for a film. What should take minutes stretches into a chaotic, hilarious, and surprisingly poignant marathon session as Tallulah, wildly drunk and utterly unfiltered, clashes with the film's exhausted editor.
show.contentWarnings: Adult language and references to substance use.

show.title: Speed-the-Plow
show.author: David Mamet
show.description: Two cynical Hollywood studio executives are on the verge of greenlighting a formulaic, guaranteed-hit blockbuster when a temporary secretary convinces one of them to instead champion a strange, high-minded literary novel about the end of the world. A sharp, fast-talking satire of ambition, integrity, and the movie business.
show.contentWarnings: Adult language and themes.

show.title: True West
show.author: Sam Shepard
show.description: Two estranged brothers — Austin, a buttoned-up Hollywood screenwriter, and Lee, a rootless drifter and petty thief — are thrown together in their mother's suburban California kitchen. As a screenplay deal draws them into escalating rivalry, the brothers' identities begin to blur and unravel, in a searing, darkly comic look at family, ambition, and the myth of the American West.
show.contentWarnings: Contains violence and adult language.

show.title: Hollywood Arms
show.author: Carrie Hamilton & Carol Burnett
show.description: A semi-autobiographical drama co-written by Carol Burnett and her daughter Carrie Hamilton, based on Burnett's own memoir. The play follows a young girl growing up in 1940s Hollywood, raised largely by her tough but loving grandmother amid her parents' struggles with alcoholism, finding resilience and humor even in hardship.
show.contentWarnings: Depicts alcoholism and family hardship.

show.title: Hollywood
show.author: Joe DiPietro
show.description: A drama set against the backdrop of the 1920s silent film industry, centered on the real, still-unsolved 1922 murder of director William Desmond Taylor — a scandal that gripped the nation and exposed the seedy underbelly beneath the glamour of early Hollywood. I have moderate confidence in this synopsis; recommend a quick verification before publishing given limited available detail on this particular script.

show.title: Hollywood, Nebraska
show.author: Kenneth Jones
show.description: Two fortysomething actresses return to their once-thriving hometown in the Nebraska panhandle for separate family emergencies — one to check on her ailing mother, the other to bury her father. Distracted by two charismatic local men, both women are forced to reckon with the choices that took them away and the pull of the place — and the people — they left behind. A hope-filled, tears-and-laughter comedy about small towns, big dreams, and coming home.
show.contentWarnings: Contains adult language.

show.title: Mean Girls
show.author: Tina Fey (book, based on the Paramount Pictures film)
show.description: The smash-hit Broadway musical based on the iconic film. When Cady Heron, homeschooled in Africa for years, transfers to an American public high school, she's quickly swept into the orbit of the Plastics — North Shore High's most ruthless, popular clique, led by queen bee Regina George. Filled with sharp comedy, infectious music, and timely themes, it's one of the season's biggest crowd-pleasers.

show.title: Dracula: A Comedy of Terrors
show.author: Gordon Greenberg & Steve Rosen (very loosely based on Dracula by Bram Stoker)
show.description: A Charleston regional premiere, fresh off runs in London's West End and Off-Broadway. A meek English real estate agent journeys to Transylvania to meet a mysterious new client, unaware he's about to meet the world's most infamous vampire. Just five actors play more than a dozen characters — including Van Helsing, Harker, Mina, and Lucy — in this gender-bending, lightning-fast comic spoof.
show.contentWarnings: Recommended for ages 16 and up. Uses strobe lighting, flashing lights, theatrical fog and other atmospheric effects.

show.title: Les Liaisons Dangereuses
show.author: Christopher Hampton (adapted from the novel by Pierre Choderlos de Laclos)
show.description: The season's lone dramatic offering: an elegant, gripping story of seduction, manipulation, and revenge among the aristocracy of pre-Revolutionary France. Two former lovers wage a cruel game of sexual conquest and psychological warfare, using others as pawns until the game turns deadly.
show.contentWarnings: Mature sexual themes and manipulation.

show.title: Shear Madness
show.author: Paul Pörtner (original); American adaptation by Bruce Jordan & Marilyn Abrams
show.description: One of the longest-running non-musical plays in the world. A murder occurs above a busy Charleston hair salon, and the audience becomes part of the investigation — quizzing suspects and voting each night on who they believe is guilty. Since the ending is decided live by the crowd, no two performances are ever the same.

show.title: A Christmas Story
show.author: Philip Grecian (adapted from the book by Jean Shepherd)
show.description: Back by popular demand. Inspired by the beloved 1983 film, this heartwarming and hilariously relatable tale follows 9-year-old Ralphie Parker on his one big Christmas mission: securing a genuine Red Ryder BB gun. From pleading his case to his mom, his teacher, and Santa himself, Ralphie's journey brings all the film's classic scenes to life — the grumpy furnace, the triple-dog dare at the frozen flagpole, the 'major award' leg lamp, and Ralphie's wild daydreams of heroism. NOTE: this show is not part of the Season 95 MainStage subscription package.

show.title: Barefoot in the Park
show.author: Neil Simon
show.description: Paul and Corie Bratter are newlyweds in every sense of the word. He's a straight-as-an-arrow lawyer; she's a free spirit always chasing the next kick. Their new apartment is her latest find — too expensive, with bad plumbing and in need of a paint job. After a six-day honeymoon, they get a surprise visit from Corie's loopy mother, and Corie decides to play matchmaker during a dinner with their eccentric upstairs neighbor, Velasco, where everything that can go wrong does.

show.title: The Red Velvet Cake War
show.author: Jessie Jones, Nicholas Hope & Jamie Wooten
show.description: Small-town rivalry turns deliciously funny in this heartwarming Southern comedy. Two families compete in a fierce baking contest, uncovering long-held secrets and serving up laughter along the way.

linkedVenueId.name: North Iredell High School Performing Arts Center

show.title: Disney's High School Musical
show.author: David Simpatico (book)
show.composer: Matthew Gerrard, Robbie Nevil & others (original songs)
show.description: Get ready to sing and dance along with Disney's High School Musical! Troy, Gabriella, and their classmates navigate the ups and downs of high school, friendship, and following your dreams in this energetic, feel-good musical.

linkedVenueId.name: North Iredell High School Performing Arts Center

show.title: All Shook Up
show.author: Joe DiPietro (book)
show.description: A 1950s jukebox musical set in a conservative Midwestern town, featuring the catalog of Elvis Presley. Inspired by Shakespeare's Twelfth Night, the plot follows a leather-clad roustabout named Chad who rides into town, upending strict morality laws, inspiring rock 'n' roll rebellion, and triggering a chaotic chain of unrequited love.

show.title: Charlotte's Web
show.author: Joseph Robinette (adapted from the novel by E.B. White)
show.description: Our talented young performers bring E.B. White's beloved story to life. Follow Wilbur the pig and his clever friend Charlotte in a heartwarming tale of friendship, courage, and hope.

show.title: The Lion, The Witch & The Wardrobe
show.author: Adapted from The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe by C.S. Lewis
show.description: Step through the wardrobe and into the magical land of Narnia in this immersive, family-friendly walking-tour adaptation. Join Lucy, Edmund, Susan, and Peter as they battle the White Witch and discover the courage and wonder that lies within.

linkedVenueId.name: West Iredell High School Performing Arts Center

show.title: To Kill a Mockingbird
show.author: Christopher Sergel (adapted from the novel by Harper Lee)
show.description: Experience the timeless story of justice, morality, and growing up in the racially divided South in this powerful stage adaptation of Harper Lee's classic novel, following young Scout Finch as her father Atticus defends an innocent Black man against false accusations.
show.contentWarnings: Depicts racial injustice and violence.

show.title: Wait Until Dark
show.author: Frederick Knott
show.description: Hold your breath! A gripping thriller about a blind woman who must outwit a group of dangerous criminals in her own apartment. Suspense and tension build with every twist in this classic stage thriller.
show.contentWarnings: Contains suspenseful/threatening content.

linkedCompanyId.name: The Freedom Players Youth Theatre Group

show.title: Little Shop of Horrors
show.author: Howard Ashman (book)
show.description: Meek floral assistant Seymour Krelborn stumbles upon a strange and interesting plant, which he names Audrey II after his coworker crush. The plant turns out to have a mysterious craving for human blood, and as it grows in size and popularity, Seymour is drawn into a deal with dark consequences. This off-beat, off-Broadway sci-fi musical comedy blends horror, romance, and 1960s doo-wop-inspired music into a beloved cult classic. The Freedom Players' Autumn 2026 production, the third and final installment of their 2026 season following To Kill a Mockingbird and Shrek Jr.

show.title: Head Over Heels
show.author: Jeff Whitty (conceived and original book); adapted by James Magruder (based on "The Arcadia" by Sir Philip Sidney)
show.description: In a campy celebration of love and identity, the royal family of Arcadia tries to outrun four ominous prophecies to keep their famous 'Beat.' From the team behind Avenue Q, Spring Awakening, and Hedwig and the Angry Inch comes a pop-punk mash-up of hit songs by The Go-Go's. By the end of this gender-rollercoaster ride, one thing is certain: 'We Got the Beat.'

show.title: The Courtroom: A Reenactment of One Woman's Deportation Proceedings
show.author: Transcripts arranged by Arian Moayed
show.description: For some living in the United States, one wrong stroke of a pen can change a life. This documentary-style play tells the true story of Elizabeth Keathley, a Filipina immigrant who checked the wrong box after years of correctly following procedure, and found herself at the mercy of the U.S. immigration system. Using text taken verbatim from real court transcripts, the production follows Elizabeth's journey from Chicago Immigration Court to the U.S. Court of Appeals, at a time when dialogue around immigration and deportation is more urgent than ever.
show.contentWarnings: Depicts real immigration/deportation legal proceedings.

show.title: The African Company Presents Richard III
show.author: Carlyle Brown
show.description: In the Grand Ballroom of the first-ever hotel in the United States, the African Company prepares to continue their sold-out run of Shakespeare's Richard III — six nights a week, 300 people a house. But a leading New York City producer has plans to stage his own white Richard III nearby, and he'll go to terrible lengths to remove the competition. Based on a true story from roughly forty years before the end of slavery, exploring race, artistic legitimacy, and the fight to be seen.
show.contentWarnings: Depicts racism and the realities of American slavery-era society.

show.title: Gross Indecency: The Three Trials of Oscar Wilde
show.author: Moisés Kaufman
show.description: From trial transcripts, personal correspondence, interviews, and other direct source material, the playwright behind The Laramie Project reconstructs the three legal trials that changed the life of Oscar Wilde. Wilde's artistry and wit flare against censorship, homophobia, and discrimination in a play that chronicles his journey from toast of the town to social pariah.
show.contentWarnings: Depicts historical homophobia and legal persecution.

show.title: Continuity
show.author: Bess Wohl
show.description: A film crew has six takes to complete their climate change film, but when panic, ego, and Hollywood money creep into the process, the actual issues at stake might seep out of frame entirely. This action movie's plot gets as fictionally outlandish as the interpretation of the climate facts contained within, in a sharp satire of art, activism, and the entertainment industry.

linkedVenueId.name: Wortham Center for the Performing Arts

show.title: 369 Monologue and Short Play Festival Part 4: Get Up STAND UP
show.author: Various playwrights
show.description: The fourth year of Different Strokes!'s signature series of monologues and short plays. This year's theme: Get Up, STAND UP! — stories of inspiration, success, or survival, despite the odds. Featuring material from local authors and writers from around the world.

linkedVenueId.name: Wortham Center for the Performing Arts

show.title: The Charleston Gambit
show.author: Chesney Goodson
show.description: Step aboard history's most daring escape in this riveting one-man show bringing the legendary Robert Smalls to life. Born enslaved in Beaufort, South Carolina, Smalls commandeered a Confederate warship in 1862, sailing himself and his crew to freedom. His audacity changed the course of the Civil War, and his later legacy as a statesman helped reshape Reconstruction. A world premiere performed by Chesney Goodson (last seen in DS!PAC's Juked), directed by Stephanie Hickling Beckman, spanning Smalls' transformation from enslaved pilot to U.S. Congressman.
show.contentWarnings: Depicts the realities of American slavery.

show.title: Jane Austen's Northanger Abbey
show.author: Adapted by Emma Szuba, based on the novel by Jane Austen
show.description: One of two new plays performed in repertory, adapted from Jane Austen's first and last completed novels. Young Catherine Morland, an avid reader of Gothic novels, is invited to the fashionable resort town of Bath, where her overactive imagination leads her to suspect dark, sinister secrets lurking within the walls of Northanger Abbey. A playful send-up of the Gothic novel genre wrapped in Austen's signature wit. Adapted and directed by Emma Szuba.

tickets.notes: General Admission $25; Students, Seniors & Artists $20. See both Northanger Abbey and Persuasion with the $40 Jane Austen Pass. Each play runs about 2 hours, including a 15-minute intermission. Free tea party and Regency dance lesson between the Saturday shows (Nov. 7 and 14); costumes encouraged.

show.title: Much Ado About Nothing
show.author: William Shakespeare
show.description: A witty battle of the sexes unfolds as the sharp-tongued Beatrice and Benedick are tricked into falling for one another, while a darker plot threatens to destroy the marriage of young lovers Hero and Claudio. One of Shakespeare's most beloved comedies, full of wordplay, mistaken identity, and romance. Directed by Emma Szuba.

show.title: Jane Austen's Persuasion
show.author: Adapted by Emma Szuba, based on the novel by Jane Austen
show.description: The second of two new plays performed in repertory, adapted from Jane Austen's first and last completed novels. Years after breaking off her engagement to naval officer Frederick Wentworth under family pressure, Anne Elliot encounters him again, now a wealthy and successful captain. As old feelings resurface amid the shifting social tides of Regency England, Anne must decide whether it's too late for second chances. Adapted and directed by Emma Szuba.

tickets.notes: General Admission $25; Students, Seniors & Artists $20. See both Northanger Abbey and Persuasion with the $40 Jane Austen Pass. Each play runs about 2 hours, including a 15-minute intermission. Free tea party and Regency dance lesson between the Saturday shows (Nov. 7 and 14); costumes encouraged.

show.title: On Golden Pond
show.author: Ernest Thompson
show.description: Brunswick Little Theatre closes its 2026 season with the poignant blockbuster On Golden Pond, directed by Ken Greenman. Made popular by the acclaimed film starring Henry Fonda and Katharine Hepburn, the story follows an aging couple, Norman and Ethel Thayer, spending the summer at their Maine lake house with their new teenage stepchild. The play touches on themes of aging with grace, building generational bridges, and mending family relationships, exploring the turbulent relationship between father and daughter and the difficulties faced by a couple in the twilight years of a long marriage.

show.title: Yes, Virginia, There Is a Santa Claus
show.author: Andrew Fenady
show.description: Brunswick Little Theatre ends its 2026 season with this perennial holiday favorite. Set in New York City in 1897, this radio drama follows eight-year-old Virginia O'Hanlon, who suddenly finds herself facing a crisis of belief when her friends tell her Santa Claus isn't real. Determined to know the truth, Virginia writes a letter to a local newspaper asking for a definitive answer to that most crucial of Christmas questions — inspired by the real, famous 1897 New York Sun editorial written in response to an actual letter from an 8-year-old Virginia O'Hanlon.

show.title: The Hope of Oz
show.description: Set a decade after Dorothy's defeat of the Wicked Witch of the West and her subsequent departure, this original dark fantasy brings us to a newly invigorated Capital where the Wizard's power has grown immensely amid constant systematic oppression of his denizens and a drug-fueled war with a new cadre of Witches that brings its citizens to their knees. The story follows Gale, an investigative 'Witch-hunter,' on the trail of East's assassination. Trapped in a bar with a synthetic (known as a mimic), surrounded by encroaching revolutionaries, Witches, and the Wizard's ever-watchful eyes, Gale must survive the night if Oz will see its dawn. But in an empire of extremes, who can survive? Directed by Gabby Bailey.
show.contentWarnings: Contains mature/dark themes including drug abuse, violence, and systemic oppression.

show.title: Crimes of the Heart
show.author: Beth Henley
show.description: A southern gothic drama that uses dark comedy to tell the tale of three eccentric sisters as they escape their dark past to seize their future.

show.title: It's a Wonderful Life: Radio Play
show.author: Adapted from the 1946 film
show.description: This 1946 classic American holiday story follows George Bailey and his guardian angel, Clarence, as Clarence tries to save his life. George, a despondent, self-sacrificing man, contemplates taking his own life on Christmas Eve until heavenly intervention shows him how profoundly he has impacted the lives of those around him. Presented in radio-play format.

show.title: The Glass Menagerie
show.author: Tennessee Williams
show.description: A 1944 memory play set during the Great Depression, following Tom Wingfield, his mother Amanda, and his sister Laura. The story explores the family's struggles with poverty, shattered dreams, and a fragile escape from reality.

show.title: Next to Normal
show.author: Brian Yorkey (book & lyrics)
show.description: A rock musical about Diana Goodman, a suburban mother with bipolar disorder, and how her mental illness and unacknowledged grief tear her family apart.
show.contentWarnings: Explores mental illness, grief, and drug use; contains mature themes.

show.title: Come From Away
show.author: Irene Sankoff & David Hein
show.description: Come From Away tells the remarkable true story of a small town that welcomed the world. On September 11, 2001, 38 planes carrying nearly 7,000 passengers were unexpectedly grounded in Gander, Newfoundland, nearly doubling the town's population overnight. As fear and uncertainty gripped the world, the people of Gander opened their homes, hearts, and community to stranded travelers from across the globe. Filled with soaring music, humor, and humanity, this critically acclaimed musical celebrates the power of community and the extraordinary kindness that can emerge in the face of tragedy.
show.contentWarnings: Contains discussion related to the September 11 terrorist attacks.

show.title: Charlotte's Web
show.author: Joseph Robinette (adapted from the novel by E.B. White)
show.description: When Wilbur, a small pig with a big heart, learns that his future on the farm is uncertain, he finds an unexpected champion in Charlotte — a wise and wonderful spider with a talent for writing. With the help of Fern, who understands the language of animals, and Templeton, a reluctant but resourceful rat, Charlotte hatches a plan to change Wilbur's fate. As mysterious messages begin appearing in her web, the barnyard — and soon the whole town — takes notice. Gentle, funny, and deeply moving, Charlotte's Web is a classic, heartwarming tale that celebrates loyalty, kindness, and what it truly means to be a friend.

show.title: Finding Nemo
show.author: Lindsay Anderson (book adaptation, based on the 2003 Disney/Pixar film written by Andrew Stanton, Bob Peterson & David Reynolds)
show.description: Based on the 2003 Disney/Pixar film, Finding Nemo follows Marlin, an anxious and over-protective clownfish who lives in the Great Barrier Reef with his kid Nemo. When Nemo is captured and taken to Sydney, Marlin faces his fears and sets off on an epic odyssey across the ocean. With the help of lovable characters such as optimistic Dory, laid-back sea turtle Crush, and the supportive Tank Gang, Marlin and Nemo both overcome challenges on their journey to find each other and themselves. Disney and Pixar's Finding Nemo: A 60-Minute Family Musical is a new stage version of the beloved film designed specifically for young audiences, featuring a memorable score from award-winning songwriting team Kristen Anderson-Lopez and Robert Lopez (Frozen, Coco). Music and orchestrations adapted and arranged by Myrna Conn.

show.title: The Addams Family: A New Musical Comedy
show.author: Marshall Brickman & Rick Elice (book, based on characters created by Charles Addams)
show.description: Presented through special arrangement with Theatrical Rights Worldwide. Wednesday Addams, the ultimate princess of darkness, has grown up and fallen in love with Lucas, a sweet, smart young man from a respectable family her parents have never met. Wednesday confides in her father Gomez and begs him not to tell her mother Morticia, forcing Gomez to keep a secret from his beloved wife for the first time ever. Everything changes for the whole family on the fateful night they host a dinner for Lucas and his parents. Directed by Lauren S. Parker, music directed by Heaven Watson-Weary.
show.contentWarnings: Rated PG for some adult content/humor/language.

show.title: Evil Dead: The Musical
show.author: George Reinblatt (book & lyrics)
show.composer: Frank Cipolla, Christopher Bond, Melissa Morris & George Reinblatt
show.description: It's back! Evil Dead: The Musical takes all the elements of the cult classic trilogy — The Evil Dead, Evil Dead 2, and Army of Darkness — and combines them for one of the craziest, funniest, and bloodiest theatrical experiences of all time. Five college students go to an abandoned cabin in the woods, and they accidentally unleash an evil force that turns them all into demons. It's all up to Ash, a housewares employee turned demon-killing hero, and his trusty chainsaw to save the day. Blood flies, limbs are severed, and demons tell bad jokes — all set to a completely off-the-wall score with titles like 'All the Men in My Life Keep Getting Killed by Candarian Demons.' This is a pure comedy from start to finish — you don't need to be a fan of Evil Dead, horror, or even musicals to love this show, as long as you like having fun. It's also the only show with a 'Splatter Zone' — a section of the audience that gets covered in fake blood. The first four rows are now considered the Splatter Zone, so beware where you purchase your tickets!
show.contentWarnings: Comedic depictions of gore/blood (splatter zone effects); not intended to be scary or graphic in tone.

show.title: Into the Woods JR
show.author: James Lapine (book)
show.description: This musical follows a Baker and his wife, Cinderella, and Jack (and the Beanstalk) as they journey into the woods to break a Witch's curse, learning that wishes come with consequences and responsibilities. Presented through special arrangement with Music Theatre International (MTI).

show.title: Elf Jr
show.author: Thomas Meehan & Bob Martin (book, based on the New Line Cinema film written by David Berenbaum)
show.description: Buddy, a young orphan, mistakenly crawls into Santa's bag of gifts and is transported to the North Pole. The would-be elf is raised, unaware that he is actually a human, until his enormous size and poor toy-making abilities cause him to face the truth. With Santa's permission, Buddy embarks on a journey to New York City to find his birth father and discover his true identity. Faced with the harsh reality that his father is on the naughty list and that his half-brother doesn't even believe in Santa, Buddy is determined to win over his new family and help New York remember the true meaning of Christmas. Presented through special arrangement with MTI. Happening at the Burnsville Town Center, a different venue from Parkway's main stage.

show.title: The Enchanted Bookshop: The Musical
show.author: Todd Wallinger (book)
show.description: An ordinary used bookshop by day, A Likely Story becomes a magical place each night. Thanks to a spell from the Book Fairy, the characters inside the books come alive every evening. Six of those characters — Dorothy Gale, Robin Hood, Pollyanna, Sherlock Holmes, Heidi, and Tom Sawyer — long to help Margie, the scatterbrained owner, save her struggling store, but they're not allowed to leave the building or be seen by human eyes. So when a pair of bungling smugglers comes looking for a stolen necklace hidden inside one of the books, the characters are torn: should they warn Margie and risk disappearing forever, or find a way to defeat the crooks without being seen? With appearances by other literary characters like the Queen of Hearts, Long John Silver, and Doctor Doolittle, and a toe-tapping jazz, march, and pop score, this charming musical celebrates the joy of reading for audiences young and old.

show.title: The Crucible
show.author: Arthur Miller
show.description: Arthur Miller's landmark drama uses the Salem witch trials as an allegory for the McCarthy-era Red Scare. As accusations of witchcraft sweep through a small Puritan community, personal grudges, fear, and mass hysteria spiral out of control, forcing ordinary people to choose between protecting themselves and standing by the truth. A powerful examination of integrity, reputation, and the destructive power of collective panic.
show.contentWarnings: Due to subject matter and sensitivity, cast is 18+ only. Explores false accusations, mass hysteria, and execution.

show.title: The Hitchcock Radio Hour
show.description: Start your Halloween fun a few days early by experiencing what it was like to be a member of the studio audience of a 1940s live Hitchcock Radio Hour broadcast. Two tales of horror and suspense are on tap, complete with spooky background music and sound effects performed live on stage: 'Mark of a Beast' and 'Cask of Amontillado.'

show.title: A Banner Elk Christmas
show.description: Don't miss the holiday show that has become a must-see in the NC High-Country. It's a fast-paced homage to the television holiday musical variety shows of the 60's and 70's, complete with all or parts of nearly forty songs, lots of choreography and costume changes, patterned after the Andy Williams and Bing Crosby TV Christmas specials.

show.title: It's a Wonderful Life: A Live Radio Play
show.author: Joe Landry (adapted)
show.description: It's Christmas Eve, 1946, and the cast and crew of radio station WBFR are bringing you a live broadcast of the most beloved holiday story ever told. But when a massive snowstorm keeps most of the cast from making it in, a handful of actors and crew members must step up and save the show. Watch as this scrappy ensemble voices dozens of characters, conjures an entire world with nothing but microphones, sound effects, and pure theatrical magic, and reminds us all why George Bailey's story still matters. Warm, witty, and wonderfully nostalgic, this charming production is a love letter to old-time radio, community, and the people who make life worth living. Directed by Glenna Grant. Performed in the Fangmeyer Theatre.

show.title: The Complete Works of William Shakespeare (Abridged) [Revised]
show.author: Adam Long, Daniel Singer & Jess Winfield
show.description: To celebrate the 20th anniversary of the Reduced Shakespeare Company's classic farce, two of its original writer/performers (Daniel Singer and Jess Winfield) thoroughly revised the show to bring it up to date for 21st-century audiences, incorporating some of the funniest material from the numerous amateur and professional productions performed throughout the world. This cultural touchstone was born when three inspired, charismatic comics, having honed their pass-the-hat act at Renaissance fairs, premiered their preposterous masterwork at the Edinburgh Festival Fringe in 1987. It quickly became a worldwide phenomenon, earning the title of London's longest-running comedy after a decade at the Criterion Theatre, and remains one of the world's most frequently produced plays, translated into several dozen languages. Featured are all 37 of Shakespeare's plays, meant to be performed in 97 minutes, by three actors. Fast paced, witty, and physical, it's full of laughter for Shakespeare lovers and haters alike.

show.title: Reader's Theatre: The Inspector General
show.author: Nikolai Gogol
show.description: A satirical play by Russian author Nikolai Gogol, first performed in 1836. Set in a small provincial town, the narrative revolves around the mayor, Anton Antonovich, who receives alarming news that an incognito inspector from the capital is visiting to assess the region. In a frenzied attempt to avoid exposure of corruption and incompetence, the local officials scramble to cover up their misdeeds and present a façade of respectability. The plot intensifies with the arrival of Khlestakov, a bumbling individual mistaken for the inspector. As the townspeople attempt to curry favor with him, they unwittingly expose their own corruption and absurdities.

show.title: Under the Guise of Piracy
show.author: Travis Lowe
show.description: A general history of the pyrates Bonny, Rackham, and Read, and their effect on the government and economic systems of the Caribbean colonies between the years of 1719 and 1720, having shaped an extra-lawful community surrounding the islands of Cuba, Jamaica, and Hispañola in the form of living, laughing, loving, and generally giving the finger to all governmental and corporate entities. Written by a local playwright and recently developed through Hendersonville Theatre's New Works Series, this swashbuckling mature comedy is a tale about recognizing and being your true self.
show.contentWarnings: Mature comedy content.

show.title: Nerdy Prudes Must Die
show.author: Matt Lang & Nick Lang (book)
show.description: A teen-slasher comedy about a group of geeks and their ghostly tormentor, from StarKid, the creators of Trail to Oregon and The Guy Who Didn't Like Musicals. When the biggest losers at Hatchetfield High unwittingly complete an ancient, evil ritual, they unleash an all-powerful, angry spirit with a grudge against nerds. That's when Stephanie Lauter, Grace Chasity, and a cast of social rejects must fight to save themselves and nerdy prudes everywhere. But can any of them survive the fury of a bully from beyond the grave?

show.title: Hand to God
show.author: Robert Askins
show.description: After the death of his father, meek Jason finds an outlet for his anxiety at the Christian Puppet Ministry, in the devoutly religious, relatively quiet small town of Cypress, Texas. Jason's complicated relationships with the town pastor, the school bully, the girl next door, and — most especially — his mother are thrown into upheaval when Jason's puppet, Tyrone, takes on a shocking and dangerously irreverent personality all its own. Hand to God explores the startlingly fragile nature of faith, morality, and the ties that bind us. Performed in Firmen's Kitchen (second stage). NOTE: this show's own detail page lists Oct 16-31, while the season overview page said Oct 16-21 — I used the individual page's range since it aligns with the full 3-weekend/Thursday pattern shown.

show.title: Men on Boats
show.author: Jaclyn Backhaus
show.description: Ten explorers. Four boats. One Grand Canyon. Men on Boats is the true(ish) history of an 1869 expedition, when a one-armed captain and a crew of insane yet loyal volunteers set out to chart the course of the Colorado River. With the adventurers played by an ensemble of women and gender-expansive actors, Men on Boats reframes masculine arrogance as a farcical, thrilling exploration of everything that goes into, well, exploration.

show.title: Constellations
show.author: Nick Payne
show.description: One relationship. Infinite possibilities. In how many universes would you love someone? Nick Payne's Olivier Award-winning play is about free will and friendship; it's about quantum multiverse theory, love, and honey. Roland is a beekeeper. Marianne is a quantum physicist. What are their odds of falling in love? With infinite moments that can change the trajectory of a life, it's anyone's guess how cosmic collision is possible. This play moves from the question of 'what if' to a poignant picture of 'what is.' Performed in Firmen's Kitchen (second stage).

show.title: Head Over Heels
show.author: Jeff Whitty (conceived and original book)
show.description: From the visionaries that rocked Broadway with Hedwig and the Angry Inch, Avenue Q, and Spring Awakening. This laugh-out-loud love story is set to the music of the iconic 1980s all-female rock band The Go-Go's, including 'We Got the Beat,' 'Vacation,' Belinda Carlisle's 'Heaven Is a Place on Earth,' and 'Mad About You.' A hilarious, exuberant celebration of love, this bold musical comedy follows the escapades of a royal family on an outrageous journey to save their beloved kingdom from extinction — only to discover the key to their realm's survival lies within each of their own hearts.

show.title: Frozen
show.author: Jennifer Lee (book)
show.description: In the beautiful kingdom of Arendelle, Princesses Anna and Elsa grow up sheltered inside their castle, isolated from the world and increasingly distant from each other. When Elsa is crowned queen, the magical powers she's desperately tried to conceal from her sister take control, and she flees into the mountains. As winter descends, Anna sets off on an epic journey to find Elsa and bring her home — with help from hardworking ice harvester Kristoff, his loyal reindeer Sven, and a happy-go-lucky snowman named Olaf. Full of magic, humor, and a stunning musical score, Frozen is a powerful tale of sisterhood, acceptance, and finding the real meaning of true love.

show.title: Imogen Says Nothing
show.author: Aditi Brennan Kapil
show.description: A revisionist comedy in verse and prose featuring Imogen, a character who only appears in the first folio of William Shakespeare's Much Ado About Nothing, speaks no lines, and is probably a typo. A modern hijacking of Shakespeare that investigates the voices that have been absented from our canon, and the consequences of cutting them. Performed in Firmen's Kitchen (second stage).

show.title: The Little Mermaid Jr
show.author: Doug Wright (book)
show.composer: Alan Menken (music); Howard Ashman & Glenn Slater (lyrics)
show.description: A Penguin Project production, returning to HCT for a second year. A trip to a magical underwater kingdom, where the beautiful young mermaid Ariel longs to leave her ocean home (and her fins) behind and live in the world above. But first, she'll have to defy her father, King Triton, and make a deal with the evil sea witch, Ursula, to convince Prince Eric that she's the girl whose enchanting voice he's been seeking.

show.title: Terminus
show.author: Gabriel Jason Dean
show.description: First produced in 2016, Terminus is a haunting and deeply human Southern Gothic drama set in rural Georgia. Eller Freeman and her grandson Jaybo share a fierce, unconventional bond in a weathered house by the railroad tracks. But as Eller's memory begins to slip and fragments of her past surface, the walls of the old family home seem to echo with buried truths. Past and present intertwine as Jaybo is forced to confront what love demands—and what history refuses to forget. This lyrical play blends psychological realism with ghostly imagination, exploring how the past lives on in the present and how the inheritance of history shapes us all.
show.contentWarnings: Contains mature themes including racism, family trauma, grief, and memory loss, as well as haunting imagery and emotionally intense situations.

show.title: Six Degrees of Separation
show.author: John Guare
show.description: What if a stranger could change your life with a single story? Inspired by actual events, Six Degrees of Separation follows a charismatic young con man who gains access to Manhattan's elite by claiming to be the son of Sidney Poitier. When Ouisa and Flan Kittredge welcome the brilliant Paul into their home, they're captivated by his charm and proximity to fame — until an unexpected discovery forces them to question everything. As they trace how he slipped so easily through their world, scandal gives way to something far more revealing. This Pulitzer Prize finalist popularized the phrase 'six degrees of separation' and examines race, privilege, and our longing for connection in a world built on illusion.
show.contentWarnings: Contains mature themes and adult language.

show.title: BKLYN the Musical
show.author: Mark Schoenfeld & Barri McPherson (book)
show.description: BKLYN is a high-voltage pop musical with a heart as big as the borough that inspired it. Beneath the Brooklyn Bridge, a troupe of street performers spins the tale of a young singer who travels from Paris to New York in search of the father she's never known. But her arrival ignites an epic battle for stardom with the reigning diva of the scene, forcing her to confront the cost of ambition and the meaning of home. With a contemporary pop score that demands powerhouse vocals and delivers one anthem after another, BKLYN is part concert, part fable, and entirely thrilling, blending the storytelling frame of Hadestown with the vocal fireworks of Dreamgirls.
show.contentWarnings: Contains mature themes.

show.title: Infinite Life
show.author: Annie Baker
show.description: In a fasting clinic in Northern California, five women swap stories, philosophize, and humorously provoke each other while undergoing a course of treatment that promises to cure a variety of ailments from cancer to thyroid issues, infections to chronic pain. A blazingly visceral yet often tremendously funny exploration of pain, endurance, and the awkwardness of strangers sharing endless days together. Directed by Heather Levinson.
show.contentWarnings: Discusses chronic illness and pain.

show.title: Little Women, the Musical
show.author: Allan Knee (book)
show.description: Based on Louisa May Alcott's beloved novel, Little Women: The Musical is a sweeping and heartfelt celebration of family, love, resilience, and the pursuit of dreams. Set during the Civil War, the story follows the remarkable March sisters — Jo, Meg, Beth, and Amy — as they navigate the joys and challenges of growing up. At its heart is the fiercely independent Jo March, an aspiring writer determined to tell stories that matter.

show.title: Dolly Parton's 9 to 5, the Musical
show.author: Patricia Resnick (book)
show.description: Featuring music and lyrics by the legendary Dolly Parton, 9 to 5: The Musical is the hilarious, high-energy comedy based on the beloved 1980 hit film. Set in the late 1970s, three overworked and underappreciated coworkers — Violet, Judy, and Doralee — have had enough of their sexist, egotistical boss. When an unexpected opportunity turns their daydreams of revenge into reality, the trio takes charge of the office and discovers just how powerful they can be together.

show.title: Inherit the Wind
show.author: Jerome Lawrence & Robert E. Lee
show.description: Inspired by the historic 1925 Scopes 'Monkey' Trial, Inherit the Wind is a powerful courtroom drama that explores the enduring conflict between faith, science, and the freedom to think. When a small-town Tennessee teacher is put on trial for teaching Charles Darwin's theory of evolution, the case ignites a national debate. Facing off are two brilliant legal minds: renowned defense attorney Henry Drummond, who champions intellectual freedom, and celebrated orator Matthew Harrison Brady, whose religious convictions fuel the prosecution.

show.title: Neil Simon's Barefoot in the Park
show.author: Neil Simon
show.description: Fresh from their honeymoon, newlyweds Paul and Corie Bratter couldn't be more different. Paul is a practical young lawyer who prefers order and routine, while Corie embraces life with boundless spontaneity. As they settle into their quirky New York apartment — with its tiny rooms, faulty plumbing, and eccentric upstairs neighbor — their honeymoon bliss is quickly tested by family visits, unexpected mishaps, and the realities of married life.

show.title: Agatha Christie's Murder on the Nile
show.author: Agatha Christie
show.description: Blessed with beauty, wealth, and a new husband, Kay Ridgeway seems destined for a perfect honeymoon as she embarks on a luxurious voyage down the Nile. But paradise quickly turns deadly when a shocking murder shatters the tranquility of the journey. With every passenger harboring secrets — and more than one motive for murder — the elegant river cruise becomes a trap where suspicion falls on everyone aboard. This version maintains the intrigue of the original while adding theatrical excitement and a stronger call to suspense.

show.title: The Hunchback of Notre Dame in Concert
show.author: Peter Parnell (book, based on the novel by Victor Hugo and the Disney film)
show.description: A special fundraising event for Lee Street theatre, featuring a 16-piece live orchestra with musicians from the Salisbury Symphony Orchestra performing Alan Menken and Stephen Schwartz's soaring score. Hidden away in the Notre Dame bell tower is Quasimodo, the kindhearted but isolated bell-ringer controlled by the powerful Archdeacon Claude Frollo. When Quasimodo ventures beyond the cathedral walls during the Feast of Fools, he encounters Esmeralda, a courageous young woman whose compassion changes his world. Featuring songs including 'The Bells of Notre Dame,' 'Out There,' 'God Help the Outcasts,' and 'Hellfire.' Directed by Rod Oden, music directed by Dr. Corey Gaston. Follows last year's sold-out Titanic in Concert fundraiser.

show.title: Spring Awakening
show.author: Steven Sater (book & lyrics, based on the play by Frank Wedekind)
show.description: Winner of 8 Tony Awards including Best Musical, Spring Awakening is the groundbreaking rock musical about young people struggling to understand themselves in a world determined to keep them in the dark. Germany, 1891: Wendla wants to understand the world beyond her sheltered existence; Melchior is intelligent and rebellious; his best friend Moritz buckles beneath crushing pressure. Their rigid, restrained world explodes into a contemporary rock concert as these young people give voice to everything they've been forbidden to say. A Lee Street LAB production.
show.contentWarnings: Contains strong language, sexual content and situations, discussions and depictions of sexual abuse, physical abuse, suicide, death, abortion, and mental health struggles.

show.title: for colored girls who have considered suicide / when the rainbow is enuf
show.author: Ntozake Shange
show.description: A landmark 'choreopoem' of American theatre combining poetry, dance, music, and movement. Seven women, identified by the colors of the rainbow, come together to share stories of love, joy, heartbreak, abandonment, identity, violence, friendship, sexuality, resilience, and self-discovery. First developed in the 1970s before arriving on Broadway in 1976, the work placed the voices and experiences of Black women unapologetically at the center of the theatrical event, and remains a vital exploration of survival, sisterhood, and self-worth. A Lee Street LAB production.
show.contentWarnings: Contains mature language and themes, including discussions and depictions of racism, sexism, sexuality, intimate partner violence, sexual violence, abortion, abandonment, death, child loss, and suicide/suicidal ideation.

show.title: The Third Man
show.author: Adapted from the novel/screenplay by Graham Greene
show.description: The American Premiere of The Third Man is a gripping theatrical adaptation of the classic noir film, set in post-World War II Vienna. American writer Holly Martins arrives in a city divided by occupying forces to reconnect with his old friend Harry Lime, only to discover Lime has apparently died under mysterious circumstances. As Holly investigates, he is pulled into a shadowy world of deception, black-market dealings, and moral ambiguity. This developmental production is directed by Sir Trevor Nunn, the Tony and Olivier Award-winning director of Broadway and West End's biggest musicals including Les Misérables, Cats, and Sunset Boulevard.

show.title: RENT
show.author: Jonathan Larson
show.description: Jonathan Larson's Tony Award and Pulitzer Prize-winning masterpiece changed the landscape of musical theatre forever. Set in New York City's East Village during the height of the HIV/AIDS epidemic, Rent follows a vibrant group of artists, musicians, and friends as they pursue their dreams while confronting poverty, illness, addiction, and the fragility of life. Powered by an electrifying rock score featuring iconic songs like 'Seasons of Love,' 'La Vie Bohème,' and 'Take Me or Leave Me,' this groundbreaking musical inspires audiences to measure life 'in love.'
show.contentWarnings: Contains mature themes including drug use, HIV/AIDS, and adult relationships.

show.title: Kimberly Akimbo
show.author: David Lindsay-Abaire (book & lyrics)
show.description: Funny, poignant, and utterly original, Kimberly Akimbo is the Tony Award-winning Best Musical that reminds us life isn't valued by the years we have, but by how fully we choose to live them. As Kimberly navigates first love, family chaos, and an extraordinary medical condition that causes her to age rapidly, she discovers that the greatest adventures come from embracing the unexpected. Overflowing with humor, heart, and hope, this unforgettable musical is a joyful celebration of making every moment count.

show.title: Ain't Too Proud: The Life and Times of the Temptations
show.author: Dominique Morisseau (based on the book "The Temptations" by Otis Williams with Patricia Romanowski)
show.description: The 2019 Tony Award-winning Broadway smash hit follows The Temptations' extraordinary journey from the streets of Detroit to the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame. Bursting with electrifying choreography, dazzling harmonies, and iconic songs including 'My Girl,' 'Just My Imagination,' and 'Papa Was a Rollin' Stone,' this musical chronicles the triumphs, trials, and brotherhood behind one of the greatest groups in music history. With 42 Top Ten hits and 14 No. 1 singles, Ain't Too Proud is an unforgettable celebration of the music that defined a generation and the legendary artists who created it.

show.title: Les Misérables
show.author: Alain Boublil & Claude-Michel Schönberg (book, based on the novel by Victor Hugo)
show.description: An undisputed masterpiece of musical theatre, Les Misérables has captivated audiences around the globe for more than 40 years. This epic tale follows the life of ex-convict Jean Valjean as he is ruthlessly pursued by Inspector Javert against the backdrop of the French Revolution. Winner of the Tony Award for Best Musical and Best Original Score, the production continues to move audiences with its timeless message that 'to love another person is to see the face of God.'

show.title: TR Sings...Rockin' Christmas
show.description: Join us in rockin' around the Christmas tree and celebrating the holiday season! This high energy event brings a rock-inspired twist to your favorite classic and modern Christmas songs, providing a festive and spirited night of music on the Cabaret stage. Part of Theatre Raleigh's TR Sings series, offering a platform to showcase the Triangle's extraordinary vocal talent.

show.title: The Santa Switch
show.composer: Various pop/holiday songs, arranged by Jesse Vargas
show.description: Set in mid-century New York City and the North Pole, The Santa Switch centers on Santa and Mrs. Claus as they consider retiring from the holiday grind after a century of service. But retirement becomes complicated when the magical Sleigh Bells choose Jack Chase, a cynical young New York advertising executive, as Santa's successor — and Jack refuses. His rejection puts the North Pole into crisis, threatening the future of Christmas itself. As Mrs. Claus steps forward to take charge, an idealistic young artist, a warmhearted children's charity worker, and a very determined group of elves become part of a chaotic, funny, and touching journey about discovering purpose and finding where you truly belong.

show.title: To Kill a Mockingbird
show.author: Christopher Sergel (adapted from the novel by Harper Lee)
show.description: Set in the small Southern town of Maycomb, Alabama, during the Great Depression, To Kill a Mockingbird is a powerful story about childhood, family, justice, prejudice, courage, and the loss of innocence. Seen largely through the eyes of Scout Finch, the story follows her father Atticus, a respected attorney appointed to defend Tom Robinson, a Black man falsely accused of assaulting a white woman. As the trial divides the community, Scout and Jem discover that the adult world is far more complicated than they imagined.
show.contentWarnings: Addresses racism, prejudice, violence, poverty, abuse, and injustice with period-accurate language.

show.title: You're a Good Man, Charlie Brown
show.author: Clark Gesner (book, music & lyrics); additional dialogue by Michael Mayer; additional music & lyrics by Andrew Lippa; based on the comic strip "Peanuts" by Charles M. Schulz
show.description: A charming, episodic musical that brings the beloved Peanuts gang to life on stage. Sad, morose Charlie Brown struggles to find meaning and his own place in the world alongside his mischievous dog Snoopy, sharp-witted sister Sally, domineering Lucy, wise blanket-toting Linus, and piano-obsessed Schroeder — a warm, funny slice-of-life look at childhood, friendship, and self-acceptance. Presented through special arrangement with Concord Theatricals. Directed by Danielle Comeau.
show.contentWarnings: Some heavier moments exploring grief, loneliness, and depression.

show.title: Liberation
show.author: Bess Wohl
show.description: It's 1970. Somewhere in Ohio, six women meet on a basketball court to form a consciousness-raising women's liberation group, determined to shake up their lives and change the world. Fifty years later, one of their daughters tries to understand where things fell apart. A provocative, wildly theatrical play that poses vital questions about friendship, legacy and the true meaning of liberation, investigating what we inherit, what we forget, and what we're still fighting to understand. Winner of the 2026 Tony Award for Best Play and 2026 Pulitzer Prize for Drama. Directed by Donna Bradby.
show.contentWarnings: Contains mature language, discussions of sexism, racism, sexuality, reproductive rights, and family relationships, as well as non-sexual nudity.

show.title: Here There Are Blueberries
show.author: Moisés Kaufman & Amanda Gronich
show.description: A special limited engagement staged reading. An album of never-before-seen World War II-era photographs arrives at the desk of United States Holocaust Memorial Museum archivist Rebecca Erbelding. As Rebecca and her team of historians begin to unravel the shocking mystery behind the images, the album soon makes headlines around the world. In Germany, a businessman recognizes his own grandfather in the photos and begins a journey of discovery into the lives of other Nazi descendants, reckoning with his family's past and his country's history. Confronts a difficult question: how do everyday people become monsters, and how do we face that capacity within ourselves? Directed by Robin Tynes-Miller.
show.contentWarnings: Shows real images of Nazis at death camps and centers the historical events surrounding the Holocaust.

show.title: Coal Country
show.author: Jessica Blank & Erik Jensen
show.description: Marking Three Bone Theatre's first musical. Coal Country tells the true story of the 2010 Upper Big Branch mine disaster, the deadliest American mining accident in nearly 50 years, which killed 29 men in Montcoal, West Virginia. Drawn from over 40 hours of interviews with survivors and the families left behind, this play with music brings their voices directly to the stage, woven together with original songs by Steve Earle that serve as a haunting, elegiac heartbeat throughout the piece. At its core, a story about what happens when corporate greed overrides worker safety, and why solidarity among working people matters now more than ever. Directed by Johnny Hohenstein.
show.contentWarnings: Depicts and discusses coal mining disasters, death, grief, and industrial safety failures, with references to real-life tragedy.

show.title: The Reservoir
show.author: Jake Brasch
show.description: A sharply funny, deeply moving semi-autobiographical new play about family, memory, and the messy work of healing. Fresh out of rehab and back home in Denver, Josh finds himself leaning on the last people he expected — his four aging grandparents, each navigating their own relationship to memory and dementia. What follows is equal parts hilarious and heartbreaking, as Jazzercise classes, unsolicited advice, and long-buried family history collide. Asks what we inherit from the people who raised us, and how we find our way back to ourselves through them. Directed by Glynnis O'Donoghue.
show.contentWarnings: Contains mature language, depictions of alcoholism and treatment, references to illness, memory loss, and dementia, and emotionally intense conversations about grief and personal struggle.

show.title: Purpose
show.author: Branden Jacobs-Jenkins
show.description: For decades, the Jasper family has stood as a pillar of Black American politics — civil rights leaders, pastors, congressmen. But when the youngest son returns home to Chicago with an uninvited guest in tow, old loyalties crack under the weight of long-buried secrets and unresolved resentments. As the family gathers under one roof, they're forced into a reckoning with faith, legacy, and the price of believing in something larger than yourself. A sharp, funny, and devastating portrait of a family determined to protect its public image even as the truth pushes to the surface. Winner of the 2025 Tony Award for Best Play and 2025 Pulitzer Prize for Drama. Directed by Sidney Horton.
show.contentWarnings: Contains mature language, family conflict, emotional and psychological abuse, discussions of race, religion, and generational trauma, as well as moments of intense interpersonal confrontation.

show.title: The Importance of Being Earnest
show.author: Oscar Wilde
show.description: Exploring themes of identity, social expectations, and the nature of truth and deception, this classic comedy follows two friends, Algernon Moncrieff and Jack Worthing, who both lead double lives to escape the constraints of Victorian society. Packed with unforgettable one-liners and razor-sharp wit, it remains one of the funniest plays ever written.

show.title: Bonnie & Clyde
show.author: Ivan Menchell (book)
show.description: Bored waitress Bonnie Parker falls in love with an ex-con named Clyde Barrow, and together they embark on a murderous cross-country crime spree stealing cars and robbing banks. A high-octane musical fusing rockabilly, blues, and gospel to tell the true story of the infamous outlaw couple whose romance and violence made them Depression-era legends.
show.contentWarnings: Depicts violence, crime, and gunfire.

linkedVenueId.name: 2nd Street Stage (Hannah Block Historic USO/Community Arts Center)

show.title: A Charlie Brown Christmas
show.author: Charles M. Schulz (based on the television special by Bill Melendez & Lee Mendelson); stage adaptation by Eric Schaeffer
show.description: The classic animated television special comes to life in this faithful stage adaptation, in which Charlie Brown, Snoopy, and the rest of the Peanuts gang discover the true meaning of Christmas. Charlie Brown is feeling down about the holiday and wonders what it's really all about. As he reluctantly directs the school Christmas play, he faces commercialism, chaos, and criticism from his friends. With the help of Linus and a tiny, overlooked Christmas tree, Charlie Brown discovers the true meaning of Christmas in this heartwarming holiday classic.

linkedVenueId.name: 2nd Street Stage (Hannah Block Historic USO/Community Arts Center)

show.title: Junie B. Jones Jingle Bells Batman Smells
show.author: Allison Gregory (adapted from the book by Barbara Park)
show.description: Laugh and learn with Junie B. Jones this holiday season! Tattletale May is constantly spoiling Junie B.'s fun. Junie hatches the perfect plan to teach her a lesson when she draws May's name for Secret Santa, but as her first-grade teacher Mr. Scary advises, 'The holidays are the time of year that we spread peace and goodwill.' Junie B. has a tough choice to make — keep the best gift for herself or discover the joy of giving. Through her hilarious antics, young audiences explore meaningful lessons about friendship, empathy, and the true spirit of the season.

linkedVenueId.name: 2nd Street Stage (Hannah Block Historic USO/Community Arts Center)

show.title: The Neverland Project
show.author: Stephen Gregg
show.description: You've heard of Peter Pan. You might even think you know the story — about a boy who can fly, about Neverland and pirates and Lost Boys and Tinker Bell. But you don't know the real story because the man who wrote it all down wasn't actually there. Wendy Moira Angela Darling, who was there, is about to fix that. She'll show you what really happened to Peter's shadow and how Peter learned to fly. She'll teach you about Tinker Bell (who is meaner than you thought), and introduce you to a key character you've never heard of, by staging a play called The Neverland Project. Get ready to fly, because the best way to explain Neverland is to take you there.

linkedVenueId.name: 2nd Street Stage (Hannah Block Historic USO/Community Arts Center)

show.title: Disney's The Lion King JR
show.author: Roger Allers & Irene Mecchi (book, based on the Broadway production directed by Julie Taymor)
show.composer: Elton John & Tim Rice; additional music/lyrics by Lebo M, Mark Mancina, Jay Rifkin & Hans Zimmer
show.description: Disney's The Lion King has captivated the imagination of audiences around the world, and now Thalian Youth Theatre brings the African savanna to life on stage with Simba, Rafiki, and an unforgettable cast of characters as they journey from Pride Rock to the jungle and back again in this inspiring coming-of-age tale. Features classic songs from the Broadway musical and animated film, including 'I Just Can't Wait to Be King,' 'He Lives in You,' and 'Hakuna Matata.' This production features an all-rookie cast, with free tickets to the public on a first-come, first-served basis.

linkedVenueId.name: 2nd Street Stage (Hannah Block Historic USO/Community Arts Center)

show.title: Seussical JR
show.author: Lynn Ahrens & Stephen Flaherty (book); co-conceived with Eric Idle
show.description: Now one of the most performed shows in America, Seussical is a fantastical, magical, musical extravaganza. Tony winners Lynn Ahrens and Stephen Flaherty have lovingly brought to life all our favorite Dr. Seuss characters, including Horton the Elephant, The Cat in the Hat, Gertrude McFuzz, lazy Mayzie, and a little boy with a big imagination — Jojo. The Cat in the Hat tells the story of Horton, an elephant who discovers a speck of dust containing the Whos, including Jojo, a Who child sent off to military school for thinking too many 'thinks.' Horton faces ridicule, danger, kidnapping, and a trial while protecting the Whos and guarding an abandoned egg left in his care by the irresponsible Mayzie La Bird — but the intrepid Gertrude McFuzz never loses faith in him.

show.title: Moon Over Buffalo
show.author: Ken Ludwig
show.description: In the madcap comedy tradition of Lend Me a Tenor, this hilarious farce centers on George and Charlotte Hay, fading stars of the 1950s. At the moment, they're playing Private Lives and Cyrano De Bergerac in rep in Buffalo, New York with just five actors. On the brink of a disastrous split-up caused by George's dalliance with a young ingénue, they receive word that they might just have one last shot at stardom: Frank Capra is coming to town to see their matinee, and if he likes what he sees, he might cast them in his movie remake of The Scarlet Pimpernel. Unfortunately for George and Charlotte, everything that could go wrong does, abetted by a visit from their daughter's clueless fiancé and hilarious uncertainty about which play they're actually performing, caused by Charlotte's deaf, old stage-manager mother who hates every bone in George's body. Directed by Mary Ross.

show.title: A Year with Frog and Toad
show.author: Willie Reale (book & lyrics)
show.description: Based on Arnold Lobel's well-loved books, and featuring a hummable score, this whimsical show follows two great friends — the cheerful, popular Frog and the rather grumpy Toad — through four fun-filled seasons. Waking from hibernation in the Spring, Frog and Toad plant gardens, swim, rake leaves, go sledding, and learn life lessons along the way. The two best friends celebrate and rejoice in the differences that make them unique and special. Part vaudeville, part make believe... all charm, A Year with Frog and Toad tells the story of a friendship that endures throughout the seasons. Directed by Vivian Stem and Kim Plyler.

show.title: Moscow Moscow Moscow Moscow Moscow Moscow
show.author: Halley Feiffer
show.description: Ever since their brother Andrey gambled away the family fortune, Olga, Masha, and Irina have been doomed to the boredom of the Russian countryside. One day soon, they hope, they'll return home to Moscow and live the exciting lives they were always meant to have. When the military comes to town, bringing with them variety, entertainment, and a whole lot of chaos, Moscow feels closer than ever and it seems the sisters' luck is about to change. In this contemporary twist on Chekhov's Three Sisters, one delightfully dysfunctional family navigates the absurdity of class, culture, and love. Directed by Stuart Parks II. Performed upstairs at The Black Pelican Restaurant.

show.title: Marjorie Prime
show.author: Jordan Harrison
show.description: It's the age of artificial intelligence, and 85-year-old Marjorie — a jumble of disparate, fading memories — has a handsome new companion who's programmed to feed the story of her life back to her. What would we remember, and what would we forget, if given the chance? In this richly spare, wondrous play, Jordan Harrison explores the mysteries of human identity and the limits, if any, of what technology can replace. Directed by Tim Hass. Performed at Dare Arts.

show.title: Lend Me a Soprano
show.description: A riotous, fast-moving farce packed with mistaken identities, backstage chaos, and perfectly timed entrances and exits. When a world-famous opera star goes missing right before curtain, an ambitious producer scrambles to save the night — leading to outrageous comedy, romantic mix-ups, and nonstop surprises.

show.title: Purlie Victorious
show.author: Ossie Davis
show.description: Dynamic traveling preacher Purlie Victorious Judson returns to his small Georgia town hoping to save Big Bethel, the community's church, and emancipate the cotton pickers who work on oppressive Ol' Cap'n Cotchipee's plantation. With the assistance of Lutiebelle Gussie Mae Jenkins, Purlie hopes to pry loose from Cotchipee an inheritance due his long-lost cousin and use the money to achieve his goals. Fortunately, Cotchipee's son Charlie proves to be far more fair-minded than his brutal father, saving the church from destruction with a brave act of defiance.

show.title: Finding Neverland
show.author: James Graham (book)
show.description: An inspiring, imaginative musical about playwright J.M. Barrie and the family who helped spark the creation of Peter Pan. As Barrie rediscovers play, possibility, and hope, audiences are swept into a world where dreams take flight. With soaring music and theatrical magic, it is a heartfelt story about family, healing, and the power of believing.

show.title: Robin Hood
show.description: Robin Hood follows the legendary outlaw who steals from the rich to give to the poor, leading a band of merry misfits in daring adventures through Sherwood Forest while standing up to the Sheriff of Nottingham. Packed with action, humor, and heart, this classic tale celebrates courage, justice, and community.

show.title: The Diary of Anne Frank
show.author: Frances Goodrich & Albert Hackett (based on the diary of Anne Frank)
show.description: Powerful and deeply human, The Diary of Anne Frank tells the true story of Anne and her family as they hide from the Nazis in an Amsterdam attic during World War II. Through Anne's wit, hope, and honesty, the play offers an unforgettable portrait of courage in the face of fear — and a reminder of the enduring strength of the human spirit.
show.contentWarnings: Depicts the realities of the Holocaust and Nazi persecution.

show.title: Emma! A Pop Musical (JV)
show.author: Paul Gordon (book, music & lyrics, based on the novel by Jane Austen)
show.description: Fresh, funny, and filled with catchy pop songs, this musical puts a modern twist on Jane Austen's classic comedy of manners. Emma is brilliant, confident — and convinced she is the best matchmaker around — until her well-intended meddling spirals into misunderstandings, surprises, and a lesson about listening to the heart.

linkedCompanyId.name: Triad Pride Performing Arts (Triad Pride Acting Company)

show.title: POTUS: Or, Behind Every Great Dumbass Are Seven Women Trying to Keep Him Alive
show.author: Selina Fillinger
show.description: A Tony-nominated Broadway farce about the seven women in the President's inner circle who scramble to contain a massive PR disaster after he uses a crude word to describe the First Lady. This fast-paced, R-rated comedy follows the chaos as these women — including the Chief of Staff, Press Secretary, and the President's sister — try to manage the fallout, leading to mistaken identities, substance use, and escalating absurdity. A satirical look at the women behind the scenes who keep the country running.
show.contentWarnings: Contains adult language, substance use, and mature political satire.

show.title: Winter Concert
show.description: TPPA's annual Winter Choral Concert brings together stunning vocal arrangements, festive holiday favorites, and brilliant contemporary harmonies performed by TPPA's Upper and Lower Voice Choruses to celebrate the winter season. NOTE: this appears to be a chorus concert rather than a Triad Pride Acting Company theatrical production, though staged under the same TPPA organizational umbrella.

show.title: Broadway Our Way
show.description: Broadway Our Way — Broadway favorites with a twist, presented by Triad Pride Acting Company.

show.title: Theatre For All - Spring Show
show.description: Theatre For All puts the spotlight on stories of performers with disabilities. Triad Pride Acting Company is proud to present Theatre For All, a program which provides a safe and accessible environment for individuals with disabilities to express their creativity on stage.
