show.title: Fun Home
show.author: Lisa Kron (book & lyrics, based on the graphic memoir by Alison Bechdel)
show.description: This Tony Award-winning musical tells the story of Alison's coming out as a lesbian and her complex relationship with her closeted, gay father, exploring memory, family secrets, and identity through a non-linear narrative that follows Alison at different ages. The show is celebrated for its groundbreaking, honest, and emotionally rich portrayal of these themes, winning 5 Tony Awards including Best Musical in 2015.
show.contentWarnings: Explores suicide, coming out, and complicated family/parental relationships.

show.title: This Murder Was Staged
show.description: Opening night. A brand-new mystery. One very dead director. The curtain rises on a brand-new murder mystery, and everything seems to be going according to plan — until the play's demanding director suddenly winds up dead onstage. Now the theatre is no longer just a place for make-believe; it's an active crime scene, and everyone is a suspect. With the cast, crew, and even members of the audience caught in the crosshairs, an intrepid detective must unravel a tangled web of secrets, motives, mistaken identities, and backstage rivalries. Fast-paced, delightfully chaotic, and packed with theatrical twists and turns, this is a hilarious backstage comedy where the drama is real, the suspects are everywhere, and absolutely nothing is going according to script.

show.title: Storybook Kids Weekend: The Adventures of Tiny Turkey
show.description: For kids ages 2 to 102! This special weekend begins with a kid-friendly buffet, followed by two special productions featuring Tiny Turkey — an amazing superhero with absolutely no powers! These shows come to life with goofy costumes, musical numbers, audience involvement, and lots of comedy sprinkled in. Each story runs approximately 30 minutes, with a 10-15 minute intermission for restroom breaks.

show.title: Rodgers + Hammerstein's Cinderella (Broadway Version)
show.author: Douglas Carter Beane (book)
show.description: The new Broadway adaptation of the classic musical. This contemporary take on the classic tale features Rodgers & Hammerstein's most beloved songs, including 'In My Own Little Corner,' 'Impossible/It's Possible,' and 'Ten Minutes Ago,' alongside an up-to-date, hilarious and romantic libretto by Tony Award nominee Douglas Carter Beane. Directed by Wayne Leonard, music direction by Annika Benander, choreography by Erin Nelson.

show.title: The Cottage
show.author: Sandy Rustin
show.description: A farcical comedy set in the English countryside in the 1920s. When a woman's yearly tryst at a charming country cottage takes an unexpected turn, one scandalous confession sets off a chain reaction of tangled affairs, long-buried secrets, and comic chaos among the assembled guests. Over one wild weekend getaway, deception unravels into delightful absurdity in this witty homage to classic drawing-room farce.
show.contentWarnings: Depicts adultery and adult relationship themes, played for comedy.

show.title: The Wizard of Oz (31st Annual Production)
show.description: Community Theatre of Greensboro's beloved annual tradition, now in its 31st year. Dorothy Gale is swept away from Kansas to the magical land of Oz, where she teams up with the Scarecrow, Tinman, and Cowardly Lion to journey down the Yellow Brick Road to the Emerald City, hoping to find her way back home while facing off against the Wicked Witch of the West.

show.title: Deadline
show.author: Don Zolidis
show.description: Eight diverse mystery writers travel to a foggy, isolated island mansion in the North Atlantic expecting a quiet retreat to write their next books. Instead of a peaceful writing session, they are forced into the 'Deadline Challenge.'

show.title: The Cake
show.author: Bekah Brunstetter
show.description: Della's carefully ordered life is turned upside down when the girl she helped raise returns home to get married — only the fiancé is actually a fiancée. Suddenly, Della is faced with a choice she's never had to make before: follow her instincts, confront her beliefs, and decide what kind of person she wants to be. Full of heart, humor, and a few sweet surprises along the way, this is a journey of self-discovery you'll experience right alongside her. Directed by Ashley Pearson.

show.title: Perfect Arrangement
show.author: Topher Payne
show.description: Set in 1950s America and inspired by the true story of the earliest stirrings of the gay rights movement, Perfect Arrangement is a hilarious, fast-paced farce with a surprisingly big heart. Two closeted U.S. State Department workers navigate love, secrecy, and absurdly complicated situations, all while trying to keep up appearances. Full of laughs, clever twists, and biting social commentary, this sharp and witty comedy reminds us how far we've come — and how much courage it still takes to live authentically. Directed by Jonathan Furr.

show.title: No Kidding
show.author: Scott Icenhower
show.description: Calvin Rogers has created a fictional daughter so that he can enter various contests through the mail. When a phone call informs him that his daughter has won the grand prize in a contest, he is overjoyed... until he learns that the publicity department is coming to photograph the lucky girl. Now, he must get his unsuspecting wife out of the house, find someone to play his daughter, and convince the suspicious contest promoters of his ruse. Presented by arrangement with Eldridge Publishing Co.

show.title: Twelve Angry Jurors
show.author: Sherman L. Sergel (adaptation, based on the 1954 teleplay by Reginald Rose)
show.description: Based on the 1954 teleplay '12 Angry Men' by Reginald Rose (later adapted into the classic 1957 courtroom drama film that marked director Sidney Lumet's feature debut), Twelve Angry Jurors tells the story of twelve jurors charged with the arduous task of deciding a young man's fate. Accused of murdering his father, the young man's life hangs in the balance as a jury of his peers battles heated tempers, deep-seated prejudices, and their own consciences to reach a verdict.
show.contentWarnings: Discusses a murder trial and themes of guilt, prejudice, and justice.

show.title: Help! I'm an Alien Stuck in the Dying Mall of America
show.author: Makayla Micheo
show.description: An original immersive dance production following an alien who crash-lands on Earth and finds themselves in a once-thriving American shopping mall that has seen better days. As the alien explores the mall and encounters its unusual inhabitants, they get a firsthand look at the strange rituals, trends, and culture of American mall life. Told entirely through dance and movement, the show takes audiences on a fun, imaginative trip through the rise, transformation, and decline of the American mall.

show.title: Hamlet, Prince of Denmark
show.author: William Shakespeare
show.description: Following the death of his father, Prince Hamlet returns home to Denmark to find his uncle Claudius has swiftly claimed the throne and married his mother, Gertrude. When the ghost of Hamlet's father reveals he was murdered by Claudius, Hamlet is drawn into a spiraling quest for revenge, questioning sanity, mortality, love, and the nature of justice along the way. One of Shakespeare's most enduring tragedies, exploring grief, betrayal, and the cost of vengeance.
show.contentWarnings: Depicts murder, suicide, and psychological distress.

show.title: Gee's Bend
show.author: Elyzabeth Gregory Wilder
show.description: The true story of a single African American family in rural Alabama in the early 20th century who created a new style of quilting all their own. Inspired by the real-life quilters of Gee's Bend, Alabama, this play weaves together history, resilience, and art in a deeply human story. It's about creativity as survival, and the bonds that hold a community together through generations. Performed in repertory with The Pitmen Painters.
show.contentWarnings: Discussions of racism, civil rights, domestic abuse, and some swearing.

show.title: The Pitmen Painters
show.author: Lee Hall
show.description: In rural England in the 1920s, a group of out-of-work coal miners unexpectedly discover a passion for painting. Since they have no preconceptions about what 'art' is, they develop a style that is truly new, challenging what art is and who gets to make it. It's funny, heartfelt, and full of underdog energy that's impossible not to root for. Performed in repertory with Gee's Bend.
show.contentWarnings: Some swearing.

show.title: The Fantasticks
show.author: Tom Jones (book & lyrics)
show.description: One of the great American musicals, The Fantasticks remains the longest-running musical in American history, running Off-Broadway non-stop from 1960 to 2015. It tells the story of two families determined to get one's daughter and the other's son together — so determined, in fact, that they build a wall to keep them apart. A charming, timeless musical about young love, illusion, and growing up, filled with wit, warmth, and unforgettable songs, opening into something surprisingly profound about what it means to really see the world (and each other).

show.author: Bradley Moss (adapted from the novel by Charles Dickens)
show.description: Center Theater Company's annual holiday tradition, now in its fourth year. Dickens' beloved tale of the miserly Ebenezer Scrooge, visited by the ghosts of Christmas Past, Present, and Yet to Come, who show him the true meaning of generosity, family, and redemption before it's too late.

show.title: Die Mommie Die!
show.author: Charles Busch
show.description: A comic melodrama evoking the 1960s 'Grande Dame Guignol' films that featured aging stars such as Bette Davis, Joan Crawford, and Lana Turner. Ex-pop singer Angela Andrews is trapped in a hateful marriage with film producer Sol Sussman. Desperate to find happiness with her younger lover, an out-of-work TV actor named Tony Parker, Angela murders her husband with the aid of a poisoned suppository. In a plot that reflects Greek tragedy as well as Hollywood kitsch, Angela's Elektra-like daughter Edith convinces Angela's son Lance that they must avenge their father's death by killing their mother. A surprising twist ending airs out all of the Sussman family's dirty laundry once and for all.
show.contentWarnings: Contains mature content; all cast members must be 18+.

show.title: Santino Fontana: A Holiday Concert
show.description: Santino Fontana brings his remarkable voice and signature charm to PlayMakers for a festive evening of holiday favorites, Broadway hits, and more. The Tony Award-winning star of Broadway's Tootsie, Disney's Frozen, and Crazy Ex-Girlfriend makes his PlayMakers debut in this special concert.

show.title: Billy Crudup: A Benefit Staged Reading
show.description: Tony Award winner Billy Crudup joins PlayMakers in an exclusive staged reading at the Paul Green Theatre. The acclaimed star of Almost Famous and The Morning Show brings his celebrated stage and screen artistry to this rare, one-night-only theatrical event. The title of the piece and full cast will be announced soon.

show.title: Treasure Island
show.author: Wayne Robert Scott (book)
show.composer: Nolan Livesay, Jason Livesay & Wayne R. Scott (music & lyrics)
show.description: Meet courageous Jim Hawkins, irrepressible Long John Silver, and a host of unforgettable characters as they engage in swashbuckling sword fights, double crosses, and mysterious secrets while searching for hidden treasure. Performed by STP's ATA/TTA/Staff.

tickets.notes: Tickets from $8.79 to $24.99. 50% off for groups of 8 or more at the Wednesday, Oct. 28 performance. Performed by STP's ATA/TTA students and staff.

show.title: Scrooge!
show.author: Wayne Robert Scott (adapted from Charles Dickens' "A Christmas Carol")
show.description: Dickens' classic A Christmas Carol comes to life in this powerful family production. Music, comedy, and the powerful redemption of Ebenezer Scrooge combine with the sights and sounds of the season for an unforgettable presentation of the true meaning of Christmas. Performed by STP's Christmas Intensive Class.

show.title: [title of show]
show.author: Hunter Bell
show.description: Ever panicked so hard about a work deadline that you accidentally created an entire Broadway musical about your panic? Hunter Bell and Jeff Bowen did. This musical follows two desperately struggling writers and two delightfully enabler-adjacent actress friends as they attempt to create a brand-new musical completely out of thin air in just 21 days. It's a backstage comedy filled with existential dread, artistic insecurity, and ridiculously catchy songs about trying to make it in show business.

show.title: The Play That Goes Wrong
show.author: Henry Lewis, Henry Shields & Jonathan Sayer
show.description: The Play That Goes Wrong proudly guarantees a 100% disaster rate. This laugh-out-loud comedy invites you to witness the opening (and quite possibly closing) night of The Murder at Haversham Manor, staged by the aggressively incompetent Cornley Polytechnic Drama Society. When everything that can go wrong does, the result is one of the funniest comedies ever to hit the stage — imagine Sherlock Holmes colliding head-on with Monty Python, and nobody surviving the crash.

show.title: Every Brilliant Thing
show.author: Duncan Macmillan (with Jonny Donahoe)
show.description: Every Brilliant Thing is a beautiful, life-affirming celebration of human connection that will leave you holding your loved ones a little tighter. What begins as a seven-year-old child's simple gift to a depressed mother — a list of everything worth living for, from ice cream to the color yellow — grows into a lifelong journey of resilience, hope, and healing. More than just a performance, Every Brilliant Thing is an interactive theatrical experience: together, as an audience, you'll help bring the story to life, sharing laughter, tears, and a heartfelt reminder that even the smallest moments can make life extraordinary.
show.contentWarnings: Explores depression and suicidal ideation within a family, handled with warmth and hope.

show.title: Ghost Light
show.author: Ira David Wood IV
show.description: Ghost Light invites you into a theatre where the stage never truly went dark. It is the summer of 2020. Outside, the world is locked down, isolated, and coming apart. Theatres across America have closed their doors — except one. Deep within an old playhouse in Raleigh, North Carolina, a different kind of door has quietly swung open: a door for the dead. Welcome to a haunting theatrical limbo where memory, performance, and the afterlife collide, as the ghosts of actors, playwrights, stagehands, and dreamers from every generation of American theatre are mysteriously drawn together. Funny, unsettling, deeply theatrical, and unexpectedly heartfelt, Ghost Light is a moving meditation on life, death, art, memory, and the enduring human desire to be seen before the lights finally go out.

show.title: The Complete Works of William Shakespeare (Abridged)
show.author: Adam Long, Daniel Singer & Jess Winfield
show.description: The cultural touchstone that is The Complete Works of William Shakespeare (Abridged) was born when three inspired, charismatic comics, having honed their pass-the-hat act at Renaissance fairs, premiered their preposterous masterwork at the Edinburgh Festival Fringe in 1987. It quickly became a worldwide phenomenon, earning the title of London's longest-running comedy after a decade at the Criterion Theatre. Featured are all 37 of Shakespeare's plays, meant to be performed in 97 minutes, by three actors. Fast-paced, witty, and physical, it's full of laughter for Shakespeare lovers and haters alike.

show.title: Irving Berlin's White Christmas
show.author: David Ives & Paul Blake (book)
show.description: Veterans Bob Wallace and Phil Davis have a successful song-and-dance act after World War II. With romance in mind, the two follow a duo of beautiful singing sisters en route to their Christmas show at a Vermont lodge, which just happens to be owned by Bob and Phil's former army commander. With a dazzling score featuring well-known standards including 'Blue Skies,' 'I Love a Piano,' 'How Deep Is the Ocean,' and the perennial title song, White Christmas is an uplifting, wholesome musical that will delight audiences of all ages.

show.title: A Streetcar Named Desire
show.author: Tennessee Williams
show.description: After losing her Mississippi home to creditors, Blanche DuBois relocates to the New Orleans home of her younger sister and brother-in-law, Stella and Stanley Kowalski. Undermined by romantic illusions, Blanche is unable to cope with life's harsh realities. Though she finds a glimmer of hope while connecting with Stanley's gentlemanly friend, Mitch, Blanche cannot face the truth of her own troubled past and ultimately descends into madness.
show.contentWarnings: Contains mature themes including sexual violence, alcoholism, and mental breakdown.

show.title: Peter and the Starcatcher
show.author: Rick Elice (based on the novel by Dave Barry & Ridley Pearson)
show.description: A young orphan and his mates are shipped off from Victorian England to a distant island ruled by the evil King Zarboff. They know nothing of the mysterious trunk in the captain's cabin, which contains a precious, otherworldly cargo. At sea, the boys are discovered by a precocious young girl named Molly, a Starcatcher-in-training who realizes that the trunk's precious cargo is starstuff, a celestial substance so powerful that it must never fall into the wrong hands. When the ship is taken over by pirates — led by the fearsome Black Stache, a villain determined to claim the trunk and its treasure for his own — the journey quickly becomes a thrilling adventure.

show.title: Junie B. Jones Jr.
show.author: Marcy Heisler (book, based on the books by Barbara Park)
show.description: Join Junie B. on her first day of first grade, where many changes are in store: Junie's best friend Lucille has found new best friends — and Junie B. makes friends with Herb, the new kid at school. While in Mr. Scary's class, Junie has trouble reading the blackboard — and she may need glasses. Add in a friendly cafeteria lady, an intense kickball tournament and a 'Top-Secret Personal Beeswax Journal,' and first grade has never been more exciting. Featuring many lovable characters and fun-filled songs, this Broadway Junior production is performed by local youth performers.

show.title: The Producers
show.author: Mel Brooks & Thomas Meehan (book)
show.description: Failed Broadway producer Max Bialystock and his mild-mannered accountant Leo Bloom hatch a wildly illegal scheme: raise way more money than needed for a guaranteed flop, then pocket the difference when it closes immediately. Their chosen vehicle — a tasteless tribute to Hitler called 'Springtime for Hitler' — backfires spectacularly when audiences find it hilarious instead of offensive. A gleefully outrageous Mel Brooks farce and multiple Tony Award winner.
show.contentWarnings: Simulated gunshots; satirical content involving Nazi imagery played for comedy.

show.title: The Importance of Being Earnest
show.author: Oscar Wilde
show.description: Two friends, Algernon Moncrieff and Jack Worthing, both invent fictitious personas to escape the constraints of Victorian social obligations. As their double lives collide with the women they're courting, mistaken identities, absurd coincidences, and razor-sharp wit combine in one of the funniest comedies ever written.
show.contentWarnings: Haze/fog effects, strobe lights, simulated gunshots.

show.title: Priscilla Queen of the Desert the Musical
show.author: Stephan Elliott & Allan Scott (book, based on the film)
show.description: Two drag queens and a transgender woman journey across the Australian Outback aboard a battered bus named Priscilla, en route to a cabaret gig in the middle of the desert. Along the way, they confront prejudice, forge unlikely friendships, and discover strength in their chosen family — all set to a high-energy jukebox score of disco and pop anthems, with outrageous costumes and glittering spectacle.
show.contentWarnings: Simulated gunshots.

show.title: Murder on the Orient Express
show.author: Ken Ludwig (adapted from the novel by Agatha Christie)
show.description: Just after midnight, a snowdrift stops the famed Orient Express in its tracks. By morning, an American tycoon lies dead in his locked compartment, stabbed eight times. Isolated in the snow with a killer among them, the passengers rely on the legendary detective Hercule Poirot to unmask the murderer before they strike again. A glamorous, thrilling adaptation of one of Agatha Christie's most beloved mysteries.

show.title: Dogfight
show.author: Peter Duchan (book, based on the Warner Bros. film)
show.description: On the eve of shipping out to Vietnam in 1963, a trio of young Marines play a cruel game: each tries to bring the ugliest date possible to a going-away party, with cash going to whoever brings the biggest 'dog.' When brash Eddie Birdlace meets Rose, an awkward and idealistic waitress, an unexpected connection sparks between them, forcing Eddie to confront his own choices as the night unfolds. A moving, bittersweet musical about love, cruelty, and redemption.
show.contentWarnings: Contains mature language, sexual content, and themes of war and cruelty.

show.title: The Rocky Horror Show
show.author: Richard O'Brien
show.description: Back by popular demand, now for two nights! Newly engaged couple Brad and Janet stumble upon the eerie mansion of Dr. Frank-N-Furter, a mad scientist unveiling his latest creation. A satirical, gleefully campy tribute to sci-fi and horror B-movies, packed with iconic rock numbers and audience participation traditions. Come up to the lab and do the Time Warp again!
show.contentWarnings: Contains sexual content, adult themes, and campy horror elements.

show.title: The Trial of Ebenezer Scrooge
show.author: Mark Brown
show.description: In this zany holiday comedy set one year after A Christmas Carol, Ebenezer Scrooge has reverted to his miserly ways and is now suing Jacob Marley and the three ghosts — of Christmas Past, Present, and Future — for various charges including breaking and entering, kidnapping, and emotional distress. Directed by Peg Tribert.

show.title: Carrie: The Musical
show.author: Lawrence D. Cohen (book, based on the novel by Stephen King)
show.description: At school, Carrie White is a teenage outcast bullied by the popular crowd. At home, she's dominated by her loving but cruelly controlling mother. But Carrie's just discovered she's got a special power, and if pushed too far, she's not afraid to use it. Directed by James Crider.
show.contentWarnings: Depicts bullying, abuse, and violence.

show.title: Death By Golf
show.author: Gregg Kreutz
show.description: When an escaped convict, an anxious bride, a scheming new husband, and a suspicious attorney all convene at Grandpa's house, it doesn't take long for Grandpa to realize he has to reschedule his golf game. Directed by Thurmond Whatley.

show.title: Sweeney Todd: The Demon Barber of Fleet Street
show.author: Hugh Wheeler (book, adapted by Christopher Bond)
show.description: This dark musical tells the story of Benjamin Barker, who returns to London after 15 years of wrongful exile. Now known as Sweeney Todd, he seeks revenge against Judge Turpin, the man who destroyed his life by falsely imprisoning him and assaulting his wife. Directed by James Raby.
show.contentWarnings: Depicts murder, violence, and dark psychological themes.

show.title: Native Gardens
show.author: Karen Zacarías
show.description: Gardens and cultures clash, turning friendly neighboring couples — Pablo and Tania, and Frank and Virginia — into feuding enemies in this hilarious comedy about good intentions and bad manners. Directed by Wendy Dietzel.

show.title: Jeeves at Sea
show.author: Margaret Raether (adapted from the stories of P.G. Wodehouse)
show.description: Life aboard the Vanderley yacht is everything Bertie Wooster could hope for... right up until his pal Crumpet assaults a prince. What follows is a swift descent into chaos: Bertie masquerading as a romance novelist, Crumpet posing as his own long-lost twin, and a sinister foreign count issuing a formal challenge to a duel. Meanwhile, Lady Stella has ideas about Bertie's future that he finds deeply alarming. Will this madcap case of mistaken identities end in Bertie's doom — or worse, his marriage? Have no fear; Jeeves will sort it all out. Part of NC Stage's beloved annual Jeeves tradition.

show.title: Primary Trust
show.author: Eboni Booth
show.description: Kenneth has his routine, and his routine suits him just fine. Bookstore by day, mai-tais at his favorite tiki bar by night — what more could a person need? When Kenneth is unexpectedly laid off, the walls of the life he's carefully constructed start to close in, and he's forced to reckon with everything he's been quietly avoiding: connection, vulnerability, and the terrifying possibility of something new. Winner of the 2024 Pulitzer Prize for Drama, funny, precise, and quietly devastating.

show.title: Mike Wiley presents "Changing Same"
show.author: Mike Wiley & Howard L. Craft
show.description: On July 8, 1944, Private Booker T. Spicely boarded a bus in downtown Durham but never made it back to camp. The Black soldier, newly stationed at a nearby Army base and unfamiliar with the South's Jim Crow laws, was shot twice in the chest by the bus driver after a dispute over his seat. The driver reboarded the bus and continued his route; an all-White jury later acquitted him in 28 minutes. Award-winning playwright and performer Mike Wiley brings Spicely, the driver, and a chorus of witnesses back to life in this searing solo show, excavating a story that faded from public memory. Co-presented by NC Stage and the YMI Cultural Center. Performed at the YMI Cultural Center, 39 S. Market St, Downtown Asheville.
show.contentWarnings: Depicts historical racial violence and injustice.

show.title: Jacob Marley's Christmas Carol
show.author: Tom Mula
show.description: Jacob Marley is dead — and things are about to get worse. Shackled, miserable, and tormented by a hell-sprite who is far too enthusiastic about his work, Marley faces an eternity of exactly what he deserves. Unless, of course, he can do something about Ebenezer Scrooge. In this re-imagining of the classic Christmas Carol story, the ghost gets his own journey — and it turns out redemption is just as hard to come by on the other side of the grave as it is on this one.

show.title: R. Buckminster Fuller: The History (and Mystery) of the Universe
show.author: D.W. Jacobs (from the life, work, and writings of R.B. Fuller)
show.description: Expelled from Harvard twice, trained as a naval engineer, after many personal, family and business crises, R. Buckminster Fuller learned that his life belonged to the Universe and humanity. What followed were the explorations of one of the most restlessly inventive minds of the twentieth century. In this one-man tour de force, we encounter the life and mind of Fuller — futurist, philosopher, poet, architect of the geodesic dome — to see how we already have everything we need to save the planet, if we just 'think different' about how we are Operating Spaceship Earth.

show.title: Misery
show.author: William Goldman (adapted from the novel by Stephen King)
show.description: Paul Sheldon has survived the crash — but he's not sure that's a good thing. Rescued from a Colorado snowbank by his self-proclaimed number one fan, the bestselling romance novelist finds himself bedridden and dependent on Annie Wilkes, a devoted reader who offers to nurse Paul back to health. When Annie discovers that Paul has killed off her favorite character in his latest manuscript, his situation goes from dire to something much worse. A white-knuckle battle of wills between a captive and his captor, and a darkly funny question about what we owe the people who love our work.
show.contentWarnings: Contains violence and psychological intensity.

show.title: Menopause The Musical (25th Anniversary Tour)
show.author: Jeanie Linders
show.description: Join the party celebrating two decades of laughter and sisterhood! Four women at a lingerie sale have nothing in common but a black lace bra AND memory loss, hot flashes, night sweats, not enough sex, too much sex, and more. This hilarious musical parody set to classic tunes from the '60s, '70s and '80s will have you cheering and dancing in the aisles. Seen by more than 17 million women and fans worldwide over 25 years.
show.contentWarnings: Adult humor about menopause and sexuality.

show.title: The Unauthorized Hallmark(ish) Parody Musical
show.author: Tim Drucker, Joel Waggoner & Bonnie Milligan
show.description: The musical comedy that celebrates your favorite holiday movies. Holly, an overworked city executive, is forced to return to her quirky hometown to help her mother run the family business. She reunites with Mark, an old flame who is now the local Sheriff, and discovers the town's long-running cookie contest cheating conspiracy involves a moose on the loose. As Holly juggles romance, small-town drama, and a looming corporate merger, she learns that love and community might matter more than work. Packed with immersive holiday moments and original pop songs.

show.title: E(a)rnest
show.author: Adapted by Emily Emerson from the play by Oscar Wilde
show.description: A modern-day reimagining of Oscar Wilde's classic, in which two men juggling double identities and a tangle of romantic complications collide with high society and low honesty. Wilde's legendary wit gets a contemporary spin, delivering nonstop clever lies and outrageous misunderstandings that ultimately argue the truth is overrated and being earnest is entirely optional.

show.title: Come From Away
show.author: Book and Lyrics by Irene Sankoff and David Hein
show.composer: Music by Irene Sankoff and David Hein
show.description: In the days after September 11, the small town of Gander, Newfoundland opened its doors to thousands of stranded travelers, turning fear into community and strangers into friends. This uplifting true-events musical celebrates kindness, resilience, and human connection, leaving audiences inspired and hopeful about what people can accomplish when they come together.

show.title: The Happy Holidays Collection
show.description: A holiday-themed production for ages 6-11.

show.title: Disney's The Little Mermaid Kids
show.author: Doug Wright (book)
show.composer: Alan Menken (music); Howard Ashman & Glenn Slater (lyrics)
show.description: A young-performer adaptation of Disney's The Little Mermaid, following Ariel, a mermaid princess who dreams of life on land and makes a fateful bargain with the sea witch Ursula to become human. An HART Academy production.

show.title: Les Misérables
show.author: Alain Boublil & Claude-Michel Schönberg (book, based on the novel by Victor Hugo)
show.description: An undisputed masterpiece of musical theatre, following the life of ex-convict Jean Valjean as he is ruthlessly pursued by Inspector Javert against the backdrop of the French Revolution.

show.title: White Christmas
show.author: David Ives & Paul Blake (book)
show.description: Veterans Bob Wallace and Phil Davis have a successful song-and-dance act after World War II. With romance in mind, the two follow a duo of beautiful singing sisters en route to their Christmas show at a Vermont lodge, which just happens to be owned by Bob and Phil's former army commander.

show.title: Six: Teen Edition
show.author: Toby Marlow & Lucy Moss
show.description: The six wives of Henry VIII take the mic to reclaim their own stories in this pop-concert-style musical, remixing history into a fierce celebration of female empowerment. A teen-performer edition of the hit West End/Broadway musical. An HART Academy production.

show.title: A View From the Bridge
show.author: Arthur Miller
show.description: Arthur Miller's classic American tragedy follows Eddie Carbone, a Brooklyn longshoreman whose obsessive love for his orphaned niece Catherine sets off a devastating chain of jealousy, betrayal, and violence when two undocumented Italian relatives come to stay with his family.

show.title: The Addams Family Musical
show.author: Marshall Brickman & Rick Elice (book, based on characters created by Charles Addams)
show.description: Wednesday Addams, the ultimate princess of darkness, has grown up and fallen in love with Lucas, a sweet, smart young man from a respectable family her parents have never met. Wednesday confides in her father Gomez and begs him not to tell her mother Morticia — forcing Gomez to keep a secret from his beloved wife for the first time ever.

show.title: Shrek the Musical
show.author: David Lindsay-Abaire (book & lyrics)
show.description: Once upon a time, there was a little ogre named Shrek who lived alone in a swamp. Everything changes when his swamp is overrun by fairytale misfits, sending Shrek on a quest with a wisecracking Donkey to rescue Princess Fiona from a fire-breathing, love-sick dragon. A hilarious, heartwarming musical about accepting yourself, love at first sight, and the many roads to happily ever after.

show.title: The Cottage
show.author: Sandy Rustin
show.description: A farcical comedy set in the English countryside in the 1920s. When a woman's yearly tryst at a charming country cottage takes an unexpected turn, one scandalous confession sets off a chain reaction of tangled affairs, long-buried secrets, and comic chaos among the assembled guests.
show.contentWarnings: Depicts adultery and adult relationship themes, played for comedy.

show.title: Angel Street
show.author: Patrick Hamilton
show.description: First produced under the title Gaslight, this classic thriller follows the Manninghams: the suavely handsome Mr. Manningham slowly drives his gentle, devoted wife to the brink of insanity with an insinuating kindness that masks far more sinister motives — the original source of the term 'gaslighting.'
show.contentWarnings: Depicts psychological manipulation and abuse.

show.title: The Game
show.author: Bekah Brunstetter
show.description: A play by Bekah Brunstetter, whose work often blends warmth, humor, and sharp emotional insight into stories about family and connection.

show.title: 9 to 5 Jr.
show.author: Patricia Resnick (book)
show.description: A junior-scale adaptation of the hit musical based on the 1980 film. Three overworked coworkers take charge of their sexist boss's office after an unexpected opportunity turns their daydreams of revenge into reality. An HART Academy production.

show.title: Finding Neverland
show.author: James Graham (book)
show.description: An inspiring, imaginative musical about playwright J.M. Barrie and the family who helped spark the creation of Peter Pan. As Barrie rediscovers play, possibility, and hope, audiences are swept into a world where dreams take flight. With soaring music and theatrical magic, it is a heartfelt story about family, healing, and the power of believing.

show.title: Elf Jr.
show.author: Thomas Meehan & Bob Martin (book, based on the New Line Cinema film written by David Berenbaum)
show.description: Buddy, a young orphan, mistakenly crawls into Santa's bag of gifts and is transported to the North Pole. The would-be elf is raised, unaware that he is actually a human, until his enormous size and poor toy-making abilities cause him to face the truth. With Santa's permission, Buddy embarks on a journey to New York City to find his birth father and discover his true identity, in this junior version adaptation of the beloved holiday musical.

show.title: Driving Miss Daisy
show.author: Alfred Uhry
show.description: Spanning 25 years, this Pulitzer Prize-winning play follows the evolving relationship between Daisy Werthan, a strong-willed elderly Jewish widow in Atlanta, and Hoke Coleburn, the Black chauffeur hired by her son to drive her after she's deemed unfit to drive herself. What begins as reluctant tolerance grows into a deep, tender friendship that transcends barriers of race, class, and age.
show.contentWarnings: Addresses racial prejudice in the mid-20th century American South.

show.title: Les Misérables
show.author: Alain Boublil & Claude-Michel Schönberg (book, based on the novel by Victor Hugo)
show.description: An undisputed masterpiece of musical theatre, following the life of ex-convict Jean Valjean as he is ruthlessly pursued by Inspector Javert against the backdrop of the French Revolution. Winner of the Tony Award for Best Musical and Best Original Score.

show.title: Speakeasy
show.description: It's 1978. The fight is on. The plates are hot. And Virginia needs every dollar she can get. Facing the loss of her childhood home, she turns one big fight night into a business opportunity. But when the doors open, so does a world of unexpected trouble.

show.title: Short & Sweet One Act Festival
show.author: Various
show.description: Cherryville Little Theatre's annual festival showcasing a collection of short one-act plays. Free admission.

show.title: Frankenstein & Dracula
show.description: A double-feature Halloween-season event: two classic horror tales, Frankenstein and Dracula, presented as two shows in one night.

show.title: Riveted
show.description: A musical drama depicting the impact of the cultural, political and social conflicts that bore down on one white, American family through the post-WWII, Vietnam and contemporary eras.
show.contentWarnings: Explores wartime trauma and social/political conflict across three American eras.

linkedVenueId.name: Duke Energy Theatre (Spirit Square Center for the Arts & Education)

show.title: Mariposa/Butterfly
show.author: Sandra Fenichel Asher & José Casas
show.description: In a small Texas town, two neighbors are quite different. One grows flowers, the other grows veggies. One speaks English, the other Spanish. They can't even agree on the weather! But when a tiny caterpillar appears on the fence, everything changes. A grumpy disagreement turns into shared wonder as their little friend transforms into a mariposa/butterfly and continues its northern migration from Mexico. A gentle, heartwarming bilingual first adventure for the littlest ones — a reminder that the beautiful world we share is big enough for all of us. Features puppetry beautifully executed to help the story unfold.

show.title: Avenue Q
show.author: Jeff Whitty (book)
show.description: A hilarious, irreverent Tony Award-winning musical following Princeton, a recent college grad who moves to a rundown New York neighborhood populated by an eclectic mix of human and puppet neighbors. Together they navigate finding a job, falling in love, and figuring out their purpose in life, all set to a score filled with catchy songs tackling grown-up themes with playful, puppet-filled humor.
show.contentWarnings: Contains adult language, sexual content/puppet nudity, and mature themes; not appropriate for young children.

show.title: Million Dollar Quartet
show.author: Colin Escott & Floyd Mutrux
show.composer: Various (Elvis Presley, Johnny Cash, Jerry Lee Lewis & Carl Perkins catalog)
show.description: On December 4, 1956, four rock 'n' roll legends — Elvis Presley, Johnny Cash, Jerry Lee Lewis, and Carl Perkins — came together for one unforgettable, unplanned jam session at Sun Records in Memphis. This Tony Award-winning musical recreates that legendary night, packed with early rock, gospel, R&B, and country classics performed live on stage.

linkedVenueId.name: Historic Main Stage at Thalian Hall

show.title: The Full Monty
show.author: Terrence McNally (book, based on the film)
show.description: Based on the hit film of the same name, The Full Monty follows the fortunes of six unemployed steelworkers in Buffalo, New York. With no job, money or prospects, they are fed up. When the men spy their wives and other local women going crazy over a group of male strippers, an idea begins to emerge. Overcoming their jealousy and feelings of emasculation, they decide to make some quick cash by forming their own act — a team of male strippers with 'real man' bodies. However, their rehearsals are not easy. As they prepare for the performance of their lives, they are tested and exposed, both physically and emotionally. Overcoming their fears, self-consciousness, and inner demons, the men realize that they are strong together and find solace in their friendship.
show.contentWarnings: Contains adult language, sexual humor, and nudity implied at the show's climax.

linkedVenueId.name: Historic Main Stage at Thalian Hall

show.title: Little Women
show.author: Allan Knee (book)
show.description: Louisa May Alcott's beloved story of the adventures of the four March sisters is brought to vivid musical life in Little Women. The Civil War is in full swing, and the March sisters — Meg, the oldest, a romantic; the spirited and tomboyish Jo; sweet and loving Beth; and irascible, playful Amy — live in Concord, Massachusetts with their Marmee while their father is on the battlefield. Filled with adventure, heartbreak, and a deep sense of hope, the struggle of these 'Little Women' to find their own voices mirrors the growing pains of a young America.

linkedVenueId.name: Historic Main Stage at Thalian Hall

show.title: Priscilla, Queen of the Desert
show.author: Stephan Elliott & Allan Scott (book, based on the film)
show.description: Priscilla, Queen of the Desert tells the story of Tick, a talented drag queen, who decides to meet his young son for the first time. After enlisting the help of his friends Felicia and Bernadette, they set off on an adventure aboard a bus they've named Priscilla. As the trio travels through the Outback, they encounter a variety of characters and unexpected challenges. A celebration of self-expression, diversity, and the power of authenticity, filled with hits from the 70s and 80s and unforgettable show-girl-style costume design.

linkedVenueId.name: Historic Main Stage at Thalian Hall

show.title: Les Misérables
show.author: Alain Boublil & Claude-Michel Schönberg (book, based on the novel by Victor Hugo)
show.description: One of the world's most iconic and longest-running musicals, Les Misérables tells the story of Jean Valjean, a former convict who spends a lifetime seeking redemption. Set against the backdrop of 19th-century France and the aftermath of the French Revolution, this timeless story of intertwined destinies reveals the power of compassion and the quiet evil of indifference to human suffering. As Valjean's quest for a new life carries him into Paris and to the barricades of the Student Revolution, he is hunted by Inspector Javert and the ghosts of his past.

linkedVenueId.name: Historic Main Stage at Thalian Hall

show.title: The 25th Annual Putnam County Spelling Bee
show.author: Rachel Sheinkin (book)
show.description: An eclectic group of six kids (played by adults) vie for the spelling championship of a lifetime. While candidly disclosing hilarious and touching stories from their home lives, the tweens spell their way through a series of potentially made-up words, hoping never to hear the soul-crushing 'ding' of the bell that signals a spelling mistake. Six spellers enter; one speller leaves a champion — at least the losers get a juice box.

show.title: Legally Blonde Jr
show.author: Heather Hach (book)
show.description: Our talented young performers bring Elle Woods' empowering story to life in this high-energy, heartwarming musical adventure. A celebration of confidence, friendship, and discovering your own strength.

show.title: Once on This Island
show.author: Lynn Ahrens (book & lyrics, based on the novel "My Love, My Love" by Rosa Guy)
show.description: A breathtaking Caribbean-inspired musical filled with passion, storytelling, and powerful music. This moving tale of love, destiny, and hope will carry you to another world.

show.title: Lewis N Clark: A Family Christmas
show.description: Celebrate the season with Lewis N Clark in a warm, joy-filled Christmas show featuring beloved holiday songs, heartfelt stories, family traditions, and plenty of Christmas cheer.

show.title: Ma Rainey's Black Bottom
show.author: August Wilson
show.description: Part of August Wilson's celebrated Century Cycle, this powerful drama is set in a Chicago recording studio in 1927, where tensions boil over between the legendary blues singer Ma Rainey and her ambitious young band during a single, sweltering recording session, exploring race, art, and the exploitation of Black musicians in the music industry.
show.contentWarnings: Discusses racism and exploitation.

show.title: A Chorus Line
show.author: James Kirkwood & Nicholas Dante (book)
show.description: A concept musical capturing the spirit and tension of a Broadway ensemble audition, exploring the inner lives and bittersweet ambitions of professional Broadway dancers.

show.title: Heathers: The Musical
show.author: Kevin Murphy & Laurence O'Keefe
show.description: A dark comedy rock musical based on the 1988 cult classic film, following Veronica Sawyer as she navigates the vicious social hierarchy of Westerberg High School and her toxic relationship with a mysterious new student, J.D.
show.contentWarnings: Contains depictions of teen suicide, violence, and adult language.

show.title: The Moors
show.author: Jen Silverman
show.description: A dark comedy set on the bleak, isolated moors of Victorian England, following two sisters, their dog, a mastiff, and a governess whose arrival sets off a strange and darkly funny chain of events, blending gothic literary tropes with absurdist humor.

show.title: Alice In Wonderland JR
show.description: A junior-scale adaptation of Lewis Carroll's classic tale, following young Alice as she tumbles down the rabbit hole into a whimsical, topsy-turvy world of eccentric characters, presented by our young performers.

show.title: Hadestown: Teen Edition
show.author: Anaïs Mitchell (book, music & lyrics)
show.description: A teen-performer edition of the Tony Award-winning folk-opera retelling the Greek myths of Orpheus and Eurydice, and Hades and Persephone, blending mythology with a smoky, blues-and-jazz-infused score.

show.title: Brigadoon
show.author: Alan Jay Lerner (book & lyrics)
show.description: Two American tourists stumble upon a mysterious Scottish village that appears out of the mist only once every hundred years. As one of them falls in love with a local woman, he must decide whether to stay in this magical, timeless place forever.

show.title: It's a Wonderful Life: A Live Radio Play
show.author: Joe Landry (adapted from the film)
show.description: It's Christmas Eve, 1946, and the cast and crew of radio station WBFR are bringing you a live broadcast of the most beloved holiday story ever told. When a massive snowstorm keeps most of the cast from making it in, a handful of actors and crew members must step up and save the show, voicing dozens of characters live on air with nothing but microphones, sound effects, and pure theatrical magic.

show.title: Les Misérables
show.author: Alain Boublil & Claude-Michel Schönberg (based on the novel by Victor Hugo)
show.description: Among the most celebrated and longest-running musicals ever staged, Les Misérables follows Jean Valjean, a former prisoner who devotes his life to earning redemption. Set in 19th-century France in the years after the French Revolution, the story weaves together many lives and shows both the power of compassion and the quiet cruelty of ignoring human suffering. Valjean's search for a fresh start takes him to Paris and ultimately to the barricades of the student uprising, all while Inspector Javert and the shadows of his past pursue him. In the struggle for the soul of the city, he finds what love and salvation truly mean. Staged in more than 40 countries and 22 languages, the musical brings Victor Hugo's sweeping novel to vivid life through a rich, soaring score that includes "I Dreamed a Dream," "On My Own," and "Bring Him Home." Theatre of the Republic presents it as the opening production of its 2027 season.

tickets.notes: A concert version will also be performed Saturday, Feb 27 at 7:30 PM and Sunday, Feb 28 at 3:00 PM at the Greg Rowles Legacy Theatre.

show.title: Rodgers & Hammerstein's Cinderella: Youth Edition
show.author: Oscar Hammerstein II
show.description: Florence Little Theatre's Rising Stars program presents Rodgers & Hammerstein's Cinderella: Youth Edition. Rising Stars is FLT's theatre arts program for students in grades 7 through 12 who want to grow their stage skills in a safe, professional setting, building abilities such as teamwork, public speaking, and creative problem-solving along the way. Students audition for the show the program director selects and rehearse their roles weekly, and the semester culminates in public performances on the Florence Little Theatre main stage, backed by FLT staff and volunteers with professional-quality lighting, sound, costumes, and makeup. Directed by Education Director Lisa Sims.

show.title: Meet Me in St. Louis
show.author: Hugh Wheeler (based on the MGM film and the stories by Sally Benson)
show.description: The Marlboro Players bring Meet Me in St. Louis to the Marlboro Civic Center stage. The musical follows the Smith family of St. Louis in the year leading up to the 1904 World's Fair, including oldest sister Rose and John Truitt, the shy boy next door who becomes her love interest.

tickets.notes: Child price is for ages 12 and under. Tickets go on sale October 19.

show.title: The Lightning Thief: The Percy Jackson Musical
show.author: Joe Tracz (book), adapted from the novel by Rick Riordan
show.description: Percy Jackson has just learned he is the half-blood son of a Greek god, which leaves him with powers he can't control, a destiny he never asked for, and a whole mythology textbook's worth of monsters chasing him. When Zeus's master lightning bolt goes missing and Percy is blamed, he must track it down and return it to clear his name and stop a war among the gods. Succeeding means more than catching a thief: Percy has to journey to the Underworld and back, unravel the Oracle's riddle warning that a friend will betray him, and make peace with the father who left him. Adapted from Rick Riordan's best-selling novel and driven by an electrifying original rock score, this action-packed mythological adventure has been called "worthy of the gods" by Time Out New York. This ACT Youth Production is an immersive performance workshop built for young artists who want to learn and grow in the performing arts, giving students a hands-on tour of the entire theatrical process that culminates in public performances.
show.runtime: About 2 hours 15 minutes, including one 15-minute intermission
show.contentWarnings: May contain loud noises and flashing lights.

show.title: The Secret of Everwinter
show.author: Eli Cunningham
show.description: Something is shifting in Everwinter Forest. As old tales come back to life and long-buried mysteries begin to stir, a band of friends sets out from home looking for answers. Along the way they encounter breathtaking marvels, surprising allies, and a secret tucked away in the heart of the forest. This enchanting new original musical by Eli Cunningham weaves together ancient legends, unlikely friendships, and one remarkable adventure to reveal the true secret of Everwinter. This ACT Youth Production is an immersive performance workshop built for young artists who want to learn and grow in the performing arts, giving students a hands-on tour of the entire theatrical process that culminates in public performances.

show.title: How to Train Your Dragon Jr
show.author: Kate Thomas (book & lyrics), based on the DreamWorks Animation motion picture
show.description: Hiccup is a young Viking who breaks with tradition by befriending one of his people's deadliest enemies, a fierce dragon he names Toothless. Together the two unlikely heroes battle against the odds to save both of their worlds in this delightful stage adaptation of the DreamWorks Animation film. This ACT Youth Production is an immersive performance workshop built for young artists who want to learn and grow in the performing arts, giving students a hands-on tour of the entire theatrical process that culminates in public performances.

show.title: Trolls Jr.
show.author: Krista Knight (book & additional lyrics), based on the DreamWorks Animation motion picture
show.description: Drawn from the irreverent DreamWorks Animation movie franchise, Trolls JR. takes place in a bright, wondrous world filled with hilariously memorable characters. It follows the relentlessly cheerful Trolls, who always have a song ready, and the comically gloomy Bergens, who only feel happy with a Troll in their stomach. The Troll performers in Poppy's company swear by one motto: the show must go on. But when a tyrannical foreign emissary turns up in Bergenland, the stakes rise, and the Trolls must completely rework their show or risk being served up in the name of diplomacy by a rehired Chef bent on revenge. This ACT Youth Production is an immersive performance workshop built for young artists who want to learn and grow in the performing arts, giving students a hands-on tour of the entire theatrical process that culminates in public performances.

show.title: A Year with Frog & Toad Kids
show.author: Willie Reale (book & lyrics), based on the books by Arnold Lobel
show.description: Adapted from the three-time Tony-nominated Broadway hit and based on Arnold Lobel's beloved books, A Year with Frog and Toad KIDS features a jazzy, upbeat score overflowing with melody. Part vaudeville, part make-believe and entirely charming, it tells the story of a friendship that lasts through every season. After waking from hibernation, Frog and Toad plant gardens, go swimming, rake leaves and go sledding, picking up life lessons along the way, and over the course of the year the two best friends celebrate the differences that make each of them special. It is part of ACT's Studio Series, a hands-on performance workshop in which students ages 5 to 11 learn to prepare for and present themselves at auditions, work together with their castmates through rehearsals, and stage a lively, colorful performance in ACT's 35below.

show.title: Wee Sing Together
show.author: Based on the 1985 film from Wee Sing Productions
show.description: It's Sally's birthday, and her stuffed animals are whisking her away to Wee Sing Park, a magical place you enter with a song, where presents spring to life and everyone learns that the more we sing together, the happier we will be. Based on the 1985 film from Wee Sing Productions. It is part of ACT's Studio Series, a hands-on performance workshop in which students ages 5 to 11 learn to prepare for and present themselves at auditions, work together with their castmates through rehearsals, and stage a lively, colorful performance in ACT's 35below.

show.title: Improv Tonight: Bowl Cut Barbie, Dirt Bike Territory, Frisky Twisters
show.description: Improv Tonight! is ACT's fast, funny and entirely unscripted monthly comedy show, featuring a different lineup of improv teams each Friday and Saturday night. On this night, three teams perform at both the 8:00 PM and 10:00 PM shows, and no two shows are ever alike. Dirt Bike Territory, a long-form house team from Misfit Improv & Acting School, performs the Armando, mixing personal stories, big characters and fully improvised scenes with no script and no plan. Bowl Cut Barbie, an all-female long-form team from Asheville that met at Misfit Improv and Acting School, brings mischief, charm and sharp character work in Close Quarters, a narrative format that plays out entirely in a single location. Frisky Twisters, a group of classmates who banded together out of a hunger to keep playing, builds a fully improvised tale from the audience's suggestion and their own discussion in an improvised living room, spinning a story that will never be seen again. Improv Tonight! is part of ACT Late Night, ACT's space for exploring something a little different.

show.title: Improv Tonight: Improv Sports
show.description: Improv Tonight! is ACT's fast, funny and entirely unscripted monthly comedy show, featuring different improv teams every Friday and Saturday night, with each team performing at both 8:00 PM and 10:00 PM. This edition is Improv Sports, hosted by Chris Martin. At 8:00 PM, Waynesville's Parking Space takes on Asheville's Naughty Bottom Girls, and the winner faces Gag Me! at 10:00 PM. Parking Space, Waynesville's premier improv troupe founded in June 2025, turns audience suggestions into high-energy short-form games, with one brave host trying to keep order while a rotating cast of quick-witted improvisers happily ignores them. The Naughty Bottom Girls are a fun, over-the-top troupe known for big characters and silly but sincere relationships, and Gag Me! is an off-the-wall Asheville quartet made up of three members of the Misfit short-form team and one long-form player who insists he can shorten it down. show.title: My Favorite Christmas
show.author: Candice Dickinson (director) with members of the HART family
show.description: Returning by popular demand after its beloved 2023 debut, but completely reimagined, My Favorite Christmas is a one-of-a-kind holiday celebration that could only come from this community. Directed by Candice Dickinson in collaboration with members of the HART family, the original production blends brand-new personal stories, striking vocal performances and joyful dance into an evening centered on a warm, glowing fireplace. The show exists to celebrate the region's extraordinary talent and extraordinary people, because nothing captures the magic of Christmas quite like gathering together to share the memories that matter most.

tickets.notes: Recommended for the whole family.

show.title: Twelfth Night
show.author: William Shakespeare
show.description: Separated from her twin brother by a shipwreck, Viola disguises herself as a young man and enters the service of Duke Orsino. What follows is a joyful knot of mistaken identities, hidden affection, practical jokes and unrequited love. One of Shakespeare's most cherished comedies, Twelfth Night celebrates transformation, mischief and the delightfully unpredictable nature of love. Performed in repertory with The Humorous Adventures of Sir Andrew Auguecheek. Part of Montford Park Players' 2027 season, The Bond of Fate, performed free outdoors.

Andy is determined to test the limits of both on a globe-trotting quest to bring his humours into balance. Meanwhile, Vivian is starting to set aside her childhood fantasies of gallant heroes and get down to the business of advancing knowledge in the world. Romance is tested, Hell is maligned and Cuisine is praised in this curious contradiction of a master's education and a fool's journey. Performed in repertory with Twelfth Night. Part of Montford Park Players' 2027 season, The Bond of Fate, performed free outdoors.

But rumors, deception and misread intentions threaten to undo both romances. Packed with humor, intrigue and unforgettable characters, this lively comedy proves that love rarely goes according to plan. show.description: In the wake of a devastating civil war, Antigone defies King Creon's orders in order to honor her fallen brother. Her act of defiance ignites a powerful clash between personal conscience and the laws of the state. show.title: Improv Tonight: King Baby, Second Pancake, Not Dead Yet
show.description:
Improv Tonight! is ACT's fast, funny and entirely unscripted monthly comedy show, featuring a different lineup of improv teams each Friday and Saturday night. On this night we will feature King Baby, Second Pancake, and Not Dead Yet.

That first pancake? Just practice. The second? That’s the good stuff. Second Pancake is a long-form improv troupe of six clever and quick Asheville improvisers who aim to make every single show as perfect as that next flapjack off the griddle. Formerly Mostly Millennials during their time as a Misfit Improv house troupe, they’re now independent and ready to flip. Get your spatulas ready.

What’s to be done with the limited time we have left on this Earth? For some, it’s making world-changing scientific breakthroughs. For others, it’s composing great and enduring works of cultural significance. For some, it’s making AI or whatever. But for a select few, it’s probably goofin’ around and doing improv. Not Dead Yet is a long-form Misfit Improv house troupe made up of eight Asheville-area improvisers. While they’re here, they’re going to make each other, and hopefully you, laugh while they can.

show.title: The White One by the Bay (Staged Reading)
show.author: Susan Gross
show.description: Burning Coal's Coal Mines program, which develops new plays by writers with ties to North Carolina, presents a free staged reading of The White One by the Bay by Triangle playwright Susan Gross, directed by Abbe Fralix. Best friends Mira and Tristan were torn apart by tragic circumstances ten years ago. Now they are suddenly handed an impossible opportunity to finally say everything they left unsaid. With help from Tristan's teenage daughter, Aurora, the two move along the line between memory and reality, hoping to find peace and understanding on the other side.
show.contentWarnings: Mature themes, including grief and suicide.

tickets.notes: Free and open to the public; no reservations required.

show.title: Beetlejuice JR.
show.author: Scott Brown & Anthony King (book)
show.description: Carolina Children's Theatre - Youth Arts Academy presents a Halloween special production of Beetlejuice JR., the frightfully funny musical adapted from the beloved film that became a Broadway hit. Lydia Deetz is a strange and unusual teenager who is still mourning her mother and is preoccupied with the whole idea of being dead. Luckily for her, the new house she and her father move into is haunted by a recently deceased couple and by Beetlejuice, a delightful demon with a real zest for life. When Lydia calls on Beetlejuice to frighten away anyone with a pulse, the double-crossing ghost reveals his true colors and unleashes pandemonium from the Netherworld. The show features music and lyrics by Tony Award nominee Eddie Perfect and a book by Tony-nominated writers Anthony King and Scott Brown. The Broadway production earned eight 2019 Tony nominations, including Best New Musical, and became a social media sensation that connected with young theatre fans through its unapologetic humor and emotional honesty. Created for the generation that made it a hit, Beetlejuice JR. is a wacky theatrical party for everyone. Two performances only.

show.title: Frozen KIDS
show.author: Jennifer Lee (book, based on the Disney film)
show.description: Center Theater Conservatory's youngest performers, the Early Entertainers, present Frozen KIDS in five rotating casts at Center Theater in Carrboro. Set in the Kingdom of Arendelle, the story follows Anna as she sets out on a long, icy journey to bring home her sister Elsa, the ice queen whose hidden powers have plunged the kingdom into endless winter. Along the way audiences meet a colorful set of characters, including rock trolls, a reindeer, and a singing snowman, in a tale about the strength of sibling love and being proud of who you are.

tickets.notes: Tickets $15-$20 on Ludus.

show.title: A Christmas Story
show.author: Philip Grecian (based on the 1983 motion picture written by Jean Shepherd, Leigh Brown and Bob Clark, and on Jean Shepherd's book "In God We Trust, All Others Pay Cash")
show.description: Neuse Little Theatre brings A Christmas Story to The Hut for the holidays. Drawn from humorist Jean Shepherd's memories of a 1940s Midwestern childhood, the play follows nine-year-old Ralphie Parker and his campaign to find an official Red Ryder BB gun under the tree on Christmas morning. Ralphie argues his case to his mother, his teacher, and even Santa Claus at Higbee's Department Store, and every one of them gives the same answer: "You'll shoot your eye out!" Every favorite moment from the classic film makes it to the stage: the family's cranky, explosive furnace; Scut Farkas, the neighborhood bully; the boys' wet-tongue-on-a-frozen-lamppost dare; the Little Orphan Annie secret decoder pin; the Old Man's prize lamp shaped like a woman's leg in a fishnet stocking; Ralphie's elaborate daydreams; and more. It is the kind of show that is made to become a holiday tradition.

show.title: The Cemetery Club
show.author: Ivan Menchell
show.description: Ivan Menchell's comedy follows three Jewish widows who get together every month for tea before heading out to visit their late husbands' graves. Their routine, and their loyalty to one another, is shaken when a widower named Sam opens the door to new possibilities. Ida is ready for a fresh start, Lucille is hungry for fun and attention, and Doris holds tight to tradition. When Sam takes an interest in Ida, the group's balance starts to wobble, and each woman is pushed to face what it means to love, to let go, and to truly live again. The play mixes humor with tenderness as the friends work through grief, friendship, and the fear of moving on.

show.title: And Then There Were None
show.author: Agatha Christie
show.description: In Agatha Christie's classic mystery, ten strangers are drawn to an isolated island and accused of crimes from their pasts. The only thing they share is a guilty history none of them wants to confess, and a secret that will decide their fate. One by one the guests begin to die, each death mirroring a line of the eerie nursery rhyme "Ten Little Soldier Boys." As fear and suspicion grow, the survivors realize the killer has to be one of them and that no one can be trusted. Guilt, justice, and paranoia collide in a tightly built thriller that leaves characters and audience alike wondering who, if anyone, will make it out alive.

show.author: Adam Long, Daniel Singer & Jess Winfield (new revisions by Daniel Singer & Jess Winfield)
show.description: This fast, irreverent comedy takes on every one of Shakespeare's plays in a single riotous evening. The actors tear through the tragedies, comedies, and histories with slapstick, improvisation, and sharp parody, delivering sword fights, romance, deaths, and mistaken identities, frequently all at the same time and rarely the way anyone expects. Seasoned Shakespeare fans and complete newcomers alike will find big laughs in a show that honors both the lasting genius and the sheer absurdity of the Bard. It is a quick, witty, and very physical experience for people who love Shakespeare and people who don't.

An ensemble of performers of all backgrounds, ages, and identities sings numbers and shares stories from NRACT's past productions, with songs drawn from Nine to Five, The 25th Annual Putnam County Spelling Bee, Spring Awakening, [title of show], Pippin, Next to Normal, The Wild Party, Matilda, Hairspray, and Rent. show.title: Knock Knock
show.author: Olivia Aston Bosworth & Samantha Provenzano
show.description: Raleigh Little Theatre opens the holiday season for its very youngest audiences with Knock Knock, a theatre-for-the-very-young adventure through an apartment building. Children meet the neighbors who live behind different doors and on different floors, where delivery boxes turn into imaginary forts, snowflake crafts cause some frustration, a festive party gets going, and everyone tries to stay warm against the winter cold. There are giggles and surprises behind every door, plus lots of chances for young audience members to join in. The performers use few typical conversations, relying instead on frequently repeated key words, physical action, and props to tell the story. Created by Olivia Aston Bosworth and Samantha Provenzano, the piece was commissioned, developed, and first produced by Atlanta's Alliance Theatre in its Kathy and Ken Bernhardt Theatre for the Very Young series. Recommended for ages 0 to 5.

show.title: Inside Out and Backwards
show.author: Kathryn Chase Bryer & Natasha Holmes
show.description: Inside Out and Backwards is a cheerful, almost entirely physical show for very young audiences about a brother and sister getting ready for bed and getting gloriously sidetracked along the way. Audience members are asked to help Brother and Sister through their bedtime routine, even though Sister really does not want to go to bed and keeps causing chaos for her sibling. A simple problem with folding turns into a string of make-believe games that carry everyone to mountains, ski slopes, sea voyages, a desert island, and plenty of places in between. The show reminds families that there is room for play in the middle of everyday chores, sparking imagination and showing that even ordinary tasks can be fun. Dialogue is kept to short, simple exchanges with familiar key words and lots of physical action. Recommended for ages 0 to 5. Produced by special arrangement with Plays for New Audiences.

show.title: Baby Shark

Eccentric sibling explorers Fifi and Felix La Mer set out aboard Sylvie the Submarine on a mission to find the elusive Baby Shark, and audience members come aboard as official crew. Along the way the crew meets obstacle after obstacle, discovers new ocean creatures, sings new songs and old favorites, helps keep Sylvie in tip-top shape, and maybe even turns up some lost treasure. Audiences young and old will be singing along as they explore the ocean with the La Mer siblings. Recommended for ages 0 to 5. Produced by special arrangement with Plays for New Audiences.

show.description: Theatre In The Park presents Ira David Wood III's A Christmas Carol, a musical comedy version of the Dickens classic that has been staged every year since 1974. Called one of the most successful shows in North Carolina theatre history and named one of the Top 20 Events in the Southeast, it has been seen by more than a million people, regularly sells out, and has toured to acclaim in England and France. Its honors include the Metro Ovation Award, the Triangle Arts & Entertainment Reader's Choice Award, and proclamations from the Mayor of Raleigh, the Governor of North Carolina, and the cities of Compiegne, France, and Kingston upon Hull, England; it was also the very first theatrical production at DPAC. For 2026 the show plays only at the Durham Performing Arts Center, featuring David Henderson as Jacob Marley and Ira David Wood III as the Lamplighter. Continue a family tradition or start a new one with one of North Carolina's grandest holiday celebrations.

show.description: The North Carolina premiere of a stage adaptation of Louisa May Alcott's beloved American novel, directed by Mollye Maxner. Four actors turn a humble barn into a whimsical world where time bends and the March sisters' story comes to life. Jo's search for her own artistic identity sparks a magical look at sisterhood, as the girls transform everyday objects into the fantastical scenes of their childhood imaginations: witches, heroes, and their beloved imaginary newspaper. It is through the heartbreaking loss of Beth that Jo finally finds her voice and steps boldly into adulthood, realizing that even as families change, the love they share always stays close at heart. Sponsored by Randolph Community College and the City of Asheboro.

show.title: It's A Wonderful Life: A Live Radio Play
show.author: Joe Landry
show.description: A co-production with 88.5 WFDD, directed by Jeremy Skidmore, in which the classic story is told on the set of a 1940s radio station. Five actors (Robert Beseda, Mya Brown, Kira Geiger, Patrick Osteen, and Allen Tedder) play 42 characters, bringing all the favorite residents of Bedford Falls to life through masterful live performance, complete with the sound effects of the golden age of radio. Audiences will laugh and cry as Clarence the Angel tries to convince George Bailey that his life has truly been well lived. Close your eyes and return to the golden age of radio, or keep them open and watch the performers at work. Sponsored by Roane Law and Allegacy Financial, with additional support from Four Saints Brewing Company.
