show.title: 'Twas the Night Before Christmas
show.description: 'Twas the Night Before Christmas is a lighthearted, warm-hearted holiday offering that captures the feeling of the season through comedy, a sense of wonder, and lots of festive good cheer. The story revolves around the magic of Christmas Eve and the surprises that the night has in store, making this family-friendly show an ideal way to begin the holiday season.

show.title: The 1,683rd Annual Peppermint Party
show.author: Damon Horak
show.description: It's Christmas Eve: children everywhere are tucking into bed and dreaming their way toward Christmas morning, but at the North Pole it's the one day each year when the elves have no work, so it's time for their annual party. The eggnog is flowing, the karaoke keeps getting louder, Santa is trying to get some sleep, and the usual elf banter fills the workshop. There's just one problem: Mischievous Martha. Billed as a hilarious holiday musical extravaganza, the show features the North Pole elves along with performers sharing Christmas-themed songs and dance numbers. Directed by Eileen Connon.

show.title: POTUS
show.description: When a PR nightmare throws the White House into chaos, seven brilliant, determined women race against the clock to save the presidency. Wildly funny, fast-paced, and completely outrageous, POTUS is a sharp political farce packed with scandal, secrets, and nonstop laughs.

show.title: Matilda Jr.
show.description: Packed with high-energy songs, big laughs, and unforgettable characters, Matilda Jr. follows an extraordinary girl who discovers that even the smallest person can change the world. Based on the world-famous book by Roald Dahl.

show.title: The Full Monty
show.description: Six unemployed men with nothing left to lose decide to bare it all in a laugh-out-loud musical comedy about friendship, confidence, and finding the courage to take a chance.

show.title: Songs We'll Never Sing
show.author: Bradley Moore
show.description: An original script by New Bern Civic Theatre Executive Director Bradley Moore, following his AMERICA 250: THE ERAS TOUR. When an electrical failure during a dress rehearsal of The Book of Mormon leads to an impromptu challenge, a show is born: a fast, funny musical revue that turns conventional casting upside down by letting performers tackle iconic songs they would ordinarily never get to sing. The lineup draws on favorites from The Book of Mormon, Hamilton, Dear Evan Hansen, Les Misérables, Miss Saigon, Chicago, The Little Mermaid, Sweeney Todd, Side Show and more, in a comic celebration of musical theatre with no limits.

show.title: Skydoomer
show.description:
Over the past year, 13 local teenagers have been writing an original musical with Bradley Moore, Abbey Lewis, Chris Tilley, & River Durham. This is their story to tell.
Picture it: present-day Litchfield High School. Meet Jack, a seemingly typical high school senior. He hangs out with his friends, plays in a band, has a crush he can't quite figure out, and constantly clashes with his overbearing twin sister. Beneath it all, he's still struggling to cope with the sudden loss of his father. But in this genre-defying musical, nothing is ever quite what it seems. Packed with laughs, twists, mystery, and heart, this unforgettable journey will keep you guessing until the very last moment; you may even find yourself reaching for a tissue. One thing is certain, you've never seen a show quite like this.

show.title: Fat Ham
show.description: In this delectably comic, Pulitzer-Prize winning reinvention of Shakespeare's Hamlet, an uproarious family barbecue instigates a compelling examination of love and loss, pain and joy.

show.title: Mean Girls
show.description: Welcome to North Shore High, where popularity is everything and one new girl turns the social hierarchy upside down. Packed with hilarious comedy, unforgettable songs, and plenty of pink, Mean Girls is a fetch musical about friendship, identity, and staying true to yourself. Based on the hit movie!

show.title: Anything Goes
show.description: See this fresh take on an American classic! From the brilliant mind of Cole Porter, set sail for a laugh-out-loud adventure filled with mistaken identities, unlikely romance, and show-stopping songs. Anything Goes is a timeless musical comedy where anything can, and does, happen!

show.title: Just in the Nick of Time!
show.author: Linda Daugherty
show.description: Santa has disappeared and the North Pole is draining of color. With Christmas only days away, Detective Red Mistletoe takes the case, following the clues to track Santa down and restore the holiday spirit just in time. Ferry Tales Youth Theater presents this festive Detective Red Mistletoe mystery, packed with colorful characters, laughter and Christmas cheer: a holiday adventure for the whole family.

show.title: Wild West Murder Mystery
show.description: The Ansonia Theatre presents a Wild West-themed murder mystery dinner show, a fundraiser hosted by the Anson County Arts Council. The main dinner show begins at 7:00 PM at First United Methodist Church in Wadesboro, with a catered dinner by Sips & Spreads served during the performance. Guests can start the evening with a pre-show mingle at Native State Beer Garden at 6:00 PM (drinks and Native State purchases are sold separately). Seating is at tables of eight and tickets are limited, with a maximum of four tickets per purchase.

show.title: Always... Patsy Cline
show.author: Ted Swindley
show.description: Always... Patsy Cline tells the true story of the friendship between country music legend Patsy Cline and Louise Seger, a Houston housewife and devoted fan. This musical play mixes down-home country humor, genuine emotion and some audience participation, and features 27 of Patsy's unforgettable hits, among them "Crazy," "I Fall to Pieces," "Sweet Dreams" and "Walkin' After Midnight." The title comes from the letters Patsy wrote to Louise, which she always signed "Love ALWAYS... Patsy Cline."

linkedVenueId.name: Historic Main Stage at Thalian Hall

show.title: Brian Whitted's Very Merry Christmas
show.description: Opera House Theatre Company presents Brian Whitted's VERY MERRY CHRISTMAS, back at Thalian Hall for the holidays and moving to the Historic Main Stage for the first time. Now in its sixth year in the Wilmington area, the show features Fayetteville native Brian Whitted alongside some of Wilmington's best musicians and performers. Whitted is an accomplished pianist, conductor and music director whose career has included Broadway, international tours and work with stars such as Bette Midler, Roberta Flack, Phylicia Rashad and BeBe Winans.

show.title: Goodnight Sweet Prince: A Solo Performance of William Shakespeare's Hamlet
show.author: William Shakespeare (solo adaptation performed by John Michael Cox)
show.description: Returning by popular demand, this solo retelling of Hamlet is narrated by Horatio, the prince's closest friend, as he tries to recount Hamlet's final days. Still mourning his father and troubled by his mother's quick remarriage, Prince Hamlet is confronted by a ghostly revelation that leaves him torn between duty and damnation, with the fate of Denmark resting on whether he acts or lets the darkness win. Staged on Halloween night as a ghost story, the piece has a single actor take on fifteen characters. Performer John Michael Cox is the founding artistic director of Vagabond Shakespeare, earned an MFA in Classical Acting from the Shakespeare Theatre Company Academy at The George Washington University, and has worked on twenty of Shakespeare's plays; his Upstate credits include productions with The Warehouse Theatre, Greenville Theatre, Centre Stage, Vagabond Shakespeare, The Upstate Shakespeare Festival, Mill Town Players, SC Children's Theatre and Greenville Shakespeare Company.

show.title: The Little Mermaid
show.author: Doug Wright (book)
show.composer: Alan Menken (music); Howard Ashman & Glenn Slater (lyrics)

show.title: Young Frankenstein
show.author: Mel Brooks & Thomas Meehan (book)
show.description: Mel Brooks' stage musical, adapted from his hit film, follows Frederick Frankenstein, the grandson of the notorious mad scientist, who travels to Transylvania to settle his family's estate and is gradually pulled into reviving his grandfather's experiments with the help of the hunchbacked Igor, lab assistant Inga and the formidable Frau Blucher, leading to a creature, a lot of chaos and plenty of song and dance. May River Theatre's production, directed by Liz McInnes, opens Halloween weekend; audience members who come in costume during opening weekend (October 30 to November 1) can enter to win 2027 season tickets. Seating is priced by section, with center seats at $35 and stage-left and stage-right seats at $30. The show runs about 120 minutes, and the theatre is kept at 68 degrees.
show.contentWarnings: This show uses haze/fog effects and strobe lights.

show.title: Little Women, the Musical
show.author: Allan Knee (book)
show.description: Town Theatre is staging Little Women, the Musical as a new performance opportunity for high school students in grades 9 through 12, who will also fill production team roles alongside the cast. Based on Louisa May Alcott's novel, the musical follows the passionate and adventurous Jo March as she pursues her dream of writing, alongside her sisters Meg, Beth and Amy, their steadfast mother Marmee, the charming boy next door Laurie, the formidable Aunt March and Professor Bhaer, the German professor who eventually wins Jo's heart. The production is directed by Jane Cato with music direction by Katie Rooney and choreography by Joy Alexander.

show.title: Come From Away
show.description: Come From Away tells the remarkable true story of what happened when 38 planes were diverted to the small town of Gander, Newfoundland, in the days following September 11, 2001. As thousands of stranded travelers suddenly doubled the town’s population, local residents opened their homes, schools, and hearts to complete strangers. Told with humor, heart, and a driving folk-rock score, the musical is a powerful story about ordinary people, unexpected connections, and the extraordinary kindness that can emerge in uncertain times.

show.title: Little Women the Musical
show.author: Allan Knee
show.description: Based on the life of Louisa May Alcott, this musical follows the adventures of the four March sisters, Jo, Meg, Beth, and Amy, as they grow up in Civil War America. Jo is trying to sell her stories, but publishers aren't interested. Her friend Professor Bhaer tells her she needs to write more from her own life. Reluctantly taking his advice, Jo weaves together the story of herself and her sisters and what it was like to grow up together.

show.title: Jesus Christ Superstar
show.author: Tim Rice
show.description: A co-production of Greenville Theatre and Mauldin Theatre Company. With music by Andrew Lloyd Webber and lyrics by Tim Rice, this legendary rock opera shattered theatrical expectations and changed the landscape of musical theatre. Told entirely through song, it explores the personal relationships and struggles of the final days of Jesus of Nazareth, all viewed through the complex, critical eyes of Judas Iscariot.

show.title: Legally Blonde JR.
show.author: Heather Hach
show.description: Elle Woods takes on stereotypes, snobbery, and scandal in pursuit of her dreams. When her boyfriend Warner dumps her and heads to Harvard, claiming she isn't serious enough, Elle takes matters into her own hands, crafting a showy song-and-dance personal essay and charming her way into law school. Along the way she befriends her classmate Emmett and the spunky hairdresser Paulette, discovering that books and looks aren't mutually exclusive. As Elle begins outsmarting her peers, she realizes the law may be her natural calling after all. Tickets go on sale February 12, 2027.

show.title: Jekyll & Hyde
show.author: Leslie Bricusse
show.description: An evocative tale of two men, one a passionate and romantic doctor and the other a terrifying madman, and two women, one beautiful and trusting and the other beautiful and trusting only herself. Both women are in love with the same man, and both are unaware of his dark secret. Dr. Henry Jekyll is a devoted man of science determined to find a chemical breakthrough that could solve some of mankind's most challenging medical dilemmas. Rebuffed by the powers that be, he makes himself the subject of his own experimental treatments and accidentally unleashes his inner demons along with the man the world would come to know as Mr. Hyde. Tickets go on sale March 30, 2027.

show.title: The Lightning Thief: The Percy Jackson Musical
show.author: Joe Tracz (book), adapted from the novel by Rick Riordan
show.description: Percy Jackson has just learned that he is a half-blood son of a Greek god, and with that discovery come powers he cannot yet control, a destiny he never asked for, and a whole mythology's worth of monsters chasing him. When Zeus's master lightning bolt goes missing and Percy is blamed for the theft, he must track down the bolt and return it to clear his name and keep the gods from going to war. Succeeding means more than catching the real thief: Percy has to journey into the Underworld and back, unravel a riddle from the Oracle that warns a friend will betray him, and make peace with the father who walked out on him. Built on Rick Riordan's best-selling novel and powered by an original rock score, this action-filled mythological adventure was praised by Time Out New York as "worthy of the gods." CFRT's version is a roughly 50-minute production made for young audiences, directed by Marc de la Concha with choreography by Becca Vourvoulas and music direction by James Clark, Jr., presented for two performances on a single Saturday. CFRT Flex Pass subscribers can redeem their passes for this show.

show.title: The Best Christmas Pageant Ever
show.author: Barbara Robinson
show.description: Everyone agrees the Herdman kids are the worst children who ever lived: they lie, they steal, they smoke cigars, and they leave chaos behind them wherever they go. So when the Herdmans unexpectedly turn up at church and take over the annual Christmas pageant, the congregation prepares for catastrophe, horrified at the thought of Imogene as Mary and Leroy as Joseph. What follows is a riotous stretch of skipped rehearsals, mangled costumes and pure pandemonium, yet the show also turns out to have a great deal of heart. Hearing the Christmas story for the very first time, the Herdmans bring blunt honesty, curiosity and even some unexpected grace to a tale the church members assumed they knew completely, and the pageant that goes nothing like planned may become the best one ever. Directed by Jennifer Sell, this is CFRT's final production in its ballroom theatre at 1707 Owen Drive and is billed as a holiday outing for every generation. Rotating casts (Ginger, Cinnamon, Nutmeg and Clove) appear at different performances; select weeknight performances are Military Appreciation nights with 25% off tickets, and group rates and school performances are available through business@cfrt.org.

show.title: Frozen: The Musical
show.author: Jennifer Lee (book), based on the Disney film written by Jennifer Lee and directed by Chris Buck and Jennifer Lee
show.description: When Queen Elsa's concealed powers break loose, the kingdom of Arendelle is locked in a winter that will not end. Her fearless sister Anna sets out to rescue Elsa and bring summer back, joined on the journey by the rugged ice harvester Kristoff, his faithful reindeer Sven, and the beloved snowman Olaf. Featuring spectacular stagecraft and every favorite song from the Disney hit, the musical celebrates family, bravery and finding the magic inside yourself. CFRT's production, staged in the company's new building at 1209 Hay Street, is directed by Robert W. Schneider with choreography by Caitlin Belcik, music direction by Sarah Wussow and associate music direction by James Clark, Jr. The run opens with two preview performances on January 21 and 22 and an opening night on January 23; youth roles are shared by two alternating casts ("Snow" and "Ice") while the principal cast stays the same. Special events include a Military Appreciation Night (January 27) and a Teacher Appreciation Night (January 29), each with 25% off, a sensory-friendly performance on February 7 sponsored by ShineLight Inc., and a $35 VIP add-on on January 31 and February 6, 7, 13 and 14 offering a 45-minute post-show party for young guests with music, crafts, treats and a cast meet-and-greet. Prices vary by performance, from $20 for previews up to $39 for weekend shows.

show.title: One Man, Two Guvnors
show.author: Richard Bean, based on The Servant of Two Masters by Carlo Goldoni
show.description: Francis Henshall is always hungry and always in over his head, and when he ends up secretly employed by two different bosses at once, concealing each from the other becomes a full-time occupation. Mix-ups pile on top of mix-ups, love affairs come apart and the situation spirals wildly out of control as Francis races to stay a step ahead of discovery. Full of outrageous physical comedy, rapid-fire wit and audience participation, this farce keeps delivering surprises from beginning to end. CFRT's production, staged at its new 1209 Hay Street facility and directed by Chris O'Connor, stars the company's Education Director Marc de la Concha. The run begins with previews on March 18 and 19 and opens March 20; there are no performances on Easter Sunday (March 28). Special events include a Military Appreciation Night on March 24 and a Teacher Appreciation Night on March 26, each with 25% off. Ticket prices range from $16 for previews to $30, depending on the performance.
show.contentWarnings: Contains mild language, adult humor, and innuendo; recommended for ages 13 and up.

show.title: Big Fish
show.author: John August (book), based on the novel by Daniel Wallace and the Columbia Pictures film written by John August
show.description: Edward Bloom is a charming dreamer whose life, as he tells it, has been packed with witches, giants, mermaids and impossible exploits. The more his stories grow, the more determined his son Will becomes to separate fact from legend, and in the process Will discovers a story larger than any he imagined: that of a father, a family, and a life lived completely. Brimming with humor, warmth and vivid imagination, this musical celebrates love, legacy and the stories that make us who we are. CFRT's production plays at its new 1209 Hay Street facility, directed by Mary Catherine Burke and choreographed by Tyce Diorio. The run opens with previews on April 29 and 30 and an opening night on May 1, with a Military Appreciation Night on May 5 and a Teacher Appreciation Night on May 7 (25% off each). Tickets range from $20 for previews to $39, depending on the performance.
show.contentWarnings: Themes of family, loss, and mortality, presented through whimsical storytelling.

show.title: The Best of Broadway
show.author: Created and directed by Michael Pizzi
show.composer: Various (Gershwins, Jerome Kern, Bock and Harnick, Leonard Bernstein, Stephen Sondheim, Irving Berlin and others)
show.description: New York performers celebrate the most iconic Broadway composers and their contributions to the musical stage in this concert revue created and directed by Michael Pizzi. The program draws on favorites from the Gershwins, Jerome Kern, Bock and Harnick, Leonard Bernstein, Stephen Sondheim, Irving Berlin, William Finn, Ahrens and Flaherty, Kander and Ebb and many more, performed by Brett Boles, Jennifer Mintzer and Michael Pizzi. Two performances are offered on Saturday, November 14, at Lee Auditorium at Pinecrest High School in Southern Pines, and ten percent of all net ticket sales go to local food banks.

show.title: A Very Playhouse Christmas
show.description: This holiday fundraiser from the Playhouse of Wilson celebrates the season with festive music, holiday cheer and performances by members of the Playhouse family. Proceeds help support the company's productions throughout the year, and the event is meant to bring the community together for an evening of holiday magic. Performances are December 4 and 5, 2026, with auditions held October 25 and 26.

show.title: Alice by Heart
show.author: Steven Sater & Jessie Nelson (book); Steven Sater (lyrics)
show.description: Set in the London Underground during the Blitz, Alice by Heart retells Alice's Adventures in Wonderland through the eyes of a young girl clinging to hope in one of history's darkest moments. With a moving score by Duncan Sheik and heartfelt storytelling, the musical explores love, grief, imagination and resilience. Performances are February 19-21, 2027, with auditions January 4-6, 2027; tickets are listed as coming soon.

show.title: The Diary of Anne Frank
show.author: Frances Goodrich & Albert Hackett
show.description: Among the most powerful stories ever staged, The Diary of Anne Frank tells the true account of a young girl whose hope and humanity held fast during the Holocaust. The drama is a moving reminder of the resilience of the human spirit and of why compassion, courage and remembrance matter. Performances are April 16-18, 2027; youth auditions are February 22 and 23 and adult auditions March 1 and 2, 2027, and tickets are listed as coming soon.

show.title: The Importance of Being Earnest
show.author: Oscar Wilde
show.description: Oscar Wilde's beloved comedy follows two friends who invent elaborate alter egos to slip free of society's expectations, only to land in a tangle of hilarious misunderstandings, unexpected romance and razor-sharp wit. Packed with unforgettable one-liners and timeless humor, it remains one of the funniest plays ever written. Performances are June 11-13, 2027, with auditions April 26 and 27, 2027; tickets are listed as coming soon.

show.title: A Raisin in the Sun
show.author: Lorraine Hansberry
show.description: Lorraine Hansberry's celebrated play, set on Chicago's South Side, follows the clashing dreams of three generations of the Younger family: son Walter Lee, his wife Ruth, his sister Beneatha, his son Travis and the family matriarch, Lena. When the insurance money from her late husband finally arrives, Mama Lena hopes to move the family into a new home in a better Chicago neighborhood. Walter Lee, who works as a chauffeur, wants instead to buy a liquor store and become his own boss, while Beneatha dreams of attending medical school. Hansberry's portrait of a family fighting to hold on to its dignity in a harsh and changing world remains a searing, timeless document of hope and inspiration. Directed by Jacqueline Shaw and produced by the Imperial Centre of Rocky Mount together with Master's Training Wheel.
show.contentWarnings: Contains use of a homophobic slur.

show.title: Sense and Sensibility
show.author: Jane Austen (novel); stage adaptation not specified
show.description: Suddenly left without their fortune, the Dashwood sisters Elinor and Marianne must find their way through a world where love, money and social expectation are tightly bound together. Thoughtful, reserved Elinor tries to conceal her feelings for the kind but uncertain Edward Ferrars, while Marianne follows her heart and falls hard for the charming John Willoughby. Through love, heartbreak, secrets and unexpected friendships, each sister learns important lessons about herself and about what really matters. Set amid the elegance and wit of Regency England, the story is a heartfelt look at family, romance and the balance between following your heart and using your head.

show.title: How to Succeed in Business Without Really Trying: School Edition
show.author: Abe Burrows, Jack Weinstock & Willie Gilbert (book)
show.description: A youth-stage production of the school edition of this musical comedy about ambition, friendship, romance and finding your way up the corporate ladder, delivered with plenty of music, dancing and laughs. Two evening performances on November 23 and 24, 2026.

show.title: Catch Me If You Can
show.author: Terrence McNally (book)
show.composer: Marc Shaiman (music); Scott Wittman & Marc Shaiman (lyrics)
show.description: A thrilling musical comedy about a young con artist who lives a life of adventure while managing to stay one step ahead of the law. Auditions are December 14 and 15, 2026.

show.title: Trash
show.author: Caverly and Morrill
show.description: Tim and Jake are Deaf roommates who could not be more different, and a simple argument over whose turn it is to take out the trash quickly grows into something much larger as they sort through their personal "garbage," their complicated friendship and their very different views of what it means to be Deaf in a hearing world. Funny, honest and thought-provoking, the play examines friendship, identity, communication and the assumptions people make about one another. Written by Caverly and Morrill from Deaf perspectives, it is performed mainly in American Sign Language, with spoken translation, projections and other theatrical devices making it accessible to Deaf and hearing audiences alike.

show.title: A Gentleman's Guide to Love and Murder
show.author: Robert L. Freedman (book & lyrics)
show.description: Monty Navarro is charming and penniless until he learns he is ninth in line to inherit a wealthy family's title. Determined to climb the line of succession, he concocts ever more outrageous ways to remove the relatives standing between him and the earldom, all while juggling romance, ambition and the constant risk of being caught. This clever musical comedy is full of dark humor, surprising twists and plenty of murder. Auditions are March 15 and 16, 2027.

show.title: Broadway After Dark: A Halloween Musical Cabaret
show.description: A one-night Halloween musical cabaret from Summerfield Stage Company, performed Wednesday, October 28, 2026 at 7:00 PM at Morehead United Methodist Church in Greensboro.

tickets.notes: Free. Suggested donation of $10.

linkedVenueId.name: Jamie Lawson Auditorium at the Ihrie Theatre at Theatre Alliance

show.title: Dear Evan Hansen
show.author: Steven Levenson (book)
show.description: Evan Hansen is seventeen and has felt invisible his whole life. When a tragedy rocks his community and pushes him into the middle of a fast-growing controversy, Evan suddenly gets the chance of a lifetime: to become somebody else. But as his web of well-meant lies starts to come apart, he has to face the possibility that the cost of belonging is far higher than he expected. With a Tony-winning book by Steven Levenson and a score by Benj Pasek and Justin Paul, the musical opened at Broadway's Music Box Theatre to rave reviews, won six 2017 Tony Awards including Best Musical along with Drama League, Obie, Drama Desk, Outer Critics Circle and Helen Hayes honors, and has resonated worldwide with its message that "You Will Be Found."

linkedVenueId.name: Jamie Lawson Auditorium at the Ihrie Theatre at Theatre Alliance

show.title: Finding Neverland
show.author: James Graham (book)
show.description: Drawn from the Academy Award-winning film and the play The Man Who Was Peter Pan, this musical traces the bond between playwright J.M. Barrie and the family that inspired Peter Pan, or The Boy Who Wouldn't Grow Up. Struggling to find his next success, Barrie meets the widowed Sylvia Llewelyn Davies and her four sons in Kensington Gardens. As he befriends them, their adventures spark his imagination, especially young Peter, who has stopped playing because of his grief. Helping Peter learn to play again leads Barrie toward a whole new form, theatre for children, but who will pay to see a play about children, who will play them, and how will Peter Pan fly? Time called it a spirited, tuneful and nimbly staged delight.

linkedVenueId.name: Jamie Lawson Auditorium at the Ihrie Theatre at Theatre Alliance

show.title: Mean Girls
show.author: Tina Fey (book)
show.description: Cady Heron grew up on the African savanna, but nothing prepared her for the wild and vicious terrain of her new home in suburban Illinois. To climb the popularity ladder, the newcomer takes on The Plastics, a trio of adored frenemies led by the charming but ruthless Regina George. When Cady and her friends plot a "Revenge Party" to end Regina's reign, she learns the hard way that crossing a queen bee means getting stung. Adapted from Tina Fey's 2004 film, with a book by Fey, music by Jeff Richmond and lyrics by Nell Benjamin, the musical earned twelve Tony nominations.

linkedVenueId.name: Jamie Lawson Auditorium at the Ihrie Theatre at Theatre Alliance

show.title: Come From Away
show.author: Irene Sankoff & David Hein (book, music & lyrics)
show.description: Based on a true story, Come From Away recalls the day the remote town of Gander, Newfoundland, became host to the world. On September 11, 2001, an ordinary day turned into an international sleepover when 38 planes carrying thousands of passengers from across the globe were diverted to Gander's airstrip, and the townspeople, undeterred by cultural differences and language barriers, welcomed the stranded travelers with music and generosity. With a moving score by Irene Sankoff and David Hein, the musical has earned 37 award nominations and 13 wins, including Best New Musical at the 2019 Olivier Awards and Outstanding Musical at the 2017 Drama Desk Awards, and stands as an uplifting reminder of people's ability to come together whatever the circumstances.

linkedVenueId.name: Jamie Lawson Auditorium at the Ihrie Theatre at Theatre Alliance

show.title: Les Misérables
show.author: Alain Boublil & Claude-Michel Schönberg (book)
show.description: Theatre Alliance brings this award-laden musical phenomenon back to its stage for a second time. Seen by more than 150 million people in 57 countries, 452 cities and 22 languages over more than 45 years, Les Misérables is among the longest-running and most celebrated musicals ever written, an epic of passion and redemption amid revolution. In 19th-century France, Jean Valjean is freed after 19 years of unjust imprisonment only to meet suspicion and cruelty everywhere he turns. He breaks parole to start a new life, beginning a lifelong quest for redemption while police inspector Javert, who refuses to believe a man like Valjean can change, hunts him relentlessly. Winner of eight Tony Awards including Best Musical, Best Original Score and Best Book, it is a story of broken dreams, unrequited love, passion and sacrifice, and a timeless testament to the endurance of the human spirit.

show.title: A Christmas Carol
show.description: Alamance Children's Theatre stages a fresh take on Charles Dickens's holiday classic, framed through the eyes of a young boy and his grandfather. Thomas loves spending time at his grandfather's prominent London business, yet he cannot understand why the old man would hand his hard-earned money over to the poor. That question gives Grandfather the perfect opening to tell the story of Ebenezer Scrooge as he remembers it, and the traditional tale comes to life on stage as a play within a play: visits from three ghosts take Scrooge through his past, present and future and persuade him to turn his life around. All of the familiar Dickens characters appear, including Jacob Marley, Scrooge's sister Fan and his long-lost Belle, and the story closes with a heartwarming surprise when the audience learns who Thomas's grandfather really is. Performed by a cast of young people ages 8 to 18 and directed by Andy Kielty, the production plays the Sara McMillan Brown Theater at Studio 1 in Burlington.

show.title: Be Kind, Rewind: Home for the Holidays
show.description: A high-energy holiday musical built on the hits of the 1980s. Just days before Christmas, the owner of a struggling video rental store stumbles onto a forgotten box of '80s mixtapes, and every song she plays magically carries her back to the moments that once made the holidays feel like home. As past and present collide in a whirl of neon lights, big hair and iconic songs, she has to rediscover the people, and the holiday spirit, she has been missing. Billed as a heartfelt journey in which each song brings her one step closer to Christmas again, the show is part of the Barn Dinner Theatre's Christmas Stage season, and every ticket includes the Barn's all-you-can-eat Southern-style buffet with water along with the performance.

show.title: Something Rotten!
show.author: Karey Kirkpatrick & John O'Farrell (book); Wayne Kirkpatrick & Karey Kirkpatrick (music & lyrics)
show.description: Step into the Renaissance for Something Rotten!, an outrageous musical farce from Grammy-winning songwriter Wayne Kirkpatrick and screenwriters Karey Kirkpatrick and John O'Farrell. Embraced by audiences and critics, it collected several Best Musical nominations and was called "the funniest musical comedy in at least 400 years" by Time Out New York. In the 1590s, brothers Nick and Nigel Bottom are desperate for a hit play but stuck in the shadow of the era's rock star, "The Bard." When a local soothsayer predicts that the theatre of the future will combine singing, dancing and acting all at once, the brothers set out to write the world's first musical, only to discover amid the chaos of opening night that getting to the top means being true to thine own self. Packed with big song-and-dance numbers and a zany cast of over-the-top characters who each get a moment in the spotlight, the show famously drew a standing ovation on Broadway early in the first act. High Point Community Theatre closes its 51st season with this history-bending comedy at the High Point Theatre.

show.title: Matilda The Musical
show.author: Dennis Kelly (book)
show.description: Kernersville Little Theatre's 2026-27 season continues with Matilda The Musical, playing April 9-18, 2027 at the James Fitzpatrick Auditorium in Kernersville. Advance tickets are sold online through Ludus, and tickets are also available at the door at slightly higher prices.

show.title: South Pacific
show.author: Oscar Hammerstein II & Joshua Logan (book); Oscar Hammerstein II (lyrics)
show.description: Kernersville Little Theatre closes its 2026-27 season with Rodgers & Hammerstein's South Pacific, playing June 11-20, 2027 at the James Fitzpatrick Auditorium in Kernersville. Advance tickets are sold online through Ludus, and tickets are also available at the door at slightly higher prices.

show.title: Intimate Apparel
show.author: Lynn Nottage
show.description: Lynn Nottage's Intimate Apparel is set in New York at the turn of the twentieth century and centers on Esther, a talented seamstress whose handiwork brings happiness to others while her own heart goes painfully unfulfilled. As her hopes for love run up against hard realities, Esther must face what she truly wants and what she may already have lost. Told with exquisite restraint and deep feeling, the play is a powerful look at love in all of its complicated forms. Directed by Darleny DelRosario for the Little Theatre of Winston-Salem's 92nd season at the Hanesbrands Theatre; single tickets go on sale January 15, 2027.

show.title: Lyrics & Lore
show.description: Lexington Live invites audiences into an evening of music, myth and mystery with Lyrics & Lore, an elegant and haunting celebration of the magical, mystical spirit of All Hallows' Eve. The program pairs seasonally inspired music with tales drawn from Lexington-area ghost stories and local legend, gathering everyone in an intimate setting where song and storytelling meet the supernatural. The night is more than ghosts and legends, though: it kicks off Lexington Live's fundraising campaign for its 2026-2027 season of productions, as the company looks to build something new after a season of change and fresh starts and asks the community to raise a glass, share a story and help launch a new era. The show runs about 90 minutes with no intermission; the bar is open from 6 to 7 PM for beer and wine purchases, and non-alcoholic drinks and light snacks are available before and after the performance.

show.title: Langston Hughes' Black Nativity
show.author: Langston Hughes
show.description: Langston Hughes' Black Nativity, the poet's gospel-infused retelling of the Christmas story, is the centerpiece of the Barn Dinner Theatre's Christmas Stage 2026, running November 14-28 and again December 12-22 (Be Kind, Rewind fills the December 1-6 slot in between). As with every Barn production, the ticket price covers the performance together with the all-you-can-eat Southern-style buffet with water; Christmas-season seats are priced the same for every performance time.

show.title: Jeff Wayne's Musical Version of The War of the Worlds (Spilled Ink Staged Reading)
show.author: Rob Taylor (stage adaptation), based on the novel by H.G. Wells
show.description: Camel City Playhouse's Spilled Ink staged-reading series takes on H.G. Wells's landmark science-fiction tale of a Martian invasion in a form audiences have never seen. In 1978 composer Jeff Wayne reshaped the story into a legendary progressive-rock concept album, and its mix of symphonic orchestration, synthesizer-driven rock and cinematic sound design broke open the limits of musical storytelling and became a worldwide cultural phenomenon. This one-night multimedia staged reading brings that legacy to the stage by combining live dramatic performance, immersive projected visuals and Wayne's pounding, iconic score, reviving the terror of the Martian tripods and humanity's desperate struggle to survive. It is aimed at lifelong fans of the album and first-timers alike as a singular blend of theatre, image and sound. Directed by Gregg Vogelsmeier, with Brian Joyce as the Journalist, Logan Cox as the Artilleryman, Stephen Truhon as Parson Nathaniel, Nicole Gonzales as Beth, and Frankie Locklear and Gracie Rodgers as the Voices of Humanity.

show.title: Annie
show.author: Thomas Meehan (book); Martin Charnin (lyrics)
show.description: Inspired by Harold Gray's much-loved comic strip, Annie grew into a worldwide phenomenon and earned seven Tony Awards, Best Musical among them, with a book and score by Tony winners Thomas Meehan, Charles Strouse and Martin Charnin that includes some of the best-known songs in musical theatre, "Tomorrow" chief among them. In 1930s New York City, plucky and endlessly upbeat little orphan Annie wins over everyone she meets despite starting life with next to nothing. She is determined to find the parents who left her years ago on the doorstep of a city orphanage run by the cruel, embittered Miss Hannigan. With help from the other girls in the orphanage, Annie escapes into the wonders of New York, and over a string of fun-filled adventures she foils Miss Hannigan's wicked plots and even befriends President Franklin Delano Roosevelt. In the end she finds a new home and family with billionaire Oliver Warbucks, his personal secretary Grace Farrell, and a lovable mutt named Sandy.

show.title: The SpongeBob Musical: Youth Edition
show.description: High Point Community Theatre presents the youth edition of The SpongeBob Musical, based on the Nickelodeon animated series, at the Centennial Station Arts Center as part of its 51st season. Tickets for shows at Centennial Station can be bought at the door, where cash, checks, credit cards, PayPal, Venmo and Apple Pay are accepted; doors open 30 minutes before each performance.
